text: On 26 November 2023, the state units of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), Assam Chah Mazdoor Sangha (ACMS), and Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) among others staged a protest at the Mancotta field in Dibrugarh city (Assam) against the Centre's policies, which include new labor and farm laws, as well as the privatization of public sector units.

On 26 November 2023, members of the AITUC Manipur State Committee, Bishnupur district along with members of the All Manipur Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) Workers, anganwadi workers, mid-day-meal workers, street vendors, farmers, fisherman, Panchayat workers and many displaced persons staged a public protest program on the 'Territorial Integrity of Manipur, Establishment of Highway Protection Force on two National Highways of Manipur' at the hanga Chingmang Community Hall in Bishnupur town (Manipur) amidst ongoing conflict between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. The program launched a series of protests against the government for failing to solve the crisis in Manipur and demanded concrete steps to restore peace in the state.

On 26 November 2023, laity members of the Ernakulam Angamaly archdiocese (Catholic) staged a protest outside the St Mary's Cathedral Basilica in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) to mark one year of the holy mass getting disrupted at the church. Protesters said that the cathedral has been closed for a year due to the negative attitude of the apostolic administrator and demanded his resignation and the reinstatement of a former vicar who had advocated for mass to be conducted facing the laity.

On 26 November 2023, hundreds of CITU members joined by a CPI(M) leader held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) against the central government over denial of remunerative prices to apple farmers, to demand hundred percent import duty on imported apples and against the Indus water treaty over claimed losses incurred by J&K due to limits on power generation and demanded that the center compensate for the losses among other demands.

On 26 November 2023, scores of local people staged a protest at Chitta Harayapur village in Kaushambi district (Uttar Pradesh) against the vandalization of a statute of Dr. B R Ambedkar (a Dalit champion) (coded separately).

On 26 November 2023, over 500 members of various organizations including Jai Bhim India Network (a Dalit organization), the Jai Kisan Andolan (a farmer organization), the Adivasi Adhikar Mahasabha and the United Forum for All Adivasi Organisations held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) against the BJP-led central government observed 'Save Constitution Day' over claimed non-adherence to the constitution by the BJP-led government and demanded a caste based census.

On 26 November 2023, a BJP member along with his supporters clashed with another group involving a TMC member at Mechkoka village (Cooch Behar district, WB) over a drunk altercation during the immersion procession of Jagaddhatri Puja (a Hindu ritual). 1 TMC member was killed and 9 others from both sides were left injured in the clash. Police intervened to stop the clash. TMC claimed sharp weapons were used in the incident by the BJP members.

On 26 November 2023, 6 people, led by a village head, assaulted two people (husband and wife) and were suspected to have hurled casteist slurs, at a village in the Barabanki district (Uttar Pradesh) over a land dispute.

On 26 November 2023, hundreds of protesters led by incumbent Giridih MP from AJSU-P party blocked the main gate of the BTPS plant, a power unit of Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC), under Bermo Sub Division (Bokaro, Jharkhand) to highlight the concerns of displaced individuals and address other demands.

On 26 November 2023, supporters from the OBC community, led by a cabinet minister from NCP-AP gathered and held an OBC Elgar yatra (Load declaration to save OBC reservation) at Hingoli (Maharashtra) demanding a stay on the Kunbi (OBC) certificates being given to Marathas over the past two months and scrapping of the Justice (retired) Sandeep Shinde Committee formed to explore ways to provide reservation to the Maratha community.

On 26 November 2023, nursing staff staged a sit-in protest, wearing black badges, at the All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in Bathinda city (Punjab) over various demands including appointment of hospital attendants at the in-patient departments, completion of probation of paramedic staffers, and 8 days off monthly.

On 26 November 2023, members of the DYFI and the IYC clashed with each other in Kunnamangalam town (Kozhikode, Kerala) after a attempts by a few KSU members attempted to wave black flag at the Chief Minister during a Navakerala Sadas (CPI(M) public outreach program). Two IYC members sustained injuries.

On 26 November 2023, four persons including those from the Koli caste (OBC) assaulted a 45-year-old Dalit woman with steel pipes in Bhavnagar town (Gujarat) over her refusal to have her son withdraw a three-year-old case registered against them under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The woman succumbed to her injuries on 27 November. The death of the woman led to a demonstration (coded separately).

On 26 November 2023, JKNPP members led by a former minister held a sizeable protest by burning an effigy at Jammu city (J&K) against the BJP-led central government over claimed corruption and political use of central agencies like the enforcement directorate and central bureau of investigation.

On 26 November 2023, activists of Similipal Bikash Parishad, a local outfit working for the development of the area, and locals from three panchayats blocked roads leading to Simlipal National Prak in Joranda Chhak, Sana Uski, Chala, and Lanjighosara Chhak under Baripada town (Mayurbhanj, Odisha) over five-point charter of demands, including better roads from Kalikaprasad Gates to Gadasimilipal, the establishment of mobile towers inside the Similipal, creation of employment opportunities for unemployed youths of the peripheral areas of the sanctuary, etc.

On 26 November 2023, thousands of people staged a protest march in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) in solidarity with the LGBTQ+ community. Protesters held placards shouted slogans calling for freedom to mark their protest.

On 26 November 2023, 11 people assaulted 2 policemen and tore their uniforms in Gahara Khurd village (Agra, Uttar Pradesh) when the policemen arrived in the area to investigate a case of rioting registered against some people.

On 26 November 2023, local people assaulted a police team, vandalized their car, and snatched a pistol, in Masuri village (Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh) in a road rage incident. 4 police personnel were injured and one accused was detained.

On 26 November 2023, hundreds of farmers from across the state, including the BKU (Lakhowal) General secretary, gathered under the banner of SKM and staged 'day 1' of their 3-day protest along the road at Phase-11 near the Mohali-Chandigarh border in Mohali city (SAS Nagar, Punjab) demanding a legal guarantee of Minimum Support Price (MSP) for farmers, withdrawal of cases registered against farmers for 2020-21 protests, pension, and jobs for family members of farmers who died during the 2020-21 protests. The protest was part of a nationwide protest.

On 26 November 2023, around 600 farmers from across the state, including the BKU (Shaheed Bhagat Singh) and BKU (Rattan Singh Mann) Presidents, and members of CITU, Anganwadi workers, AIJASS, and OPS Bachao Morcha, gathered under the banner of SKM and staged 'day 1' of their 3-day protest at Sector 5 in Panchkula city (Haryana) demanding for a legal guarantee of Minimum Support Price (MSP) for farmers, withdrawal of cases registered against farmers for 2020-21 protests, pension, and jobs for family members of farmers who died during the 2020-21 protests. The protest was part of a nationwide protest.

On 26 November 2023, farmers gathered under the banner of SKM and staged a sit-in protest at the road crossing near National Highway 19 in Atoha village (Palwal, Haryana) demanding a legal guarantee of Minimum Support Price (MSP) for farmers, withdrawal of cases registered against farmers for 2020-21 protests, pension, and jobs for family members of farmers who died during the 2020-21 protests. The protest was part of a '3-day' nationwide protest.

On 26 November 2023, members of the SKM, the KRRS and the Joint Committee of Trade Unions launched a three day protest at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) demanding the withdrawal of the anti-people' policies of the Union government and the 'anti-farmer' policies of the previous BJP-led Karnataka state government.

Around 26 November 2023 (as reported), students locked the main gate of the MPC Autonomous College in Baripada town (Mayurbhanj, Odisha) in protest against the college authority organizing programs under 'Yuva Odisha Nabin Odisha' (a program backed by ruling BJD) involving some particular students.

On 26 November 2023, members of the Joint Teachers' Front, comprising 6 teacher unions, staged a massive protest, raising slogans, outside the Deputy commissioner's office in Sangrur city (Punjab) over various demands including restoration of dearness allowance, implementation of the old pension scheme, and regularization of contractual jobs. The protesters also took out a protest march to Barnala Chowk.

On 26 November 2023, family members of the deceased and local people staged a protest by placing the deceased's body along the Indri State Highway in Muradgarh village (Karnal, Haryana) against the death of a woman who was hit and dragged by a car.
On 26 November 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest outside a nursing home at the Sasni Gate area in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a newborn.

On 26 November 2023, homebuyers gathered under the banners of the Noida Estate Flat Owners Main Association and the New Era Flat Owners Association and staged a protest march at the Ek Murti roundabout in Greater Noida city (Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) demanding the provision of metro connectivity in the Greater Noida West area.

On 26 November 2023, family members of the deceased took his body from the police and staged a protest along the Gorakhpur-Hata road near Gorakhpur city (Uttar Pradesh) against the abduction and murder of a boy. Protesters also accused the police of negligence.

On 26 November 2023, members of the Good Morning Club of Dhubri and regular commuters of Fly Big staged a protest in front of Rupsi airport gate in Sukatikhata (Dhubri, Assam) against stopping its services since 7 November this year and demanded its resumption.

Around 26 November 2023 (as reported), the family members of a deceased woman and villagers staged a protest in front of Raighar police station (Nabarangpur district, Odisha) demanding capital punishment for the accused.
On 26 November 2023, locals assaulted a claimed perpetrator, held a demonstration and pelted stones at the police who attempted to rescue him at Kolkata city (WB) over the murder of a person.

Around 26 November 2023 (as reported), local youth staged a protest in the Otteri locality in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the Chennai Corporation to construct a modern playground in Otteri dump yard.

On 26 November 2023, over 200 villagers staged a protest at the gram sabha in Loliem Polem village in Canacona taluk (coded to Canacona city, South Goa, Goa) against the proposal to construct a Film City in the village. Protesters said that the proposed project posed a food, water and ecology threat to future generations and opposed the plan.

On 26 November 2023, the tribal villagers of D Koral and Dimundi of Kashipur area in Rayagada district started a dharna (sit-in protest) at the Lower PMG in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) demanding suitable compensation for the land acquired by Utkal Alumina in Kashipur area in 1996.

On 26 November 2023, job aspirants staged at protest in the city centre in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) demanding the state government to complete recruitment for firemen and drivers by the end of 2023. The recruitment process started but was allegedly halted for the past 11 months.

On 26 November 2023, farmers, workers and employees staged a protest at Bongaigaon town (Bongaigaon, Assam) against the government's anti-labour, anti-farmer, anti-people and anti-national policies. Hundreds participated in protests in Bongaigaon, Tezpur, Silchar and Dibrugarh towns.

On 26 November 2023, several thousands of farmers under the initiative of the Joint Platform of Farmers, Workers and Employees Joint Federation staged a protest at Meghdoot Bhavan in Guwahati (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) against the government's anti-labour, anti-farmer, anti-people and anti-national policies. The protest was joined by organizations like INTUC, CITU, AITUC, AICCTU, AIUTUC, TUCC, HMS, Asom Rajyik Krishak Sabha, AOKS, Assam Krishi Shramik Union, AIKKMS, All Assam Farmers Association, Krishak Mukti Sangram Samiti (KMSS) and Janaajati Adhikar Manch (Adivasi rights group).

On 26 November 2023, farmers, workers and employees staged a protest at Silchar town (Cachar, Assam) against the government's anti-labour, anti-farmer, anti-people and anti-national policies. Hundreds participated in protests in Bongaigaon, Tezpur, Silchar and Dibrugarh towns.

On 26 November 2023, farmers, workers and employees staged a protest at Tezpur town (Sontipur, Assam) against the government's anti-labour, anti-farmer, anti-people and anti-national policies. Hundreds participated in protests in Bongaigaon, Tezpur, Silchar and Dibrugarh towns.

On 26 November 2023, around 20 members of the Agila Bharatha Hanuman Sena (Hindu group) staged a protest at the Thiruparankundram bus station in Thiruparankundram town (Madurai, Tamil Nadu) against the authorities for not lighting the Karthigai Deepamon (lamp) on the premises of the Uchipillayar temple on the hilltop because a Muslim dargah (shrine) was situated close by. Police detained the protesters.

On 27 November 2023, members of the state units of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), Assam Chah Mazdoor Sangha (ACMS), Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU), including a former INC MLA, held a massive protest at the Mancotta Field in Dibrugarh city (Assam) against the 'anti-people' policies of the government including strengthening of MGNREGS with 200 days of job per year and Rs 600 as daily wage, the halt of privatization of public sector units and that of price rise etc.

On 27 November 2023, members of the BJP staged a protest in Tirunelveli city (Tamil Nadu) against the Corporation for failing to provide basic amenities including motorable roads, efficient drainage systems and the regular supply of drinking water.
On 27 November 2023, BJP supporters led by a minister held a protest amidst a 12-hour shutdown call at Khejuri town (Purba Medinipur district, WB) over the arrest of their party member.

On 27 November 2023, members of the BJP including councillors staged a protest in the Vannarpettai locality of Tirunelveli city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the dismissal of the Tirunelveli corporation council. Protesters accused the mayor and councillors of corruption and said that no developmental activities had been done. Protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 27 November 2023, members of the AIMIM assaulted and injured an auto driver supporting the Majlis Bachao Tehreek (MBT) party in the Saidabad locality (Hyderabad, Telangana) for fixing the MBT party flag on his vehicle to show his support during the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections. The assailants slapped, chased and beat up the victim.

On 27 November 2023, members of the CPI staged a protest in Puducherry city (Puducherry) against the government not maintaining the Children's Park in Venketa Nagar. Protesters raised slogans to mark their protest and said that the play area and pedestrian walkway were beyond use. Protesters also highlighted the poor lighting in the park.

On 27 November 2023, family members of a murdered (coded separately) 45-year-old Dalit woman and local Dalit leaders staged a protest outside Sir Takhtasinhji General Hospital in Bhavnagar city (Gujarat) refusing to claim her body until all four accused were arrested.

On 27 November 2023, members of the DYFI staged a protest at the Collectorate in Thoothukudi city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to fix the concrete slabs on the drainage channel in Rajiv Nagar in ward 58 the Thoothukudi Corporation. Protesters also submitted a petition to the Collector.

On 27 November 2023, a large number of farmers from Melur staged a sit-in protest in the Ottakovilpatti hamlet in Kottampatti village (Madurai, Tamil Nadu) against the district administration's decision to operate a granite quarry in the Melur area. Protesters said that the quarry would affect agriculture in the area. Protesters carried placards highlighting their concerns.

On 27 November 2023, thousands of farmers from Melur and Tirumangalam staged a protest rally from the union office to the Public Works Department (PWD) office in Melur town (Madurai, Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to release water from the Vagai dam to irrigate their single crop area.

On 27 November 2023, members of the AIADMK along with a former minister staged a protest at the Collectorate in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to release water from the Vaigai dam to irrigate agricultural land in Thirumangalam and Melur. Police arrested the protesters.

On 27 November 2023, members of the Andhra Pradesh Rythu Sanghala Samanvya Samithi (A.P. Farmers' Unions Coordination Committee) and the Trade Unions' Ikya Vedika (Trade Union's United Forum) along with a former TDP minister, members of the AIKS, the CITU, the AITUC, members of the Water Users Associations Federation, A.P. Tenant Farmers Association and others launched a two day protest in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against the BJP-led Union government's laws and policies. Protesters demanded that pre-paid smart electricity meters for agriculture motors to withdrawn by the state and Union governments.
On 27 November 2023, locals led by a sarpanch (local government head) held a protest at Buttal town (Udhampur district, J&K) against overcharging of fare by mini-buses plying on a few roads.

On 27 November 2023, employees on election duty staged protests in several locations in Telangana state (coded to Hyderabad) demanding postal ballots to exercise their right to vote during the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections. Protesters also threatened to boycott their election duties.

On 27 November 2023, women wing of Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) detained a Muslim woman (likely Meitei-Pangal based on location) over accusations that she was spying on them, at Gamgiphai village (Kangpokpi, Manipur), amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state. Members of Assam Rifles later rescued the victim.

Around 27 November 2023 (as reported), 4 people clashed with workers at the toll plaza in Bastara village (Karnal, Haryana) when the workers confronted a group of people for forcibly raising the boom barrier - which resulted in vehicles passing the toll without paying fees. 7 people were injured.

On 27 November 2023, four assailants belonging to the Muslim community attacked an independent woman candidate in the Muradnagar area in Hyderabad city (Telangana) while the woman was campaigning for the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections. The assailants assaulted and injured the woman and snatched her mobile phone and money.

On 27 November 2023, members of INC, led by its State president (former deputy mayor), staged a protest at Sector 29-B in Chandigarh city against the eviction notices served to numerous houses in the area.

On 27 November 2023, members of the 108 Ambulance Employees Association went on strike and staged a protest at the Dhakoli area in Zirakpur town (SAS Nagar, Punjab) against the non-acceptance of their demands which included an increase in salaries and regularization of contractual jobs.

On 27 November 2023, members of the All Tripura Unorganized Workers Congress (ATUWC), a trade union affiliated with the INC, staged a protest march in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) over a six-point charter of demands including, seeking the re-launch of the state government's unorganized workers assistance scheme, special financial assistance for all unorganized workers during the coronavirus crisis, immediate issuance of labor cards to all construction workers registered with the Labour department, etc. The protestors submitted a public deputation to the Labour Commissioner.

On 27 November 2023, a TMC member was assaulted by TMC members of another faction with iron rods at Radhanagar area in Gosaba tehsil (South 24 Parganas district, WB) when he sought clarification from a contractor about the poor quality of a road construction in the area. He was killed in the incident.

On 27 November 2023, several people assaulted a man from the Dalit community with sticks in Sathra village (Budaun, Uttar Pradesh) for using a public tap to drink water. The man succumbed to his injuries. One person was arrested.
On 27 November 2023, the members of two political parties clashed with each other in Kadakkal town (Kollam, Kerala) for unknown reasons.

On 27 November 2023, members of the e Imphal Naga Forum (INF) along with members of the United Naga Council (UNC), the Tangkhul Baptist Churches, and the All Manipur Christian Organisation (AMCO) held a 'Imphal Naga People's Consultative Meeting' protest at the Tarung community hall in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the state government to restore peace amidst ongoing conflict between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters condemned the indifferent attitude of the BJP-led Union government.

On 27 November 2023, about 10000 farmers from across the state, including members of BKU, on tractor-trailers, gathered under the banner of SKM and staged 'day 2' of their 3-day protest along the road at Phase-11 near the Mohali-Chandigarh border in Mohali city (SAS Nagar, Punjab) demanding a legal guarantee of Minimum Support Price (MSP) for farmers, withdrawal of cases registered against farmers for 2020-21 protests, pension, and jobs for family members of farmers who died during the 2020-21 protests. The protest was part of a nationwide protest.

On 27 November 2023, about 2000 farmers from across the state, joined by the BKU National spokesperson, gathered under the banner of SKM and staged 'day 2' of their 3-day protest at Sector 5 in Panchkula city (Haryana) demanding a legal guarantee of Minimum Support Price (MSP) for farmers, withdrawal of cases registered against farmers for 2020-21 protests, pension, and jobs for family members of farmers who died during the 2020-21 protests. The protest was part of a nationwide protest.

On 27 November 2023, members of the SKM, the KRRS and the Joint Committee of Trade Unions staged a protest for the second day protest at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) demanding the withdrawal of the anti-people' policies of the Union government and the 'anti-farmer' policies of the previous BJP-led Karnataka state government.
On 27 November 2023, an SP MLA and his supporters staged a protest at a hospital in Meerut city (Uttar Pradesh) and refused full payment to the hospital for the treatment and discharge of a patient.

On 27 November 2023, teacher recruitment candidates were joined by the Chief of Azad Samaj Party during their protest at Eco Garden in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) against the deprivation of reservations due to irregularities in reservations during the assistant teacher recruitment process. The protesters also protested outside the residence of the President of Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (MLA).

On 27 November 2023, a section of TMC members held a protest by blocking a road at Mechkoka village (Cooch Behar district, WB) over the killing of a TMC member in a clash with a BJ member and his supporters at the same location on the previous day (coded separately).

On 27 November 2023, local people gathered in large numbers and staged a protest near Mursan town (Hathras, Uttar Pradesh) against the Public Works Department for the poor quality of road repair work between the Mursan block office to Palawat village.
On 27 November 2023, locals held a protest at Gobindsar town (Kathua district, J&K) over lack of water supply in their area.
On 27 November 2023, family members of a deceased woman held a protest at Baramulla city (J&K) over claimed medical negligence leading to a woman's death.

On 27 November 2023, villagers staged a sit-in protest in Ikkalur village near the Talavadi forest range of the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve (STR) (coded to Thalavadi, Erode, Tamil Nadu) demanding the release of three farmers who had been detained by the forest authorities for questioning after an elephant was found dead when the animal was electrocuted while attempting to enter a maize field by crossing a live wire.

On 27 November 2023, local residents under the aegis of the Janakeeya Samithi (people's forum) staged protests in the Mattappally locality in Bharanicavu village (Alappuzha, Kerala) demanding the stopping of the soil quarrying in the area. Protesters said that the quarrying in connection with the construction of a national highway had not been stopped despite the state Agriculture minister's direction.

On 27 November 2023, residents of Mamidalapalli village staged a protest on the road near the Rangapet village (Karimnagar, Telangana) after a father and son died in an accident when the auto they were travelling in was hit by a lorry carrying sand. Protesters along with the bodies of the victims and demanded compensation for the family of the victims.

On 27 November 2023, BJP corporators along with a former MLA and a deputy mayor staged a protest in front of the city police commissioner's office in Belagavi city (Karnataka) against the arrest of a BJP corporator for assaulting a resident who had installed a mobile tower on his house. Protesters said that the arrest was political in nature and demanded the suspension of the officer who had arrested the corporator. Police stopped the protesters from entering the commissioner's office.

On 27 November 2023, police sub-inspector (PSI) job aspirants staged a protest outside the Chief Minister's official residence on Kumara Krupa Road in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) demanding that candidates for the recruitment re-examination be given two months to prepare. Police detained about 75 protesters.

On 27 November 2023, residents staged a protest at the sarpanch's (village head) residence in Salvador do Mundo village (North Goa, Goa) against the decision to restart work on a residential house and staff quarters by a fashion designer. Protesters objected to the construction work and demanded an explanation from the authorities.

On 27 November 2023, villagers from Ooththupatti near Kovilpatti staged a protest at the Collectorate in Thoothukudi city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to provide funding to demolish the dilapidated school building and reconstruct a new structure for the safety of students. Protesters also submitted a petition to the Collector.

On 27 November 2023, villagers from Kumarapuram Colony along with their children staged a protest at the Collectorate in Thoothukudi city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to repair building of the panchayat union primary school at South Kumarapuram. Protesters said that the building posed a threat to the students and due to this reason the children were not being sent to school. Protesters also submitted a petition to the Collector.

On 27 November 2023, a group of villagers from Kaalvaai hamlet near Srivaikundam staged a protest at the Collectorate in Thoothukudi city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the removal of an encroachment at the entrance of Esakkiamman Temple South Street in the village. Protesters said that the structure was blocking the movement of vehicles and free flow of rainwater. Protesters also submitted a petition to the Collector.

On 27 November 2023, parents of a class 10 students staged a protest in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against a teacher who had beaten up their son for scoring low marks in the quarterly exams as a result of which he had fallen ill and was undergoing treatment. Protesters also submitted a petition submitted to Chief Educational Officer (CEO) and demanding action against the teacher.

On 27 November 2023, villagers staged protests and counter protests in support and against the Bhoma road widening project during the gram sabha (village meeting) in Boma village (North Goa, Goa), Villagers questioned what the panchayat members were supporting the project and accused them of taking the government's side despite not knowing the impact of the road expansion project. Police intervened to control the situation.

Around 27 November 2023 (as reported), students staged a protest at Dr Shakuntala Misra National Rehabilitation University (DSMNRU) in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) over various demands including the provision of clean drinking water, action against students who assaulted a visually-impaired girl (coded separately) and improvement in the quality of food, among others.

On 27 November 2023, students, parents and local residents staged a road block at Melaghar town (Sepahijala, Tripura) against a construction company over claimed encroachment of school land. The company continued construction work at night despite receiving disapproval from the local residents regarding land encroachment and disturbances due to construction at night.

On 28 November 2023, residents along with members of the Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam staged a protest at the Corporation in Tirunelveli city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to lay permanent roads on four streets in Aditanar Nagar in the Palayamkottai area. Protesters also demanded the fixing of streetlights and the construction of proper drainage channels. Protesters also submitted a petition to the mayor.
On 28 November 2023, locals along with BJP members held a protest at Naxalbari town (Darjeeling district, WB) over the use of inferior quality material in road construction.

On 28 November 2023, members of the BJP staged a protest at the Gadagi Chennappa Circle in Ballari city (Karnataka) after the election to the post of Mayor of Ballari was postponed for unknown reasons. Protesters accused the Regional Commissioner of misusing his power to act as a puppet in the hands of the INC.

On 28 November 2023, a big number of BJP members including an MP staged a protest in Kothapalle village (Karimnagar, Telangana) accusing members of the BRS of distributing money to voters along with voter slips for the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections. Protesters raised slogans against the BJP candidate and the election authorities for not taking action.

On 28 November 2023, hundreds of workers, CITU members led by a former CPI(M) minister held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the central government over denial of remunerative prices to apple farmers, to demand hundred percent import duty on imported apples and against the Indus water treaty over claimed losses incurred by J&K due to limits on power generation and demanded that the center compensate it for the losses among other demands and against the arrest of sevens students for raising claimed objectionable slogans in Srinagar (coded separately).

On 28 November 2023, hundreds of CITU workers and Samyukta Kisan Morcha held a sit-in protest as part of nationwide campaign at Port Blair city (South Andaman district, A&NI) against the BJP-led central government over claimed anti-worker and anti-farmer policies, to demand minimum wages, against the Electricity Amendment Act 2022 among other issues.

On 28 November 2023, CITU workers and Samyukta Kisan Morcha (a farmer organization) held a sit-in protest as part of nationwide campaign at Diglipur city (South Andaman district, A&NI) against the BJP-led central government over claimed anti-worker and anti-farmer policies, to demand minimum wages, against the Electricity Amendment Act 2022 among other issues.

On 28 November 2023, thousands of CITU workers and Samyukta Kisan Morcha (a farmer organization) and AIKS leaders held a sit-in protest as part of nationwide campaign at Kolkata city (WB) against the BJP-led central government over claimed anti-worker and anti-farmer policies, to demand minimum wages, against the Electricity Amendment Act 2022 among other issues.

On 28 November 2023, members of the Dhangar community briefly staged a rasta roko (road blockade) protest in Padegaon, Harsul, Chikalthana and Kanchanwadi areas of Aurangabad city (Aurangabad, Maharashtra) demanding for their inclusion in the ST category.
On 28 November 2023, members of the Dhangar community briefly staged a rasta roko (road blockade) protest in Waluj city (Aurangabad, Maharashtra) demanding their inclusion in the ST category.
On 28 November 2023, members of the Dhangar community briefly staged a rasta roko (road blockade) protest in Bidkin city (Aurangabad, Maharashtra) demanding their inclusion in the ST category.

On 29 December 2023, residents of some villages including Irukkandurai, Marukalkurichi and Anaikudi staged a protest in Tirunelveli district (coded to Tirunelveli city, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for disbursing different relief amounts for victims of the recent floods in Tamil Nadu.

On 29 December 2023, members of 5 farmers' unions including BKU (Rajewal), BKU (Mansa), and Kisan Sangarsh Committee, led by the President of BKU (Rajewal) and Sanyukt Samaj Morcha, staged a protest, raising black flags and slogans, near the Dara Studio Chowk in Mohali city (SAS Nagar, Punjab) against the proposed meeting between the central government and the Punjab state government to discuss the Sutlej-Yamuna Link (SYL) water canal issue. The protesters demanded the central government stop interfering in state matters.

On 29 December 2023, some members of khaps and farmer bodies staged a protest march in Narwana town (Jind, Haryana) demanding the release of a woman who was arrested for breaching security and protesting at the Parliament premises on 13 December (coded separately).

Around 29 December 2023 (as reported), local people gathered under the banner of the Regional Development Forum (Lambloo) and staged a symbolic protest by tying posters around the neck of the goat in Lambloo town (Hamirpur, Himachal Pradesh) demanding the re-opening of closed institutions.

On 29 December 2023, locals assaulted a tribal man with plastic, iron pipes, a belt, and sticks in Barghat town (Seoni, Madhya Pradesh) on suspicion of theft. The accused also forced the victim's mother-in-law to transfer 14 acres of land in the name of another employee through a notary.

On 29 December 2023, members of the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) led by local NCP-SP Member of Parliament, marched in protest to Baramati city from Daund city (Pune, Maharashtra) during the 3rd day of the 100-km long 'Kisan Aakrosh Morcha' to press for the demands of farmers, including lifting the restriction on onion export.

Around 30 December 2023 (as reported), a large number of protesters staged a protest as a part of the Bharat Bandh called by the Adivasi Sengel Abhiyan in Behali village (Biswanath, Assam) and 105 protesters were detained by the police. Protesters demanded that the Adivasi community should be given the recognition of the Sarna Dhorom code, and should be granted the status of a protected category under the constitution of India and that the Sengel language should be granted the status of first state language for the state of Jharkhand and the status of the second additional language in the states of Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.

On 30 December 2023, a group of mid-day meal staffs under the Mid-Day Meal Workers and Helpers Welfare Association staged a protest in Agartala city (West Tripura) and demanded higher wages, annual bonus, pension and other benefits. Protesters stated that their protests would escalate if their demands were not met.

Around 30 December 2023 (as reported), Assam Congress members with the Guwahati Unit of the Congress Committee staged a protest at Rajiv Bhawan in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) and condemned the CM of Assam for his derogatory remark against people belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The CM had posted a tweet which mentioned that the duty of Shudras is to serve the other three castes.

On 30 December 2023, members of the Manipur Ima Kangleipak Meitei Leipak (Meitei women group) staged a sit in protest in the state (coded to Imphal city, Imphal West, Manipur), demanded the government to identify illegal immigrants in the state and deport them immediately amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters raised slogans and also demanded the implementation of National Register of Citizens (NRC).

On 30 December 2023, members of the Manipur Youth League (MAYOL) continued the 21 day long march for the eleventh day from Nongada village to Sagolmang village (Imphal East, Manipur) under the theme 'National Regeneration' amidst ongoing conflict between Meitei and Tribal communities. The march was organized with the aim to regenerate the Manipuri society, protect the indigenous communities in the state, promote peaceful co-existence, bring uniform development and restore peace in the state. Protesters shouted slogans and public meetings were also conducted.

Around 30 December 2023 (as reported), locals blocked roads along the highway at Barangabari village (Biswanath, Assam) as a protest and demanded the construction of a divider on the road and U-turn. This came after a driver collided with a speeding vehicle and died. The blockade was lifted after the cabinet minister of Assam who was also stranded due to the road block assured locals that actions would be taken.

On 30 December 2023, supporters of Aurangabad Member of Parliament (MP) from AIMIM staged a protest at the railway station in Aurangabad city (Maharashtra) against the non-inclusion of the MP name in an early invitation of the inaugural run of the maiden Vande Bharat Express train. Later police detained the supporters.

On 30 December 2023, truck drivers suddenly blocked the road leading to Kandla and Mundra port near Samakhiali town (Kachchh, Gujarat) in a demonstration against the proposed new penal provisions for hit-and-run cases in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (seeks to repeal and replace the Indian Penal Code, 1870). Police resorted to lathicharge to clear the road, and clashed with the drivers as they threw stones and damaged police and state transport buses. 1 policeman injured. Police also detained 9 demonstrators.

On 30 December 2023, family members of the deceased gathered on the main route from Zero Mile to Sabour and staged a protest in Bhagalpur city (Bihar) demanding compensation for the loss due to the fatal accident. A local JD(U) MLA slapped one of the protestors.

On 30 December 2023, 10 members of INC showed a black flag and held a protest in front of the Shree Jagannath Temple Administration (SJTA) office in Puri city (Odisha) opposing the visit of newly inducted BJD leader and former 5T secretary for demolition of heritage buildings in Puri under Parikrama Project and insulting Jagannath culture by bringing a Youtuber accused of promoting beef consumption. Police arrested five INC members.

On 30 December 2023, around 10 to 15 masked men assaulted the vice-president of BJD's Kendrapara minority (Muslim) cell vice president with lathis and sticks at his shop in Kendrapara town (Odisha) over a past dispute. The vice president was critically injured. The men also ransacked his shop and looted Rs 95,000 from the cash counter.

On 30 December 2023, villagers held a road blockade after a fatal road accident at Deobharandi village (Nabarangpur district, Odisha) demanding adequate compensation to the next of the deceased's kin. Police later convinced the villagers to withdraw the protest.

On 30 December 2023, Adivasi Sengel Abhiyan (a tribal group) held a protest by blocking a railway track as part of a 12-hour shutdown call at Purulia district (WB) to demand recognition of the Sarna religion in the census.

On 30 December 2023, Adivasi Sengel Abhiyan (a tribal group) held a protest by blocking a railway track as part of a 12-hour shutdown call at Bankura district (WB) to demand recognition of the Sarna religion in the census.

On 30 December 2023, Adivasi Sengel Abhiyan (a tribal group) held a protest by blocking a railway track as part of a 12-hour shutdown call at Jhargram district (WB) to demand recognition of the Sarna religion in the census.

On 30 December 2023, Adivasi Sengel Abhiyan (a tribal group) held a protest by blocking a railway track as part of a 12-hour shutdown call at Paschim Medinipur district (coded as Medinipur city (Paschim Medinipur district, WB) to demand recognition of the Sarna religion in the census.

On 30 December 2023, Adivasi Sengel Abhiyan (a tribal group) held a protest by blocking a railway track as part of a 12-hour shutdown call at Adra city (Purulia district, WB) to demand recognition of the Sarna religion in the census.

On 30 December 2023, Adivasi Sengel Abhiyan (a tribal group) held a protest by blocking a railway track as part of a 12-hour shutdown call at Saltora village (Bankura district, WB) to demand recognition of the Sarna religion in the census.

On 30 December 2023, Adivasi Sengel Abhiyan (a tribal group) held a protest by blocking a railway track as part of a 12-hour shutdown call at Paschim Bardhaman district (coded as Asansol city (Paschim Bardhaman district, WB)) to demand recognition of the Sarna religion in the census.

On 30 December 2023, Adivasi Sengel Abhiyan (a tribal group) held a protest by blocking a railway track as part of a 12-hour shutdown call at Kharibari city (Darjeeling district, WB) to demand recognition of the Sarna religion in the census.

On 30 December 2023, ASHA workers (female health workers) union held a protest at Naxalbari city (Darjeeling district, WB) over police inaction in the case of an ASHA worker who was being harassed by her in-laws and demanded action.

On 30 December 2023, Kudumi Mahato community members held a protest sit-in as part of a 12-hour nationwide campaign to block railway tracks at Kalipahari station near Asansol town (Paschim Bardhaman district, WB) to demand scheduled tribe status and the intervention of the state and centre for the inclusion of Kurmali language in the Eight Schedule to the Constitution of India.

On 30 December 2023, Kudumi Mahato community members held a protest sit-in as part of a 12-hour nationwide campaign to block railway tracks at Kantadih town (Purulia district, WB) to demand scheduled tribe status and the intervention of the state and centre for the inclusion of Kurmali language in the Eight Schedule to the Constitution of India.

On 30 December 2023, Kudumi Mahato community members held a protest sit-in as part of a 12-hour nationwide campaign to block railway tracks at Adina town (Maldah district, WB) to demand scheduled tribe status and the intervention of the state and centre for the inclusion of Kurmali language in the Eight Schedule to the Constitution of India.
On 30 December 2023, many BJP members held a protest at Nashri area in Ramban district (J&K) against the increase in the toll tax at Chenani-Nashri tunnel.

On 30 December 2023, members of the BJP, including a BJP MP and the BJP State general secretary, staged protests at four locations including at ITO crossing in Delhi - Darya Ganj (Central Delhi, Delhi), near India Gate, near Le Meridian Hotel, and at 11 Murti roundabout (coded separately), against the AAP-led state government whom the protesters accused of failing to address the rising air pollution in the city.

On 30 December 2023, farmers gathered under the banner of BKU (Charuni) and Rahon Road Sangharsh Union staged a protest at the Ladhowal Toll Plaza near Ladhowal Village (Ludhiana West, Ludhiana, Punjab) against the poor condition of the Rahon road.

On 30 December 2023, a section of diocese members staged a protest in front of the Nilackal diocese of the Orthodox Church in Ranni town (Pathanamthitta, Kerala) after a priest along with 47 Christian families joined the BJP and attended a Christmas function hosted by a minister.

On 30 December 2023, hundreds of local people (likely farmers, since the protest is on protection of crops) from various villages staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Collectorate in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) against the destruction of crops caused by stray cattle.

On 30 December 2023, local people, gathered under the banner of Kishan Sangarsh Samiti (farmers' advocacy body) and Swayam Sangharsh Samit, staged a protest in Ramnagar city (Nainital, Uttarakhand) against the rise in tiger attacks and demanded compensation and free treatment for the victims and their family members.

On 30 December 2023, villagers and members of the Namathu Nilam Namathe Vivasayigal Nala Sangam (Our Land is Our Farmers' Welfare Association) staged a protest at a farm in Thalavadi town (Erode, Tamil Nadu) after a farmer was killed by a wild elephant when he was guarding his ragi crop. The protesters demanded compensation and a government job for the kin of the deceased, and accused the Forest Department officials of not responding to their phone calls during emergencies.

On 30 December 2023, farmers from 11 villages launched a protest in Anakavur town (Tiruvannamalai, Tamil Nadu) demanding the authorities to cancel the Goondas Act and release a farmer for protesting against the proposed State Industries Promotion Corporation of Tamil Nadu (SIPCOT) project in Melma.

On 30 December 2023, anganwadi workers (female health workers) along with the TDP president (former Chief Minister and current leader of opposition) staged a protest in Kuppam city (Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for not regularising their services and increasing their wages.

On 30 December 2023, JKPDP members along with its chief staged a sit-in protest at Bafliaz town (Poonch district, J&K) over not being allowed by police to meet the families of Gujjar community members killed under custody by India army in Bafliaz town on 23 December 2023 (coded separately). Police later detained three JKPDP leaders.

On 30 December 2023, residents of Siddayyanahundi village in Nanjangud along with members of the KRRS and members of the Kasuvinahalli gram panchayat staged a protest in front of Excise Department's office in Mysuru city (Karnataka) opposing the decision to set up a liquor shop in the village. The protesters said that the liquor shop was situated close to schools and colleges and requested the authorities to shift the shop.

On 30 December 2023, e-rickshaw drivers staged a protest at the Mayapuri police station in the Delhi - Delhi Cantonment (New Delhi, Delhi) demanding action over the death of a man who was killed when his e-rickshaw was hit by a car driven a policeman (likely drunk, based on the report).

On 30 December 2023, contractual employees gathered under the banner of Jal Supply and Sanitation Contract Workers' Union and staged a protest march and burned an effigy in Tarn Taran city (Punjab) demanding the regularization of jobs.

On 30 December 2023, members of the '8736 Kache Adhyapak Union Punjab' staged a protest along the national highway and also climbed atop a water tank near the Grain Market in Dirba town (Sangrur, Punjab) against the state government whom the protesters accused of 'incomplete regularization' and demanded the provision of benefits on par with state government employees.

Around 30 December 2023 (as reported), women organisations staged protests in Karnataka state (coded to Bengaluru, Bengaluru Urban) demanding the arrest of an RSS leader for his derogatory remarks against Muslim women.

On 30 December 2023, hundreds of local people staged a protest outside the Girinagar range forest office next to Mahrar village (Sirmaur, Himachal Pradesh) demanding the removal of nomadic Gujjar people from the government land they had encroached upon. The protesters attempted to enter the office premises during which the main gate broke, then clashed with police who tried to stop them.

On 30 December 2023, BJP councillors clashed with SP and BSP Councillors during a Meerut Nagar Nigam board meeting in Meerut city (Uttar Pradesh) over a comment made by a BJP councillor on house tax. A video of the incident was circulated online.

On 30 December 2023, local people staged a protest, raising slogans, along the Narnaul-Patan highway near Narnaul city (Mahendragarh, Haryana) demanding action against the accused whose overloaded dumper truck hit a tractor-trolley and seriously injured 3 women.

Around 30 December 2023 (as reported), family members of a deceased person staged a protest outside the police station in Meerut city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the remaining accused involved in the assault and death of a man. 3 accused were arrested.

On 30 December 2023, family members of a deceased person staged a protest along the Chaubeypur-Shivli road in Chaubeypur village (Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a young man whom the protesters claimed was murdered.

On 30 December 2023, the parents of a boy who was beaten by his teacher for not doing his homework staged a protest in front of the Sri Chaitanya School in Currency Nagar in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) demanding action against the teacher.

On 30 December 2023, relatives and parents of an infant who passed away soon after being administered a vaccine staged a demonstration at the Urban Primary Health Care Centre (UPHC) in Arakkonam town (Ranipet, Tamil Nadu) accusing the hospital of being responsible for the baby's death. The rioters vandalised the hospital and entered into an argument with the doctors and duty staff.

On 30 December 2023, truck drivers blocked the road on Rajkot-Ahmedabad highway near Maliyasan village (Rajkot, Gujarat) in a demonstration against the proposed new penal provisions for hit-and-run cases in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (seeks to repeal and replace the Indian Penal Code, 1870). Police cleared the road and detained two drivers.

On 30 December 2023, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization), reached Thane district (Maharashtra) and staged a protest march blaming the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' started from Bengaluru city on 10 December.

On 30 December 2023, members of the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) led by local NCP-SP Member of Parliament, marched in protest to the collectorate in Pune city from Baramati city (Pune, Maharashtra) during the 4th day of the 100-km long 'Kisan Aakrosh Morcha' to press for the demands of farmers, including lifting restriction on onion export.

On 30 December 2023, members of the BJP, including a BJP MP and the BJP State general secretary, staged protests at four locations including at 11 Murti roundabout in Delhi - Chanakya Puri (New Delhi, Delhi), against the AAP-led state government whom the protesters accused of failing to address the rising air pollution in the city.

On 30 December 2023, members of the BJP, including a BJP MP and the BJP State general secretary, staged protests at four locations including near India Gate in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi), against the AAP-led state government whom the protesters accused of failing to address the rising air pollution in the city.

On 30 December 2023, members of the BJP, including a BJP MP and the BJP State general secretary, staged protests at four locations including near Le Meridian Hotel in Delhi - Parliament Street (New Delhi, Delhi), against the AAP-led state government whom the protesters accused of failing to address the rising air pollution in the city.

On 31 December 2023, students and staff of Princeton International School staged a sit in protest in the school at Kshetrigao in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) against the grenade found in their campus (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters raised placards and condemned the act.

On 31 December 2023, a group of drivers under the Khowai District Committee of the All Drivers Welfare Association staged a protest in front of Agartala Press Club in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) and demanded several points. Their demands included the formation of national and state commissions for drivers, launch of the All India Drivers Aayog Diwas from September 1, to provide full renewal to commercial drivers, to regularize drivers working on outsourcing contracts under equal pay in various corporations and institutions and an insurance of 20 lakhs for each motorist.

On 31 December 2023, members of the Manipur Youth League (MAYOL) continued the 21 day long march for the twelfth day from Sagolmang village to Lamlong village in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) under the theme 'National Regeneration' amidst ongoing conflict between Meitei and Tribal communities. The march was organized with the aim to regenerate the Manipuri society, protect the indigenous communities in the state, promote peaceful co-existence, bring uniform development and restore peace in the state. Protesters shouted slogans and public meetings were also conducted.

On 31 December 2023, 7 suspected Bajrang Dal members 'detained' 3 individuals in a pick-up van with two bullocks, fired shots in the air and set the van on fire in Kanika under Hemgir police limits (Sundargarh, Odisha) over suspicion of cattle smuggling.

On 31 December 2023, nearly 250 truck drivers under the banner of All India Motor Transport Congress held a demonstration by blocking a road and burning tires at Chanditala city (Hooghly district, WB) as part of a 2 day nationwide strike called by the AIMTC against the proposed new penal provisions for hit and run cases in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (the recently passed replacement of the Indian Penal Code, 1870). Police later arrested 12 of them.
On 31 December 2023, locals held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) to demand better maintenance of the swimming pool and its renovation.

On 31 December 2023, drivers of trucks and commercial vehicles staged a protest, raising slogans, and blocked the Etah National Highway 91 with a large number of stationary vehicles near Umravupar village in Etah district (Uttar Pradesh) against the strict provisions applicable to truck operators and commercial drivers stated within the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (Indian Justice Code) - which includes a 10-year jail sentence for hit-and-run cases.

On 31 December 2023, drivers of trucks and commercial vehicles staged a protest, raising slogans, and blocked the Bypass over Sardala drain on Kasganj Road with stationary vehicles in Kasganj district (Uttar Pradesh) against the strict provisions applicable to truck operators and commercial drivers stated within the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (Indian Justice Code) - which includes a 10-year jail sentence for hit-and-run cases.

On 31 December 2023, members of the Almaya Munnettam (lay people's forum comprising members of the Catholic church) and a group of parishioners staged separate protests in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against those who were spreading derogatory remarks against a priest who reached the parish to bless a marriage.

On 31 December 2023, the family members of a Dalit man who was killed by members of a dominant caste group (coded separately) staged a protest along the Tirunelveli-Tiruchendur road in Thoothukudi city (Tamil Nadu) demanding action against the accused.

On 31 December 2023, locals, including a Uttarakhand Parivartan Party (UPP) functionary, gathered under the banner of Kishan Sangarsh Samiti (farmers' advocacy body) and Swayam Sangharsh Samit and staged a protest at the Corbett Headquarters in Ramnagar city (Nainital, Uttarakhand) against the rise in tiger attacks and demanded compensation and free treatment for the victims and their family members. Police arrested 23 protesters.

On 31 December 2023, hundreds of members of various Kannada organisations including the KRV staged a demonstration at the Chennamma Circle in Belagavi city (Karnataka) against the arrest of the KRV president for staging a demonstration and vandalising English language signboards in Bengaluru. The demonstrators shouted slogans against the INC-led state government. The demonstrators also scuffled with the police.

On 31 December 2023, around 8000 domestic breeding checkers affiliated to the Tamil Nadu Dengue Kosu Puzhu Olippu Munkala Paniyalar Sangam (Tamil Nadu Dengue Mosquito Worm Eradication Frontline Staff Association) staged a one-day protest by organising a hunger strike near the Rajarathinam stadium in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the health department to ensure them job without break and regular monthly salary. According to protestors, around 38,000 domestic breeding checkers worked to control breeding of aedes mosquitoes as part of dengue-control and prevention measures of the health department, but, their salaries were paid by local bodies.

On 31 December 2023, municipal workers affiliated to the Members of the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Workers and Employees Union staged a protest in Ongole city (Prakasam, Andhra Pradesh) against the corporation for hiring private garbage-collection vehicles to clear waste from the road since municipal workers were on an indefinite protest to demand equal pay for equal work. The protesters shouted slogans to mark their protest. Police detained the protesters.

On 31 December 2023, around 150 residents along with members of the NTK and the CPI(M) including a former MLA joined the ongoing sit-in protest, on the fifth day, in front of the Coromandel International Limited in the Ennore locality in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the permanent closure of the plant after ammonia gas leaked from a subsea pipeline.

On 31 December 2023, members of the RMPI staged a dharna (sit-in protest), raising slogans, in front of the police station in Majitha town (Amritsar, Punjab) against the police for failing to take action against the accused involved in the assault on a man and his family on 13 November.

On 31 December 2023, members of the SFI staged a protest at the Payyambalam beach in Kannur city (Kerala) against the Kerala Governor's attempt to 'saffronise universities' by appointing members of right-wing Hindu groups to the university senate. The protesters burned a 30-foot-tall effigy of the Governor to mark their protest.

On 31 December 2023, about 200 guest teachers from various districts gathered under the banner of Rajkiya Atithi Adhyapak Manch (RAAM) and staged a 'mahapadao' (large sit-in protest) at the grain market in Jagadhri town (Yamunanagar, Haryana) demanding the regularization of contractual jobs. The protesters were lathi-charged by the police when they tried to march towards the residence of a BJP State minister. A couple of protesters suffered injuries - including head injuries to the RAAM State president - and some protesters were detained and later released.

On 31 December 2023, around 250 people mostly members of the Cubbon Park Walkers Association (CPWA) staged a silent protest march at Cubbon Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) opposing the loud New Year's Eve celebrations at the clubs near the park. The protesters said that the park should be preserved for future generations and demanded that the clubs within its premises be shifted outside.

On 31 December 2023, supporters of a BJP leader and former MLA, who was previously with the TDP, clashed with supporters of a TDP leader in Dharmavaram town (Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh) after the BJP member put up posters along with images of TDP chief and the TDP wishing people a Happy New Year. Police intervened to separate the two groups.

On 31 December 2023, some members of the TDP vandalised the election office of a YSRCP minister on the Sai Baba Temple Road in the Chandramoulinagar locality in Guntur city (Andhra Pradesh). The rioters, who were in an inebriated state, pelted stones and broke the glass doors and windows. The police lathi-charged the rioters.

On 31 December 2023, passengers staged a protest and sat on the railway track at the railway station in Gurgaon city (Gurugram, Haryana) after some passengers were shut out of the train due to overcrowding.
On 31 December 2023, environmental activists staged a protest at Samrala Chowk in Ludhiana city (Punjab) against the pollution of Satluj (river), Buddha Dariya (stream), and subsoil water.

On 31 December 2023, over 50 relatives of a man who was murdered by three of his friends after an altercation broke out when they were consuming liquor, staged a road roko (road block) protest at the Jambai Junction on the Bhavani - Appakudal road in Bhavani town (Erode, Tamil Nadu) demanding action against the accused. The protesters stopped the police from taking the victim's body to the hospital for an autopsy.

On 31 December 2023, overnight, twelve members of Huiyel Mamom (a newly formed social-cultural organisation, likely Meitei based on name) physically assaulted a woman over consumption of alcohol somewhere in Imphal West (coded to Imphal city, Imphal West, Manipur). A video of the incident went viral. On 12 January the Chief Judicial Magistrate issued a 15 day remand and authorized the arrest of the involved women.

On 31 December 2023, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization), reached Govandi city (coded to Mumbai Suburban - Kurla, Maharashtra) and staged a protest march blaming the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' started from Bengaluru city on 10 December.
On 31 December 2023, members of Hindu and Muslim communities clashed in Garib Nawaz Nagar in Yashodhara Nagar police limits in Nagpur city (Maharashtra) over unknown reason.
