On 5 January 2024, BJP members led by a union minister and a local minister held a protest march at Alipurduar city (WB) to demand reopening of closed tea gardens.
On 5 January 2024, TMC members led by a minister held a protest at Dinhata town (Cooch Behar district, WB) to demand the arrest of a BJP minister over his claimed involvement in murder case.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Central Reserve Police Force
text: On 5 January 2024, around 200 locals joined by TMC supporters wielding sticks and bricks held a demonstration by burning tyres and blocking roads during a raid by the enforcement directorate officials at a TMC member's residence, clashed with the CRPF personnel accompanying them and assaulted the officials and the journalists accompanying them during the raid at Sarberia village in Sandeshkhali block area (North 24 Parganas district, WB). At least three enforcement directorate officials and several journalists were left injured and the vehicles and cameras were also left damaged.

On 5 January 2024, locals held a protest by blocking a road at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over the movement of overloaded trucks leading to aggregation of stones on the roads further leading to road accidents.

On 5 January 2024, members of the AIADMK staged a protest in front of Odhiansalai police station in Puducherry city (Puducherry) demanding the police to register a case against a DMK legislator and his supporters for making derogatory remarks against the AIADMK Puducherry unit secretary during a recent protest demanding the arrest of AIADMK member for obstructing the work of the DMK legislator in the Uppalam constituency (coded separately).

Around 5 January 2024 (as reported), 7-8 persons carrying AISF flags vandalised the office of an ed-tech company in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) to oppose the misleading tuition practices of the company. 5 AISF and AIYF members were detained subsequently in connection with this.

On 5 January 2024, local people and members of Bhartiya Gau Raksha Dal reinitiated their fast and sit-in protest at Umari village (Jalaun, Uttar Pradesh) against the failure of the state authorities to take action against the Umari Gaushala (cowshed) for the suspected negligence in the care of cows.

On 5 January 2024, members of Bhartiya Gau Raksha Dal and Bajrang Dal staged a protest at the Nagla Mandhat Gaushala (cowshed) in Asoi village (Hathras, Uttar Pradesh) over suspicions of negligence in the care of cows - after dead bodies of cows were found in the cowshed.

On 5 January 2024, street vendors along with members of the CITU and the CPI(M) staged a protest outside the Hosur Municipal Corporation in Hosur city (Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu) demanding the authorities to put a stop to the street vending committee election that was scheduled for next week by the Corporation. The protesters said that the corporation should issue identity cards for all the street vendors first, and then call for nominations through advertisements in the newspapers.

On 5 January 2024, local people (likely Dalit based on the issue) staged a protest in Sarmastpur Machhua village (Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh) against the vandalization of the statue of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar (a Dalit champion) and Mahatma Buddha on around 4 January (coded separately).

On 5 January 2024, family members of the deceased, local people, and farmers staged a protest and placed the deceased's body along the Madhotanda-Pilibhit Road near Madhotanda village (Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a man who was killed by a tiger. The protesters demanded compensation and contractual jobs for the deceased's family members.

On 5 January 2024, members of Hindu organizations staged a protest, raising slogans along the Tanakpur Road in Pilibhit city (Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected encroachment of government land near an ancient religious site.

On 5 January 2024, a group of people under the aegis of the Sri Mallikarjuna Sagar Welfare and Development Society staged a protest during the Chief Minister's Praja Vani (grievance redressal event) programme at the Praja Bhavan in Hyderabad city (Telangana) accusing a former BRS minister of taking over their lands using fake documents. The protesters raised slogans and held placards to mark their protest.

On 5 January 2024, lawyers staged a protest at the Tehsil premises in Sikandra Rao city (Hathras, Uttar Pradesh) after a lawyer was accidentally hit by a police baton while trying to intervene and de-escalate a fight earlier in the day.

Around 5 January 2024 (as reported), students staged protests across Andhra Pradesh state (coded to Amaravati, Guntur) to oppose the misleading practices of an ed-tech company. The protesters accused the company of charging high fees and making things difficult for the students.

On 5 January 2024, local people staged a protest in Mathavara village in Belur taluk (Hassan, Karnataka) after an agriculture labourer was killed in a wild elephant attack. The protesters accused the government of not taking action to prevent the attacks and demanded the Forest Minister to visit them and listen to their grievances.

On 5 January 2024, villagers staged a protest on the main road on the Hyderabad-Bengaluru national highway in Balanagar town (Mahbubnagar, Telangana) after five persons including three children who were travelling in an auto-rickshaw died and two others sustained injuries when a speeding van hit the vehicle.

On 5 January 2024, family members and relatives of a father and his minor son who died in an accident staged a protest at the Papannaguda Chowrasta on Gowrelly road in the Nagole area in Uppal city (Medchal-Malkajgiri, Telangana) demanding action against the truck driver who hit the motorcycle on which the victims were traveling.

On 5 January 2024, unidentified persons assaulted the enforcement directorate officials during a raid at Bongaon town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) after they arrested a former TMC local body chairman.

On 5 January 2024, bus operators assaulted a lawyer near the Bandiwala-Kabulshah crossing in Kabulshah village (Fazilka, Punjab) whom the assailants claimed vandalized a bus with the help of a colleague earlier, on the same day (coded separately).

On 5 January 2024, a mob of 30 to 40 people assaulted a police team in Dasada taluka under Zinzuvwada police station (Surendranagar district, Gujarat) against the detention of a man wanted in a prohibition case in the district. Two policemen, including a sub-inspector and a constable, were injured.

On 5 January 2024, hundreds of Adivasis staged a protest at the weekly market in Araku town (Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh) against the YRSCP for appointing a outsider as the Araku constituency in-charge by replacing the sitting MLA. The protesters said that the new appointee was an outsider married to a non-tribal and that she never visited the region during her time as the Araku MP.

On 5 January 2024, members of the BJP staged protests across Karnataka state (coded to Bengaluru) against the arrest of a Hindutva member in connection with a 1992 criminal case. The protesters accused the INC-led state government of targeting members of Hindutva groups before the inauguration of Ram Temple in Ayodhya

On 5 January 2024, farmers under the banner of BKU (Ugrahan), led by its District President, staged a protest in front of the Bhagwanpura Sugar Mill in Dhuri city (Sangrur, Punjab) demanding the payment of pending dues from last year's sugar cane crop procurement and restart of operations at the sugar mill.

On 5 January 2024, councillors belonging to the BRS staged a protest and prevented the revenue divisional officer (RDO) from leaving the municipal council hall in Khanapur town (Nirmal, Telangana) after the RDO denied permission to the municipal councillors to move a no-confidence motion against the chairman and the vice chairman. The protesters accused the RDO of being involved in irregularities while overseeing the civic body.

On 5 January 2024, around 500 farmers, led by the President of Bharatiya Kisan Parishad, staged a protest at the National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) office in Noida city (Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) demanding an increase in the compensation for land acquired by NTPC - between 1986 to 1995 - from farmers. The police prevented the protesters from locking the gate of the NTPC office.

On 5 January 2024, local people and family members of the deceased, joined by a local MLA, staged a protest along the Ahraula-Kaptanganj Road near the PG College in Samdi village (Azamgarh, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a motorcycle-borne young man and the injury of a girl (riding pillion) after getting hit by a truck.
On 5 January 2024, some bus passengers staged a protest in the Fazilka district (Punjab) against private bus operators for unidentified reasons.

On 5 January 2024, local people staged a protest, raising slogans, in Munimpur village (Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh) demanding the release of a young man whom the police detained for creating a ruckus. Before the protest, local people had gathered and attempted to capture a stray leopard.

On 5 January 2024, family members of the deceased staged a protest 'day 1' and refused to cremate the deceased's body at the General Hospital in Hisar city (Haryana) demanding action against the accused involved in the suicide of a man. The police registered charges against 6 accused - including a Deputy superintendent of police.

On 5 January 2024, members of the Joint Front of Engineers and Employees staged a brief protest 'day 2' (during lunch hours) outside the State Electricity Board office in Mandi town (Himachal Pradesh) demanding the payment of pending salaries and pensions, and the restoration of the old pension scheme.

On 5 January 2024, members of the Joint Front of Engineers and Employees staged a brief protest 'day 2' (during lunch hours) outside most of the State Electricity Board offices in the Himachal Pradesh state (coded as Shimla city) demanding the payment of pending salaries and pensions, and the restoration of the old pension scheme.

On 5 January 2024, about 200 local traders closed their shops and staged a protest from Ghantaghar intersection to Normal Square in Gorakhpur city (Uttar Pradesh) against the widening of the road as a part of the state government's proposal to develop a heritage corridor in the area.

On 5 January 2024, a large number of laborers under the banner of Mazdoor Mukti Morcha (MMM) staged a protest, raising slogans, along the Sangrur-Patiala Road near the Punjab Chief Minister's residence in Sangrur city (Punjab) over various demands including 700 rupees daily wage under MGNREGA, 200 days' work, disbursal of scholarship to Dalit students, and loan waiver to laborers, among others.

On 5 January 2024, local people and tour operators gathered under the banner of Ravai Jan Ekta Manch (Ravai People's Unity Platform) and staged a protest march, and closed shops and hotels, in Sankari village (Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand) against the forest department's decision to limit the number of tourists on certain routes. The protesters also made various demands including cancellation of fines on tour operators and implementation of a single-window system for tourist registrations.

Around 5 January 2024 (as reported), hundreds of sanitation workers staged a silent protest in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) against the Municipal Corporation (MC) and demanded better pay, retirement benefits, and promotions.

On 5 January 2024, lawyers staged a protest in Vaniyambadi town (Tirupathur, Tamil Nadu) demanding a Combined Court Complex in the town since the Judicial Magistrate Court, Subordinate Court and District Munisf Courts were located in three different parts of town which were causing for lawyers and the court staff.

On 5 January 2024, residents staged a protest in the Kolapalli locality in Pandalur town (The Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu) against the forest officials after a leopard attacked and injured a child. The protesters demanded the officials to capture the animal.

On 5 January 2024, members of the BJP including a former MLA staged a protest in Hubballi city (Dharwad, Karnataka) against the arrest of a Hindutva member in connection with a 1992 criminal case. The protesters accused the INC-led state government of targeting members of Hindutva groups before the inauguration of Ram Temple in Ayodhya. The police detained the protesters.

On 5 January 2024, 70-80 local women staged a demonstration and smashed bottles of liquor - forcefully taken from liquor vends - at Nagla Hiraman in Banpur village (Agra, Uttar Pradesh) against the negative influence of the liquor vends on local youth whom the demonstrators claimed are getting addicted to drugs. No report of injuries.

On 5 January 2024, drivers protested on the streets and raised slogans in Gohpur town (Biswanath, Assam) against the new hit and run law under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita under which drivers can be imprisoned for 10 years along with a fine if they cause an accident due to negligence and escape. This protest was a part of the nationwide protests and 48 hour strike in Assam which was later reduced to 24 hours.

On 5 January 2024, drivers protested on the streets and raised slogans in Bongaigaon city (Bongaigaon, Assam) against the new hit and run law under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita under which drivers can be imprisoned for 10 years along with a fine if they cause an accident due to negligence and escape. This protest was a part of the nationwide protests and 48 hour strike in Assam which was later reduced to 24 hours.

On 5 January 2024, drivers protested on the streets and raised slogans in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) against the new hit and run law under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita under which drivers can be imprisoned for 10 years along with a fine if they cause an accident due to negligence and escape. This protest was a part of the nationwide protests and 48 hour strike in Assam which was later reduced to 24 hours.

On 5 January 2024, drivers protested on the streets and raised slogans in Tezpur town (Sonitpur, Assam) against the new hit and run law under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita under which drivers can be imprisoned for 10 years along with a fine if they cause an accident due to negligence and escape. This protest was a part of the nationwide protests and 48 hour strike in Assam which was later reduced to 24 hours.

On 5 January 2024, drivers protested on the streets and raised slogans in Tinsukia town (Tinsukia, Assam) against the new hit and run law under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita under which drivers can be imprisoned for 10 years along with a fine if they cause an accident due to negligence and escape. This protest was a part of the nationwide protests and 48 hour strike in Assam which was later reduced to 24 hours.

On 5 January 2024, locals including members of Meira Paibi (women torch bearers, likely Meitei based on action) staged a protest at Manaingkhol in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) and condemned the firing that took place the previous night (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 5 January 2024, Meira Paibis (women torch bearers, likely Meitei based on action) staged a sit in protest at Senjam Chirang village (Imphal West, Manipur) and condemned the continuous attacks of their village by armed Kuki assailants amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters also demanded the replacement of central forces with state forces (mostly comprising of Meiteis) due to their perceived negligence by central forces against attacks from armed Kuki assailants.

On 5 January 2024, members of the Manipur Youth League (MAYOL) continued the 21 day long march for the seventeenth day from Malom village to Sagolband Moirang Hanuba Leirak in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) under the theme 'National Regeneration' amidst ongoing conflict between Meitei and Tribal communities. The march was organized with the aim to regenerate the Manipuri society, protect the indigenous communities in the state, promote peaceful co-existence, bring uniform development and restore peace in the state. Protesters shouted slogans and public meetings were also conducted.

On 5 January 2024, a large number of protesters stopped truck drivers who were not a part of the nationwide protest and draped phulam gamocha (traditional piece of cloth significant for the indigenous people of Assam) on them as a mark of protest in Biswanath town (Biswanath, Assam) against the new hit and run law under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita under which drivers can be imprisoned for 10 years along with a fine if they cause an accident due to negligence and escape.

On 5 January 2024, a large number of people as a part of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey) staged a protest, carrying placards and raising slogans, at the High Court in Allahabad city (Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh) against the BJP-led central and state governments over various issues including corruption, communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The Yatra which began from Bengaluru city was initiated by RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization) on 10 December 2023, and is scheduled to conclude in New Delhi on 3 March 2024 - likely to pass through 80 districts across 13 states.

On 6 January 2024, 17 persons assaulted a man belonging to the Lambadi community and a woman belonging to the Muslim community when they were sitting on the Fort Lake Tankbed and talking in Belagavi city (Karnataka) based on the suspicion that they were in an inter-faith relationship. The assailants took them to a room near the lake and beat them up despite the victims telling them that they were cousins and not in a relationship.

On 6 January 2024, five persons assaulted two on-duty Indore Municipal Corporation employees with tillers and hammers in the Malharganj police station area of Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) over cutting a tree illegally.

On 6 January 2024, members of the AIMIM assaulted and threatened members of the INC including a minority leader at Ambedkar Bhavan in the Chaderghat locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) for visiting the locality to check the ongoing work of Praja Palana program (Chief Minister's grievance redressal program). The assailants warned the victims against visiting the locality again.

On 6 January 2024, retrenched employees gave death threats to the employer, assaulted a person, and opened fire outside the Dollex sugar mill in Erai village in Barauni area (Datia, Madhya Pradesh) after some of them were fired from the sugar mill. They fled the scene afterward.

On 6 January 2024, locals (likely from the Hindu community based on location) held a protest at Chabba Demote town (Ramban district, J&K) against the claimed desecration of a religious site by unidentified persons.

On 6 January 2024, a large number of people (likely from the Hindu community based on location) held a protest march at Ramban town (J&K) against the claimed desecration of a religious site by unidentified persons.

On 6 January 2024, parents of around 110 adults with various intellectual disabilities enrolled with Sanjay School Vocational Training and Rehabilitation Centre, Porvorim, took out a protest march to Panaji city (North Goa, Goa) against the state government for not making arrangements for the children to attend school after a student died while visiting the Aadhaar centre on the second floor of the school building. The children were told not to come to school and were left nowhere to go.

On 6 January 2024, a large number of INC members, led by the INC State president (former MLA) and the former Uttarakhand Chief minister (INC), staged a protest march from Rajiv Gandhi complex to Gandhi Park in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) against the BJP-led central and state governments whom the protesters accused of failing to provide jobs and address the issue of rising unemployment.

On 6 January 2024, locals held a protest and blocked a BJP minister at Bairagir Hat village (Cooch Behar district, WB) against the BJP-led central government over lack of funding for MGNREGA scheme (a rural employment scheme).
On 6 January 2024, BJP members held a state-wide protest across WB (coded as Kolkata city (WB)) against the attacks on enforcement directorate teams in Bongaon and Sandeshkhali (coded separately).

On 6 January 2024, BJP members held a protest by blocking a road as part of a state-wide campaign at Howrah city (WB) against the attacks on enforcement directorate teams in Bongaon and Sandeshkhali (coded separately).

On 6 January 2024, BJP members held a protest as part of a state-wide campaign in Hooghly district (coded as Chinsurah city (Hooghly district, WB)) against the attacks on enforcement directorate teams in Bongaon and Sandeshkhali (coded separately).

On 6 January 2024, BJP members held a protest as part of a state-wide campaign in Birbhum district (coded as Suri city (Birbhum district, WB)) against the attacks on enforcement directorate teams in Bongaon and Sandeshkhali (coded separately).

On 6 January 2024, BJP members held a protest as part of a state-wide campaign in Purba Bardhaman district (coded as Burdwan city (Purba Bardhaman district, WB)) against the attacks on enforcement directorate teams in Bongaon and Sandeshkhali (coded separately).

On 6 January 2024, BJP members held protests as part of a state-wide campaign at Purulia district (WB) against the attacks on enforcement directorate teams in Bongaon and Sandeshkhali (coded separately).

On 6 January 2024, BJP members held protests as part of a state-wide campaign at Bankura district (WB) against the attacks on enforcement directorate teams in Bongaon and Sandeshkhali (coded separately).
On 6 January 2024, BJP members held a protest march and blocked road for an hour at Jalpaiguri city (WB) against claimed corruption by TMC.

On 6 January 2024, BJP and BJYM members held a protest as part of a state-wide campaign at Kolkata city (WB) against the attacks on enforcement directorate teams in Bongaon and Sandeshkhali (coded separately).

On 6 January 2024, thousands of farmers - some arriving on tractors - gathered under the banner of BKU, led by its District president, and staged a protest in Sisauli town (Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh) over various demands including prevention of stray animal menace, payment of dues from the last year's sugarcane procurement, declaration of sugarcane price (with a hike), and free electricity for irrigation.

On 6 January 2024, farmers under the banner of BKU staged protests at various BKU District headquarters in the western region of the Uttar Pradesh state (coded as Lucknow city) over numerous demands including prevention of stray animal menace, payment of dues from the last year's sugarcane procurement, declaration of sugarcane price (with a hike), and free electricity for irrigation.

Around 6 January 2024 (as reported), members of the Tamil Nadu Farmers Association affiliated with CPI staged a protest in Budalur town (Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to declare Budhalur taluk as drought-hit. The protesters also demanded the INC-led Karnataka state government to release water to the state of Tamil Nadu.

On 6 January 2024, a large group of Anganwadi workers staged a protest on the Anantapur-Bukkaraya Samudram road in Anantapur city (Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for invoking the Essential Services Maintenance Act (ESMA) against the striking Anganwadi workers. The protesters stood behind barricades, displayed placards and raised slogans when the Andhra Pradesh Governor was passing through the area.

On 6 January 2024, members of the Anganwadi Workers and Union members and the CITU launched a relay hunger strike near the Gandhi Statue in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for invoking the Essential Services Maintenance Act (ESMA) against Anganwadi workers who were protesting over a list of demands including an increase in wages. The protesters burned copies of a government order to mark their protest.

On 6 January 2024, Opposition councillors including members of the INC staged a protest at the Kochi Corporation in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the civic administration for not taking measures to contain the pest and mosquito menace in the city. The protesters held swatters and shouted slogans against the administration to mark their protest.

On 6 January 2024, tea workers held a protest by blocking a road at Bagdogra town (Darjeeling district, WB) to demand reopening of a tea garden after it was shut down without the payment of the bonus.

On 6 January 2024, members of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP--SP) led by a former mayor held a protest in Pune city (Maharashtra) demanding the resignation of a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA for slapping an on-duty police constable.
On 6 January 2024, service selection board job candidates held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand restoration of the provision of preparing waiting lists for recruitment in government services.

On 6 January 2024, members of the Joint Front of Engineers and Employees staged a brief protest 'day 3' (during lunch hours) outside the State Electricity Board office in Mandi town (Himachal Pradesh) demanding the payment of pending salaries and pensions, and the restoration of the old pension scheme.

On 6 January 2024, members of the Joint Front of Engineers and Employees staged a brief protest 'day 3' (during lunch hours) outside most of the State Electricity Board offices in the Himachal Pradesh state (coded as Shimla city) demanding the payment of pending salaries and pensions, and the restoration of the old pension scheme.

On 6 January 2024, a large number of truck operators and drivers from across the state, including the State chiefs of All-Punjab Truck Ekta and Azad Taxi Union, gathered and staged a protest, raising slogans, along the Sangrur-Patiala Road at the toll plaza next to Kalajhar village (Sangrur, Punjab) demanding the withdrawal of the proposed new penal provisions for hit and run cases in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (the recently passed replacement of the Indian Penal Code, 1870). The nationwide strike called by AIMTC over the same issue concluded on 2 January.

On 6 January 2024, candidates for the Assistant Teacher position (at the Basic Education Department) staged a dharna (sit-in protest), raising slogans, at the Basic Shiksha Adhikari (Basic Education Department) office in Hathras city (Uttar Pradesh) against the state authorities whom the protesters accused of disregarding rules and procedures during the counseling process for Assistant Teacher candidates.

On 6 January 2024, e-rickshaw drivers staged a protest, raising slogans, in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) against the decision of the Municipal Corporation (MC) to issue licenses for e-rickshaw drivers.

On 6 January 2024, students staged a protest on the Narayan college campus in Siwan town (Bihar) against an assistant professor for demanding a 'separate homeland' for Indian Muslims in his social media post.

On 6 January 2024, autorickshaw drivers affiliated to the Karnataka Chalakara Okkuta (Karnataka Drivers Union) staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding the administration to increase their permit to operate up to 25-30 km to cover tourist spots around the city. The protesters also demanded the authorities to stop the practice of transferring autorickshaw permits from other places including cities outside Karnataka to Mysuru.

On 6 January 2024, members of various communities including the Ursu Mandali Sangh (community associated to the royal family of the Mysore Wodeyars) and the Devaraja Vanivilas Market Traders Association under the aegis of the Kanoonau Baahira Prathime Teravu Horata Samith (Kanoonak Bahira Statue Removal Struggle Forum) took out a protest march from the main entrance gate of the Dasara exhibition grounds to the office of the Deputy Commissioner in Siddarthanagar in Mysuru city (Karnataka) against the decision to install a statue of a late Hindu seer at the Gun House Circle over the proposal of the royal family of Mysure to install the statue of a late ruler. The protesters held placards to mark their protest.
On 6 January 2024, police pensioners held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) over pay anomalies and claimed discrimination with retired personnel.

On 6 January 2024, lawyers staged a protest in Vaniyambadi town (Tirupathur, Tamil Nadu) demanding a Combined Court Complex in the town since the Judicial Magistrate Court, Subordinate Court and District Munisf Courts were located in three different parts of town which were causing for lawyers and the court staff.

On 6 January 2024, thousands of tribals armed with traditional weapons gathered and held aam sabha/gram sabha (traditional rural self-rule body) at Hulasdangal village under Shikaripara block (Dumka, Jharkhand) against the administrative move of removing chudka (a traditional method of imposing restrictions on any kind of activities on a particular area proclaimed by the gram sabha) proposed coal rake point at Pagdaha.

On 6 January 2024, farmers gathered under the banner of SKM and 18 other farmer unions, including BKU, and staged a 'Mahapanchayat' (large meeting) and a protest, raising slogans, in Barnala city (Punjab) over various demands including the implementation of the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops and the Swaminathan Commission report, and justice for the victims of the violence at Lakhimpur Kheri on 3 October 2021 (coded separately).

On 6 January 2024, students, activists, professors and journalists staged a protest in Hyderabad city (Telangana) in solidarity with the people of Palestine amidst the ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestine. They condemned the killing of thousands of Palestinian children and noted the lack of solidarity events and protests in India. The protesters also recited poetry to show their solidarity.

On 6 January 2024, workers from TMC held a protest amidst a (suspected unofficial) 12 hours shutdown call by TMC at Sarberia town (South 24 Parganas district, WB) against the enforcement directorate over raid in Sandeshkhali against a TMC leader claiming BJP orchestrated it deliberately.

On 6 January 2024, members of Bajrang Dal and VHP staged a protest, raising slogans, along the road at the Ghunghru Mod (turn) Bazaar area in Jalesar town (Etah, Uttar Pradesh) against the beating of cows in the area carried out by unidentified assailants.

On 6 January 2024, family members of the deceased, joined by a BSP leader, staged a protest 'day 2' and refused to cremate the deceased's body at the General Hospital in Hisar city (Haryana) demanding action against the accused involved in the suicide of a man. The police registered charges against 6 accused - including a Deputy superintendent of police. Protesters were detained.

On 6 January 2024, locals staged protests near the Mango Range in Pandalur town (The Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu) against the forest officials after a leopard killed two persons including a child. The protesters demanded the officials to capture and kill the animal. The police resorted to a mild lathi (baton) charge to disperse the protesters.

On 6 January 2024, members held a Hindu Jan Akrosh Morcha, a demonstration march, under the aegis of Sakal Hindu Samaj and BJP, and threw stones at shops in Solapur city (Maharashtra) against 'land jihad (is a way to force Hindus to sell off their lands),' 'love jihad,'(religious conversion through a relationship/marriage) and 'gau hatya,' (cow slaughter) and the central Waqf Board Act. Two shopkeepers were injured. Two BJP MLAs gave inflammatory speech.

On 6 January 2024, members of the Morigaon Sambadik Samaj, All Assam Students' Union (AASU) and Garia-Moria Parishad staged a protest at Bihutoli ground in Morigaon town (Morigaon, Assam) against the DC for his suspected assault and misbehaviour towards a journalist.

On 6 January 2024, a group of workers under MNREGA staged a protest in Aralia Gram Panchayat (coded to Bishalgarh town, Sepahijala, Tripura) against some officials for misusing funds and attendance records.

On 6 January 2024, suspected group of Bangladeshi mobs assaulted two locals from Meghalaya who were working at a betel nut plantation at Lumsoski village (East Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya) over unknown reasons. One of the locals died while the other managed to escape.

On 6 January 2024, over hundred scribes, members of the Nagaon Press Club and other organizations staged a sit in protest near the DC office in Nagaon town (Nagaon, Assam) against the DC for his suspected assault and misbehaviour towards a journalist. Protesters demanded an immediate probe into the incident.

On 6 January 2024, farmers from Yadgir, Raichur, Bagalkot, Kalaburagi and surrounding areas staged a protest in front of the Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam Ltd (KBJNL) office at Bhimarayanagudi town (Yadgir, Karnataka) demanding the INC-led state government to release water from two Krishna reservoirs to save the chilli crops in four North Karnataka districts. The protesters also dug up graves outside the office and sat inside them to mark their protest.

The protesters demanded its withdrawal burned copies of the act to mark their protest during the Bhogi (harvest) festival celebrations.

On 14 January 2024, members of the INC staged a protest in Shimoga city (Shivamogga, Karnataka) against a BJP MP for his provocative comments about mosques and derogatory comments about the Karnataka Chief Minister. The protesters demanded legal action against the MP and burned his effigy to mark their protest.

On 14 January 2024, members of the INC staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Hassan city (Karnataka) against a BJP MP for his provocative comments about mosques and derogatory comments about the Karnataka Chief Minister. The protesters demanded legal action against the MP.

On 14 January 2024, members of the INC including an MLA staged a protest in Arasikere city (Hassan, Karnataka) against a BJP MP for his provocative comments about mosques and derogatory comments about the Karnataka Chief Minister. The protesters demanded legal action against the MP.

On 14 January 2024, members of the INC including an MLA and members of the Karnataka Backward Classes Awareness Forum staged separate protests in Mysuru city (Karnataka) against a BJP MP for his provocative comments about mosques and derogatory comments about the Karnataka Chief Minister. The protesters demanded legal action against the MP and shouted slogans to mark their protest.

On 14 January 2024, members of the TDP staged a protest at the Gandhinagar circle in Dharmavaram town (Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for the price increase of commodities, the high rate of unemployment and other issues in the state. The protesters also celebrated the Bhogi (harvest) festival, shouted slogans and burned copies of government orders and the First Information Report (FIR) against the TDP president to mark their protest.

On 14 January 2024, members of the TDP including a former minister staged a protest in Anantapur city (Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for the price increase of commodities, the high rate of unemployment and other issues in the state.

On 14 January 2024, members of the TDP including a former Chief Minister and members of the JSP staged a protest in Mandadam village (Guntur, Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for the price increase of commodities, the high rate of unemployment and other issues in the state. The protesters also celebrated the Bhogi (harvest) festival and burned placards to mark their protest.

On 14 January 2024, a mob consisting of traders and locals assaulted and killed 2 men and injured 2 others in Tetaria Mor market under Nabinagar police station (Aurangabad, Bihar) after the accidental death of a local man. The fight started when the occupants of a parked car fired at a local man who went to request them to move their car. The bullet missed its intended target and ended up killing another local bystander. On 16 January, 1 more person succumbed to his injuries in the hospital.

On 14 January 2024, a local man (likely Muslim since source specified the man belonged to the minority community) and his associates assaulted and killed a BKU leader, with bricks and stones, at Netua Grameen area's Champapurwa locality in Kanpur city (Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) in a suspected attempt to extort money while the BKU leader was collecting donations for a Hindu religious occasion. The family members of the deceased claimed that the assault was carried out in retaliation to the BKU leader raising Hindu religious slogans - the police have however denied this claim.

Around 14 January 2024 (as reported), locals staged a road blockade on national highway 37 in Kaziranga National Park (Golaghat, Assam) and protested against a forest department official's assault on a local resident.

On 14 January 2024, overnight, All Tai Khamti Singpho Youths clashed with Adivasi Youths of Namsai in Namsai town (Namsai, Arunachal Pradesh) using sharp weapons like machete and guns over a personal dispute that started between two people from the respective communities. The feud turned into a communal clash that injured over 15 people and damaged several vehicles. A curfew was immediately announced after the event.

On 14 January 2024, three upper caste men abused and assaulted a 17-year-old Dalit boy in Chandlodia locality of Ahmedabad city (Ahmadabad, Gujarat) for moving around in the lane of an upper caste neighborhood.

On 14 January 2024, relatives attacked and critically injured three persons including two women with a wooden plank at Motabadi village within Buguda police limits (Ganjam district, Odisha) on suspicion of practicing sorcery.

On 14 January 2024, a group of young people assaulted a young man from the Dalit community near the Kanausa area in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) over a dispute that took place during a cricket match. Assailants are suspected of urinating on the young man - the police have denied the claim. A similar assault was carried out on 13 January at the Khurram Nagar area (coded separately).
On 14 January 2024, Karamchari Sangh affiliated with BMS held a huge protest at Port Blair city (South Andaman district, A&NI) to demand regularization.

On 14 January 2024, local people (likely from the Hindu community based on the issue - which involves a Hindu temple) staged a protest near Dadh village (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) demanding action against officials from the Forest Department for removing solar lights from the roads leading to an ancient Hindu temple.

On 14 January 2024, AAP members held a protest march as part of 7-day 'Badlav Yatra' (transformation march) from Akhnoor to Khour (coded as Khour city, Jammu district, J&K) against the BJP-led central government over demonetization, proposed agricultural laws, claimed crony capitalism and control of constitutional agencies among other issues.

On 14 January 2024, locals held a protest at Bomal village (Jammu district, J&K) over use of low quality material in construction of Sohal-Sangrampur road and demanded an investigation into the contractor's work.
On 14 January 2024, environmental activists staged a protest near Dholewal Chowk in Ludhiana city (Punjab) over various issues including the rise in pollution, and drop in air quality.

On 14 January 2024, passengers staged a protest at Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport in Amritsar city (Punjab) against Air India whom the protesters accused of giving false information regarding the departure time of the flight.

On 14 January 2024, the former North Truck Union President and his associates went on a fast-unto-death strike and staged a sit-in protest near the Deputy Commissioner's (DC) in Jalandhar city (Punjab) demanding the withdrawal of the proposed new penal provisions for hit-and-run cases in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (the recently passed replacement of the Indian Penal Code, 1870).

On 14 January 2024, hundreds of local people, including family members of the deceased, staged a protest near a hospital in Asaura village (Hapur, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a young man whose bike collided with another bike along the Meerut Road.

On 14 January 2024, family members of the deceased and local people (likely from the Hindu community, based issue - which is over the killing a man while collecting donations for a Hindu religious occasion) staged a protest along the Naveen Ganga bridge in Kanpur city (Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused involved in the assault and death of a man at Champapurwa locality on 14 January (coded separately).
On 14 January 2024, INC members held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) against the TMC-led state government over claimed corruption and deterioration in the health services being provided in the state.

On 14 January 2024, TMC members held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) against the BJP-led central government over claimed misuse of central agencies like central bureau of investigation and enforcement directorate and denial of central funds to the state for central sponsored schemes.

actor2: Military Forces of India (2014-) Jat Regiment
text: On 14 January 2024, local women (likely Meitei based on geography and action) staged a protest at Sabungkhok village (Imphal East, Manipur) demanding the replacement of Jat Regiment (military) with state police forces in Sabungkhok village over their perceived inefficiency of military forces when their village was attacked (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. 8-11 women were injured after Jat Regiment forces used physical force to disperse the crowd.

On 14 January 2024, farmers, members of the AP Rythu Sangham (farmers group), the TDP and the CPI staged protests in front of bonfires in Kairuppala Muthukuru, Puppala Doddi and Thuruvagallu villages in Aspari mandal (coded to Aspari village, Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh) against the Land Titling Act introduced by the YSRCP-led government. The protesters also burned the copies of the law while celebrating the Bhogi festival (harvest festival) to mark their protest.

On 14 January 2024, farmers, members of the AP Rythu Sangham (farmers' group), the TDP and the CPI staged protests in front of bonfires in Billekallu village in Apsari mandal (Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh) against the Land Titling Act introduced by the YSRCP-led government. The protesters also burned the copies of the law while celebrating the Bhogi festival (harvest festival) to mark their protest.

On 14 January 2024, farmers, members of the AP Rythu Sangham (farmers' group), the TDP and the CPI staged protests in front of bonfires in Yatakallu village in Apsari mandal (Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh) against the Land Titling Act introduced by the YSRCP-led government. The protesters also burned the copies of the law while celebrating the Bhogi festival (harvest festival) to mark their protest.

On 14 January 2024, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), a protest march, reached Mau city (Uttar Pradesh) where they blamed the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The Yatra which entered 'day 36' on 10 December 2023 began in Bengaluru city under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization). The yatra is scheduled to conclude in New Delhi on 3 March 2024 - likely to pass through 80 districts across 13 states.

On 15 January 2024, members of the Valasa Adivasulu Samakya (Adivasi group) staged a protest in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the Governor to direct the INC-led state government to correct a mistake in the spelling of the Gutti Koya tribe in the Schedule of Telangana for Tribals due to which the group were being denied the benefits that they were supposed to receive from the state. The protesters said that the correction of the spelling and the issuance of a caste certificate would help the tribal group to access educational opportunities and other benefits.

On 15 January 2024, members of the IYC staged continued to stage protests across Kerala state (coded to Thiruvananthapuram) against the arrest of the IYC state president for staging a protest against the LDF-led state government's Nava Kerala Sadas (public outreach program) on 20 December 2023.

On 15 January 2024, members of the IYC staged a demonstration at the Collectorate in Alappuzha city (Kerala) against the arrest of the IYC state president for a prior demonstration against the LDF-led state government's Nava Kerala Sadas (public outreach program) on 20 December 2023. The demonstrators resorted to stone pelting and the police fired water cannons and lathi (baton) charge to disperse them. The police also beat up the demonstrators. Both IYC demonstrators including women and police personnel were injured.

On 15 January 2024, contractual employees of Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant in Bhadravathi along with their families staged a protest in front of the residence an MP in Shimoga city (Shivamogga, Karnataka) demanding the reopening of the plant so that they could get their jobs back.
On 15 January 2024, SFI and KSU students clashed with each other at the Maharaja's College in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) after one group accused another group of bullying.

On 15 January 2024, members of the IYC took out a protest march to the office of the Kanhangad RDO in Kanhangad town (Kasaragod, Kerala) against the arrest of the IYC state president for staging a protest against the LDF-led state government's Nava Kerala Sadas (public outreach program) on 20 December 2023. The police fired water cannons when the protesters attempted to climb over the barricades set up by the police.

On 15 January 2024, residents of Khola staged a protest in Canacona city (South Goa, Goa) against a proposal to set up a fish meal plant in the village. The protesters said that the functioning of the plan would affect the water and environment in the region.
Around 15 January 2024 (as reported), residents staged a protest in Patiem village (South Goa, Goa) against a proposal to set up a fish meal plant in the village.

On 15 January 2024, local residents (likely Kuki based on geography and action) staged a huge demonstration at Moreh police station and the commando complex in Moreh town (Tengnoupal, India) demanding the unconditional release of the 2 arrested Kuki men (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state. Demonstrators attempted to storm the police station to free the arrested individuals and clashed with police forces including Assam Rifles who fired tear gas and mock bombs to disperse the demonstrators. 1 woman injured.

Around 15 January 2024 (as reported), local Adivasis staged a protest and blocked national highway 15 (coded to Namsai town, Namsai, Arunachal Pradesh) demanding authorities for the prompt arrest of attackers during the clash between All Tai Khamti Singpho Youths clashed with Adivasi Youths of Namsai (coded separately). Protesters also demanded medical compensation for the injured.

Around 15 January 2024 (as reported), local people (flat owners) staged a protest, raising slogans, at Sector 63 in Chandigarh city against the Resident Welfare Association (RWA) whom the protesters accused of unilaterally installing biometric and card-operated lift access at the Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) flats without consulting the CHB.

On 15 January 2024, members of the INC engaged in an altercation with Hindu devotees, who also tore the INC flag and raised religious slogans, at Ram Mandir (Hindu temple under construction) in Ayodhya city (Uttar Pradesh) over a dispute regarding the waving of the INC flag by INC members outside the temple - the inauguration of the Ram Mandir has been led by the BJP party.

On 15 January 2024, displaced locals living near Silsako lake staged a protest using placards and burned a traditional bonfire in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) against the state government for the forced eviction of residents living around Silsako lake. Protesters also demanded compensation and rehabilitation.

On 15 January 2024, members of INC, during a 12-hour bandh (shutdown strike), blocked the National Highway-49 at Nilabenisahi village (coded as Deogarh, Odisha) over irregularities at paddy mandis and anti-farmer policies of the state government.
On 15 January 2024, MSJK members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against Pakistan and demanded that India take military action to control of Pakistan administered Kashmir.
On 15 January 2024, locals led by Shiv Sena Hindustan members held a protest at Bishnah city (Jammu district, J&K) over the poor condition of a road and demanded its repair.
On 15 January 2024, residents held a protest at Watergam town (Baramulla district, J&K) against the power department over inflated power bills.
On 15 January 2024, locals held a protest at Domana city (Jammu district, J&K) against the installation of smart power meters claiming they lead to inflated power bills.

On 15 January 2024, over 4,000 guest teachers gathered at the agricultural produce market and held a parade with bowls in their hands to beg in Barwani town (Madhya Pradesh) to protest against the non-payment of their last six months' salaries. After the parade, the guest teachers reached the collectorate and submitted a memorandum.

On 15 January 2024, large number of people held a candle march and set alight a bonfire of Chinese kite string as a mark of protest in Dhar city (Madhya Pradesh) after the death of a 7-year-old child from Chinese string.

On 15 January 2024, women from Lamlai constituency (likely Meitei due to action) blocked the Imphal-Ukhrul road (coded to Lamlai town, Imphal East, Manipur) as a protest against the dispute that occurred between Jat Regiment and protesting local women that resulted in injuries of the women (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 15 January 2024, members of labor unions gathered under the banner of Punjab Pradesh Palledar Mazdoor Union and staged a protest rally, raising slogans, along the Sangrur-Patiala highway and near the Chief Minister's residence in Sangrur city (Punjab) demanding the establishment of a labor board, work guarantee, fixed wage rates, and the removal of the contractual system in food grain procurement agencies.

On 15 January 2024, members of the Bilaspur District Truck Operators Co-op Transport Society staged a dharna (sit-in protest) along the Kiratpur Sahib-Una National Highway near Kiratpur Sahib town (Rupnagar, Punjab) against the Kiratpur Sahib Truck Operators Society (Dehni) over a dispute regarding the loading of materials.
On 15 January 2024, relatives of a murdered man held a protest in Shahpura town (Jaipur, Rajasthan) and demanded compensation for the family.

On 15 January 2024, family members of the deceased and local people staged a protest 'day 2', raising slogans and carrying Hindu religious flags, along the Naveen Ganga bridge in Kanpur city (Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused involved in the assault and death of a man at Champapurwa locality on 14 January (coded separately).

On 15 January 2024, members of the Mool Nivas Bhu Kanoon Samanvay Sangharsh Committee (Original Residence Land Law Coordinating Committee) staged a protest by burning a copy of the Land Law Ordinance and dropping copies of permanent residency certificates in the Saryu River in Bageshwar town (Uttarakhand) over various demands including the designation of Gairsain as Uttarakhand's permanent capital, better employment opportunities, and protection of native residence.

On 15 January 2024, members of INC, led by the former Chief Minister (INC) and the INC Leader of Opposition, staged a protest during a 'Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra' (an INC campaign) rally from Hathibadakala to Gandhi Park in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) demanding action the accused involved in the murder of a woman in September 2022. The protesters also accused the BJP-led state government of shielding the accused.
On 15 January 2024, locals vandalized the fire tender involved in a fatal accident and blocked the road in Patna city (Bihar), during a demonstration, demanding the arrest of the driver.

On 15 January 2024, sanitation workers staged an indefinite sit-in protest at Burari Hospital in the Delhi - Burari area (Central Delhi, Delhi) against the hospital administration whom the protesters accused of caste discrimination, sexual harassment, and violation of labor rights.

On 15 January 2024, a group of youths verbally and physically assaulted a doctor from Margherita Civil hospital in Margherita town (Tinsukia, Assam) over unavailability of rabies vaccination. 3 people were arrested the next day over the assault.

On 15 January 2024, members of the AI Welfare Workers Union staged a protest outside the Mini Secretariat in Loharu city (Bhiwani, Haryana) demanding employment as Animal Attendants under the Haryana Skill Employment Corporation.

Around 15 January 2024 (month of), farmers staged a protest in Sehsaula village (Nuh, Haryana) against the non-payment of compensation to farmers for the construction of a tunnel (for a railway corridor project) on the farmers' agricultural land.

Around 15 January 2024 (as reported), panchayat members belonging to the LDF clashed with forest officials in Mankulam village (Idukki, Kerala) over the construction of a pavilion inside the Perumpankuthu river.

On 15 January 2024, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), a protest march, reached Ghazipur city (Uttar Pradesh) where they blamed the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The Yatra which entered 'day 37' on 10 December 2023 began in Bengaluru city under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization). The yatra is scheduled to conclude in New Delhi on 3 March 2024 - likely to pass through 80 districts across 13 states.

Around 15 January 2024 (month of), over 100 students of the CCMA Government Girls' Higher Secondary School staged a protest on the school premises in Coimbatore city (Tamil Nadu) demanding basic toilet facilities at the school.

On 15 January 2024, Kuki-Zomi women staged a protest at the Additional Deputy Commissioner's office complex at Chikim Veng (locality) in Moreh town (Tengnoupal, Manipur) against the suspected attempt made by armed Meitei assailants and police personnel to occupy the office, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Manipur police commandos opened fire at the protesters, injuring one woman.

On 16 January 2024, members of Hindu right wing groups assaulted a Muslim man in Dharwad city (Hubballi, Karnataka) after accusing the man of taking the phone numbers of Hindu girls and women visiting the shop where he worked, in order to video call and blackmail them later their photos. Police arrived at the area and questioned the man and took the rioters into custody.

On 16 January 2024, members of the CPI(M) including a former minister under the aegis of the Kerala Private School Management Association staged a protest in Alappuzha city (Kerala) against a literary writer for criticising power politics and personality cults during a literature festival.

On 16 January 2024, as many as 500 beneficiaries of the Dalit Bandhu scheme (social scheme for Dalits) staged a protest in front of the INC office in Huzurabad town (Karimnagar, Telangana) after the freezing of their bank accounts. The protesters demanded the INC-led state government to help resolve their issues.

On 16 January 2024, more than 50 members of the Mysuru farmers' association staged a protest at the Karnataka Gramin Bank in Krishnarajanagara town (Mysuru, Karnataka) against the bank for auctioning of a farmer's house despite the farmer having repaid his loan. The protesters accused the bank of seizing the property in an illegal manner.

On 16 January 2024, sugarcane cultivators in Thirumandangudi and the surrounding areas in Papanasam taluk staged a protest at the Koonamchery burial ground in front of a Pudukottai-based distillery company in Koonancheri village (Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu) against the proposal to convert a private sugar mill into a distillery by a private company which had acquired the mill through the National Company Law Tribunal proceedings. The protesters completed 410 days of protest and raised slogans against the government. The protesters also said that the a distillery would affect the agricultural prospects of the area.
On 16 January 2024, members of the INC and the IYC staged a demonstration in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the Prime Minister's roadshow. The police detained six protesters.

Around 16 January 2024 (as reported), members of the Tamil Nadu Viviasayigal Sangam (farmer group) affiliated to the Communist Party of India (Marxist) staged a protest in Thirumandangudi village (Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu) against the setting up of a brewery factory in the area. The protesters said that the area was declared as a Protected Agricultural Zone and the setting of a distillery would affect the agricultural prospects of the area which was declared as a Protected Agricultural Zone.

On 16 January 2024, residents including women, farmers, petty traders, students and tribals staged a protest on the Pudur Nadu-Tirupattur town main road in the Arasampattu area in Tirupattur village (Tirupattur, Tamil Nadu) against the Department of State Highways for not taking action against the encroachment of the narrow road. The protesters also condemned the denial of access to the road and demanded action against three men who assaulted a man who complained against the encroachment (coded separately).

Around 16 January 2024 (as reported), Hindu organisations staged a protest in Krishnarajpet town (Mandya, Karnataka) after a Muslim man eloped with a minor Hindu girl. The protesters said that it was a case of 'love jihad' and demanded that the investigation be handed over to the National Investigation Agency (NIA).

On 16 January 2024, members of Hindu groups staged a protest in Bhatkal town (Uttara Kannada, Karnataka) after taluk (government) officials stopped them from repainting a 'Devanagari' signboard and removed a flag pole that was being installed near the board. The protesters said that the government officials were acting on a complaint by a mosque that was located nearby.

Around 16 January 2024 (as reported), members of the INC including an MLA staged a protest in Killiyoor town (Kanniyakumari, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government's proposal to merge a few village panchayats in the constituency with the nearby town panchayats.

On 16 January 2024, members of the INC and the IYC staged a protest in front of a police station in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) after six members of INC and the IYC were arrested by the police for staging a protest against the Prime Minister's roadshow in the city (coded separately).

On 16 January 2024, an independent legislator along with other staged a protest near the Tourism Department office in Puducherry city (Puducherry) after two people drowned in the sea. The protesters condemned the increasing incidents of drowning and demanded the department to deploy lifeguards and take other measures to stop the accidents.
On 16 January 2024, parents staged a protest outside the Little Flower School in Thane city (Maharashtra) after the school denied exam entry to 350 students over unpaid fees.

On 16 January 2024, a village Pradhan (chief) and his family members assaulted and pushed a farmer to his death - in Adari village (Jaunpur, Uttar Pradesh) over a minor dispute regarding the laying of pipes.

On 16 January 2024, IDPs (likely Meitei based on action) and the Khwairamband Ima Keithel Joint Co-ordinating Committee (KIKJCC) organized separate protests within in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding capital punishment for the 2 Kuki men who were arrested (coded separately) for the murder of a Meitei SPDO in Moreh (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters also demanded authorities to send state forces as reinforcement in Moreh to drive out armed Kuki assailants.

On 16 January 2024, a mob of locals vandalized the residence of a man and destroyed his car along with a part of his house at Jamalpur area in Dholai village (Cachar, Assam) over suspicions of the murder of another local. Locals claimed that the suspected man and 20 of his friends attacked 3 locals over a long standing rivalry and one of them was killed.

On 16 January 2024, a large number of BJP members and councilors clashed with members and councilors of INC and AAP, including the Chandigarh INC President and Chandigarh AAP co-in charge, at the Municipal Council (MC) office in Chandigarh city after the INC-AAP members rose in opposition to the BJP members attempt to take an INC councilor (Mayor candidate) away from the MC office who had come to withdraw this nomination.

On 16 January 2024, some people (likely from the Muslim community as the report indicates that they belonged to a minority group) assaulted and pelted stones at people from the Dalit community, including their shops, at the Gonchhi area in Faridabad city (Haryana) in a suspected case of retaliation against the members of the Dalit community for organizing a religious (likely Hindu, since Dalit people are predominantly Hindus) function. The assailants are accused of hurling castiest slurs.
On 16 January 2024, 8-10 people assaulted local shopkeepers with hockey sticks, sticks, and the butt of a pistol, and vandalized their shops, in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) for unidentified reasons.

On 16 January 2024, villagers under the aegis of Chhattisgarh Kisan Sabha (an AIKS affiliate) and Bhoo-visthapit Rojgar Ekta Sangh (united front for employment for the displaced) held a sit-in-protest at the South Eastern Coalfields' GM office in Kusmunda town (Korba, Chhattisgarh), demanding resolution of pending employment cases.

On 16 January 2024, hundreds of cow servants (Gau Rakshaks) staged a protest at the National Gaushala (Cow shelter) in Dharoli village (Jind, Haryana) against the manager of the cow shelter whom the protesters accused of turning the shelter into a slaughterhouse house after videos of scattered skins and skeletons of cows were circulated online.

On 16 January 2024, unemployed young people gathered, including members of ABVP, under the banner of various student outfits and staged a protest outside the Deputy Commissioner's (DC) office in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) against the state government's decision to recruit guest teachers.

On 16 January 2024, unemployed young people gathered under the banner of various student outfits and staged a protest outside the Deputy Commissioner's (DC) office in Solan city (Himachal Pradesh) against the state government's decision to recruit guest teachers.

On 16 January 2024, unemployed young people, including graduate and postgraduate degree holders in Education, gathered under the banner of various student outfits and staged a protest, raising slogans, outside the Deputy Commissioner's (DC) office in Dharamsala town (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) against the state government's decision to recruit guest teachers.

On 16 January 2024, local people and the Pradhan (village chief) of Batthan panchayat staged a protest in Thural village (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) against illegal mining in the Neugal River despite repeated complaints. The protesters accused the Mining and Forest departments of colluding with the illegal miners.
On 16 January 2024, AAP members held a protest at Hiranagar city (Kathua district, J&K) against the power department over frequent power cuts in the area.
On 16 January 2024, women led by a former panch (village government head) held a protest at Kulwanta town (Udhampur district, J&K) over lack of water supply in the area for two months.

On 16 January 2024, locals held a protest by blocking a road at Draba town (Poonch district, J&K) against Dharam Raj Construction (DRC) company for cutting work adjacent to the residential houses that may damage their houses.
On 16 January 2024, family members of a deceased person held a protest by blocking a road at Rajouri city (J&K) over the death of a person in a road accident and demanded justice.

On 16 January 2024, hundreds of farmers staged a protest at a collectorate in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) over their demands to increase compensation for their lands marked for acquisition for the Indore-Budhni railway line and outer ring road.

On 16 January 2024, locals blocked Tiddim road in Kwakta town (Bishnupur, Manipur) as a protest against the abduction and assault of 3 Meite-Pangal men (coded separately). Protesters lifted the blockade when they received the information that they were released.

On 16 January 2024, dozens of locals including Sugnu Apunba Meira Paibi Lup (women torch bearers, likely Meitei based on action) staged a protest at Sugnu market in Sugnu town (Kakching, Manipur) demanding capital punishment for the 2 Kuki men who were arrested (coded separately) for the murder of a Meitei SPDO in Moreh (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. All shops and business establishments were closed during the protest. Protesters also condemned the protests by the Kuki community for the release of the arrested men.

On 16 January 2024, members of Kuki Inpi Tengnoupal (KIT), Kuki Students' Organisation (KSO) and Kuki Women Union (KWU) Tengnoupal organized a sit in protest at Tengnoupal market in Tengnoupal town (Tengnoupal, Manipur) against the arrest of 2 Kuki men (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.
On 16 January 2024, locals detained a Mo Bus at Barang town (Cuttack, Odisha) during a protest after the bus hit a private car. Police reached the spot and pacified the protesters.

On 16 January 2024, members of the Computer Teachers Union staged a 'Mukh Mantri Bhal Yatra' (Chief Minister's Procession) protest march from Tarn Taran city to Goindwal Sahib town (Tarn Taran, Punjab) against the failure of the state government to fulfill their demands including the release of annual proficiency scheme (ACP), and the implementation of the recommendations as stated within the sixth pay commission.

On 16 January 2024, members and leaders of INC including the INC state president (MLA) and the INC Leader of Opposition staged a massive protest in Kharar town (SAS Nagar, Punjab) against the AAP-led state government whom the protesters accused of failing to maintain law and order in the state.
