On 18 January 2024, members of the Mysuru district truckers' association staged a protest by forming a human chain near Hullahalli village (Mysuru, Karnataka) as part of a state-wide strike against the proposed new penal provisions for hit and run cases in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (the recently passed replacement of the Indian Penal Code, 1870).

On 18 January 2024, members of the Telangana Gig and Platform Workers' Union staged a protest in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against aggregator companies running taxi services to passengers on private two wheelers. The protesters said that the practice was illegal and demanded the government to take action. The protesters also submitted a representation to the transport department.

On 18 January 2024, scores of autorickshaw and truck drivers and owners affiliated to the North Karnataka Autorickshaw Drivers Association, Association of Karnataka Mini Goods Drivers, Hubballi, Transport and Lorry owners Association and the Dharwad District Goods Shed Owners Association took out a protest march from the Durgad Bail to the Mini Vidhana Soudha in Hubballi city (Dharwad, Karnataka) in response to a nationwide call by the Lorry Owners Association against the proposed new penal provisions for hit and run cases in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (the recently passed replacement of the Indian Penal Code, 1870).

On 18 January 2024, members of the SFI staged a black flag protest in Cheppad village (Alappuzha, Kerala) against the Kerala Governor when he was on his way to Oachira in Kollam to attend a programme. The police arrested 15 protesters from three locations in connection with the protest.

On 18 January 2024, members of the SFI staged a black flag protest at the ONK Junction, and MSM College Junction in Kayamkulam town (Alappuzha, Kerala) against the Kerala Governor when he was on his way to Oachira in Kollam to attend a programme. The police arrested 15 protesters from three locations in connection with the protest.

On 18 January 2024, members of various civil society organisations including the Domestic Workers Rights Women staged a protest at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) demanding the BJP-led Gujarat state government to arrest the convicts who were accused of raping a woman and killing her family members in 2022. The protesters demanded the government to put them back in jail as per the order of the Indian Supreme Court.

On 18 January 2024, the residents of Thalakundah staged a protest on the Ooty-Gudalur road and the Ooty-Masinagudi road in Udhagamandalam town (The Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu) demanding action against a man who was accused of sexually assaulting a minor. The protesters demanded that the accused be charged under the Goondas Act.

On 18 January 2024, scores of TDP and JSP members staged protests in Gudivada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for not allowing them to commemorate the 28th death anniversary of a former Chief Minister. The police imposed prohibitory orders and stopped the protesters using barricades in many places. More than 50 TDP and 20 JSP protesters were detained by the police.

On 18 January 2024, residents of Sujatha Nagar staged a protest in Kavali town (Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore, Andhra Pradesh) against the encroachment on a graveyard in the area. The protesters demanded the MLA and other government officials to intervene.

On 18 January 2024, members of the Malamahanadu Telangana (social organization) staged a protest at the BR Ambedkar statue at Tank Bund in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against the INC-led state government's decision to not let an INC leader contest in the upcoming Members of a State Legislative Council (MLC) elections. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest and demanded the Chief Minister to offer a good position to the INC leader.

On 18 January 2024, villagers staged a demonstration in Veliminedu village (Nalgonda, Telangana) against a public hearing proposed by the Pollution Control Board and Forest Department on the expansion of the a private company called the MPL Steel Industries in the village. The demonstrators said that the company was causing pollution in the area and removed tents that were set up by the company for the public hearing. The police used mild force to disperse the protesters.

On 18 January 2024, a former Congress leader along with hundreds of INC activists staged a protest in Amguri town (Kokrajhar, Assam) seeking justice for her removal from the Congress party. This protest was staged amidst the ongoing Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra. Congress party cancelled their rally plans in Amguri town as a result which angered locals who were anticipating arrival of Rahul Gandhi.

On 18 January 2024, several students held a demonstration and forced their way into a university premises at Cooch Behar city (WB) over claimed financial irregularities by the university. The students entered the university's storage room and removed gym equipment.

Around 18 January 2024 (as reported), women protesters dressed in traditional mourning outfits and blocked the road to Imphal airport in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) in solidarity with police forces who were killed and injured in Moreh (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 18 January 2024, a mob of 100-150 members attacked a forest range officer and his team within the Chirang forest division (coded to Chirang town, Chirang, Assam) during an anti-encroachment drive. The forest range officer and three of his staffs sustained injuries.

On 18 January 2024, unidentified armed assailants pretending to be policemen assaulted a dozen students at a farmhouse at the Hasanpur area in Gurgaon city (Gurugram, Haryana) in a suspected case of group rivalry. The police suspect that a Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE) paper leak racket was underway at the farmhouse. 6 accused were arrested for the assault, and 12 students and a teacher were detained over suspicions of involvement in a paper leak racket.
On 18 January 2024, a mob assaulted a 'drunk' ambulance driver in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) after the driver mowed down six pedestrians injuring them.

On 18 January 2024, two groups clashed with stones, sticks, and sharp objects in Nemawar village under Khudel tehsil (Indore, Madhya Pradesh) over a land dispute. Six persons were seriously injured in the cash.

On 18 January 2024, a former sarpanch and supporters assaulted the incumbent woman Sarpanch (the head of local government body) and her husband in Chasakhanda panchayat (Jajapur district, Odisha) over an ongoing political rivalry. The incumbent Sarpanch and her husband are admitted to the district hospital.

On 18 January 2024, unidentified persons suspected to be linked to BJD threw stones and damaged the vehicle of Odisha state BJP secretary at Brajarajnagar city (Jharsuguda district, Odisha) over political rivalry. The vehicle was parked in a garage and there was nobody in the vehicle. No one was injured.

On 18 January 2024, family members of the rape accused pelted stones at a police team (on duty) in Machhlishahr town (Jaunpur, Uttar Pradesh) when the police arrived in the area to arrest the accused. 2 policemen were injured.

On 18 January 2024, INC and AAP municipal councilors, including a former INC state minister, staged a protest, raising slogans, outside the Municipal Corporation (MC) office in Chandigarh city against the BJP-led central government for delaying the Mayoral elections. The protesters were prevented from entering the MC office.

On 18 January 2024, members of the Petroleum Dealers Welfare Association staged a dharna (sit-in protest), raising slogans, at the state-level coordinator (SLC) of the Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) in Panipat city (Haryana) against the non-fulfillment of their long-standing demands for a hike in commission.

On 18 January 2024, members of the Jayati-Jayati Hindu Mahan Sangathan and Gau Seva Dal (cow service groups) staged a protest in Dharoli village (Jind, Haryana) demanding actions against the manager of the cow shelter whom the protesters accused of turning the shelter into a slaughterhouse house after videos of scattered skins and skeletons of cows were circulated online.

On 18 January 2024, local people staged a protest at the Kachehri crossing in Dharamsala town (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) against the state government for failing to deposit money for the transfer of forestland to Central University of Himachal Pradesh (CUHP).

On 18 January 2024, hundreds of junior office assistant (IT) candidates staged a protest, raising slogans, outside the State Secretariat in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) demanding the declaration of the examination (conducted in 2021) results for the posts of junior office assistant (IT).

On 18 January 2024, residents led by a former sarpanch (village government head) held a protest at Mangota town (Rajouri district, J&K) against the authorities over failure to connect a specified transformer despite funds being sanctioned for the same.

On 18 January 2024, a large group of Valmiki community members reached the police station and held a protest in Moghat road in Khandwa city (Khandwa, Madhya Pradesh) demanding immediate action against the teacher for assaulting a student from the community.

On 18 January 2024, thousands of students from Kangpokpi district staged a protest rally organized by Kuki Students' Organization Sadar Hills with placards and slogans from Nute Kailhang to DC office in Kangpokpi town (Kangpokpi, Manipur) against the suspension of 3 Kuki ZEO officials and de-affiliation of 25 schools in Kuki areas amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state. Protesters also submitted a 4 page memorandum to the PM through Kangpokpi DC.

On 18 January 2024, thousands of students from Churachandpur district staged a protest rally organized by the Joint Student Body (JSB) with slogans and placards from Lamka Public Ground till Mini Secretariat in Churachandpur town (Churachandpur, Manipur) against the suspension of 3 Kuki ZEO officials and de-affiliation of 25 schools in Kuki areas amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state. Protesters also submitted a 4 page memorandum to the PM through Churachandpur DC.

On 18 January 2024, a large number of women traders and IDPs staged a rally protest from the main market area to the CM's bungalow and the Raj Bhavan in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) against the increasing violence in the state after 5 Meitei men were killed in different locations (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters also demanded the removal of the chairman of the inter-agency Unified Command. Police fired tear gas shells to disperse the crowd.

On 18 January 2024, thousands of people including Meira Paibi (women torch bearers, likely Meitei based on action) and Youth of Manipur members attempted to stage a protest rally from Moirangkhom locality to CM's residence in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) against the resurgence of violence amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Combined security forces (likely police forces) fired tear gas to disperse the crowd.

On 18 January 2024, hundreds of job aspirants staged a protest in Bhubaneswar city (Khorda, Odisha) over irregularities in junior teacher recruitment conducted by the Odisha School Education Programme Authority (OSEPA).

On 18 January 2024, farmers, led by an SKM leader, staged a protest and parked narma cotton-laden vehicles on the road at the Old city area in Abohar city (Fazilka, Punjab) against the Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) for failing to fulfill its promise of procuring cotton crops from farmers.
On 18 January 2024, some local shopkeepers staged a protest, raising slogans, near Mata Rani Chowk in Jalandhar city (Punjab) against the traffic police for harassing visitors in the market area.

On 18 January 2024, provisionally selected candidates under the aegis of nursing officer and paramedical recruitment Sangharsh Samiti 2023 held a protest outside the State Institute of Health and Family Welfare (SIHFW) in Jaipur city (Rajasthan) demanding appointment to the posts.

On 18 January 2024, hundreds of job aspirants who cleared the TET in 2022 staged a protest at Shiksha Bhawan in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) demanding immediate recruitment of teachers for available posts. Protesters claimed that although 1,615 vacancies were there in TET-I and 1,643 in TET-II, the recruitment process was halted.

On 18 January 2024, family members of the deceased staged a protest and placed the deceased's body along the road at the market area in Bandhwa village (Jaunpur, Uttar Pradesh) against the failure of the police to take action against the Adari village Pradhan (chief) and his family members for assaulting and killing a man (farmer) on 16 January (coded separately).
On 18 January 2024, members of ABVP staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Collectorate in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against illegal coaching centers in the city.

On 18 January 2024, contractual sanitation workers from the Municipal Corporation went on strike and staged a protest at the Ekta Vihar area in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) demanding the payment of pending wages, and better pay and benefits.
On 18 January 2024, more than 300 local people staged a protest at Dumak village under Joshimath Tehsil (Chamoli, Uttarakhand) against the exclusion of Dumak village from a road project.
On 18 January 2024, BJP members including a minister held a protest march at Kolkata city (WB) against the TMC-led state government over an unspecified issue.

On 18 January 2024, around 1000 farmers, led by the Bharatiya Kisan Parishad (BKP) President, staged a march towards, and locked the gates of, the Noida Authority's office at Sector 6 in Noida city (Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) during a demonstration demanding a portion of Abadi developed plots or an equivalent amount in compensation for land acquired by the authority for various projects (since 1997). The demonstrators engaged in a scuffle with the police (likely violent based on injuries) as they tried to overcome the barricades, and 2 people suffered minor injuries.

On 18 January 2024, villagers, including a farmer leader and BJP member, held a protest in Piplia Mandi town (Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh) after the Narcotics Central Bureau (NCB) team confiscated the DVR of the CCTV at the farmer's house.
On 18 January 2024, evicted roadside vendors staged a protest in Puri city (Odisha) demanding their proper rehabilitation.

On 18 January 2024, more than 300 students at IIT Madras staged a protest on the campus in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) over various issues such as the mess fees for the full semester in advance, the burden on Ph.D. and MS students after the introduction of new credit courses, which require them to publish one paper every semester. The Director, dean of planning, and the chairman council of wardens addressed the students. The administration also decided that students would be allowed to pay mess fees in installments.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Indian Reserve Battalion
text: On 18 January 2024, locals from in and around Naransena village (likely Meitei based on action) stormed into the camp of 2nd IRB in Naransena village (Bishnupur, Manipur), demanding weapons to protect themselves while citing inefficiency of police forces amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. This came after the village was attacked by armed Kuki assailants (coded separately). IRB personnel opened fire and 5 people were injured.

On 18 January 2024, women vendors, shopkeepers, locals from Kakching under Kakching Keithel Apunba Ima Lup and Kakching Bazar Business Welfare Association (all likely Meitei based on action) staged a sit in protest at Kakching market in Kakching town (Kakching, Manipur) and put forward demands to the state government amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Demands included immediate deployment of state forces at Moreh, penalty for the 2 arrested Kukis linked to the killings of Meitei SDPO (coded separately) and the removal of Security Advisor of Manipur. A former legislator (BJP) and INC members also joined the protest.

Around 18 January 2024 (as reported), members of the Karni Sena (Hindu group) staged a protest at the Directorate Of Archives And Archaeology in Panaji city (North Goa, Gao) demanding action against illegal structures in Old Goa. The protesters said that there was a temple under the Sancoale Church and demanded an inspection of the church premises.

On 18 January 2024, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization), reached Muzaffarpur district (Bihar) and staged a protest march blaming the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' started from Bengaluru city on 10 December.

On 19 January 2024, members of the BJP took out a protest march to the Memorial at Killikurissimangalam near Ottappalam town (Palakkad, Kerala) against the LDF-led state government for not paying the staff and students of the Kalakkath Kunchan Nambiar Memorial which housed many artefacts and documents about the history and literature of Kerala.

On 19 January 2024, a Dalit prisoner who was arrested for attacking the YSRCP head and current Chief Minister five years ago, and his mother, brother and leaders of various organisations staged a protest by organising a hunger strike in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding the Chief Minister to attend the court hearings pertaining to the criminal case filed after the attack.

On 19 January 2024, contractual employees of Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plan staged a protest in front of the VISL main gate in Bhadravati city (Shivamogga, Karnataka) marking one year of their agitation demanding the BJP-led Union government to reopen the plant.

On 19 January 2024, lawyers under the banner of a Joint Action Committee staged a protest in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to provide security to the Madurai Deputy Mayor who was attacked and whose house was vandalised on 9 January 2024 (coded separately). The protesters also condemned the attack and demanded action against the accused.

On 19 January 2024, several members of the United Teachers' Federation Vizianagaram took out a protest march from the fort to the clock tower junction in Vizianagaram city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding the YSRCP-led state government to release the pending payments related to the provident fund and other claims.

On 19 January 2024, three assailants including a minor physically assaulted and verbally abused a nursing student and her male friend at the Kadri park in Mangaluru city (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) for being together. The assailants questioned the couple of their identities and why they were at the park. The assailants also took photos and videos of the couple.

On 19 January 2024, residents staged a protest in the Vaazhaithottam hamlet in Palakkodu (Dharmapuri, Tamil Nadu) demanding a road under the railway bridge in the area. The protesters erected flexes threatening to boycott the upcoming General Assembly elections if they demand was not fulfilled.

On 19 January 2024, relatives of a youth who died in an accident after his two-wheeler was hit by a truck staged a protest by placing the victim's body on the Trichy-Chennai National Highway (NH) at the Sanjeevi Nagar intersection in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) to demand the construction of a vehicular underpass in the area. The protesters said that two-wheelers heading to nearby villages could use the underpass to travel safety while the main road could be used for bigger vehicles.

Around 19 January 2024 (as reported), the family members of a murdered Bajrang Dal member placed the body and held a protest at the old bus stand in Rajgarh city (Madhya Pradesh), demanding capital punishment for the culprits.

Around 19 January 2024 (as reported), a large number of people, mostly women (likely all Meitei based on protest demands) staged a protest in Ningthoukhong town (Bishnupur, Manipur) demanding justice for the 4 farmers who were killed (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

Around 19 January 2024 (as reported), local people staged a protest, raising slogans, and burned an effigy in Hathras city (Uttar Pradesh) against the Municipal Corporation (MC) whom the protesters accused of failing to construct the Nagla Bhura Road, based on the proposed specifications.

On 19 January 2024, hundreds of AKSU and KPP(U) members jointly held a protest by walking on a railway track near Jaldhaka rail bridge (coded as Jaldhaka town, Jalpaiguri district, WB) against BJP and TMC to demand a separate Kamtapur state and that the BJP-led central government initiate peace talks with KLO.

On 19 January 2024, about 500-700 unemployed young people gathered under the banner of United Unemployed Morcha and staged a protest march, raising slogans, to the Deputy Commissioner's (DC) office in Nahan town (Sirmaur, Himachal Pradesh) against the state government's decision to recruit guest teachers.

On 19 January 2024, hundreds of tribals carrying traditional weapons bows and arrows, flags of the 'Sarna' religion, and posters of the chief minister, took out the protest march from Morabadi ground to Kutchery Chowk in Ranchi city (Jharkhand) against questioning of Jharkhand CM by the Enforcement Directorate in a suspected money laundering case.

On 19 January 2024, students held a protest on the road in front of the Kendriya Sanskrit Vishwavidyalaya in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) after a fellow student enrolled in PhD was hit by an autorickshaw.

On 19 January 2024, Hynniewtrep Youths' Council (HYC) (Khasi and Jaintia tribes are collectively known as Hynniewtrep) staged a protest in Shillong city (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) against the Ministry of Home Affairs for ignoring their demand for the implementation of the Inner Line Permit (ILP). Police stopped them at the Civil Hospital junction, before they could reach either the Raj Bhawan or the venue of the North Eastern Council's plenary session, following which the protesters shouted slogans and released black balloons.

On 19 January 2024, locals blocked the National Highway-55 in Angul city (Anugul, Odisha) to protest over poor road conditions that are causing frequent accidents after the death of an ASHA worker in a fatal accident.

On 19 January 2024, family members of two deceased kids and others from the neighborhood staged a protest, after kids died trying to escape from dogs, in the Baner area of Jodhpur city (Rajasthan) demanding the dogs were caught. The dog squad of the municipal corporation apprehended the pet dogs.

On 19 January 2024, hundreds of residents in and around Teliamura sub division staged a road blockade protest and blocked the Assam-Agartala National Highway (coded to Teliamura town, Khowai, Tripura) demanding protection from wild elephant attacks. Locals claimed that they had brought the issue up to authorities multiple times but no actions were taken. Protesters lifted the blockade on the same day.

On 19 January 2024, about 500 Samagra Shiksha teachers staged a protest in front of the office of the Siksha Bhawan in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) against concerned authorities for delaying their D.El.Ed completion certificates and for financial deprivation.

On 19 January 2024, hundreds of Panchayat Raj Department (local government) employees from across the district, including sanitation workers, Assistant Development Officers, and Secretaries, staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Panchayat Vikas Bhawan in Darsana village (Hathras, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused who behaved indecently (over a phone call) with the District Panchayat Raj Officer (DPRO) over the name of BJP state minister.

On 19 January 2024, Adivasi community members (tribal group) held a protest at Malandighi village (Paschim Bardhaman district, WB) over people from their community not being employed by a gas lifting company operating in the area.

On 19 January 2024, AKSU and KPP(U) members jointly held a protest by blocking a railway track at Betgara town (Jalpaiguri district, WB) against BJP and TMC to demand a separate Kamtapur state and that the BJP-led central government initiate peace talks with KLO.
On 19 January 2024, Bangiya Hindu Mahamancha (a Bengali Hindu group) held a sit-in protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) to demand protection for women in the city.

On 19 January 2024, students led by TMCP members held a protest at Cooch Behar city (WB) against a university over claimed misuse of funds allocated for sport activities and demanded the resignation of the vice-chancellor.

On 19 January 2024, members of the Voice of the People Party's (VPP) and police personnel engaged in a scuffle (likely violent) after VPP members attempted to enter the Secretariat in Shillong city (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) during a protest over the state government's refusal to reinstate sacked Lokayukta officials. Those present asked the police not to 'manhandle' the Member of the Legislative Assembly present.

On 19 January 2024, locals held a demonstration by burning tyres at Nagri Parole village (Kathua district, J&K) over the death of a school teacher in a road accident and demanded ban on entry of dumper trucks in the area.

On 19 January 2024, students and members of the Bhim Army, led by the Bhim Army Chief (ASP National President), staged a protest at Delhi University's North Campus area in Delhi - Civil Lines (Central Delhi, Delhi) in support of an assistant professor whose service was terminated in 2020 - she was known for protesting against the suspected caste-based discrimination and harassment by the Daulat Ram College administration. Protesters were detained.

On 19 January 2024, members of BKU staged a protest in Nausha village (Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh) demanding an increase in the Kisan Samman Nidhi (Farmer's Tribute Fund - a kind of minimum income support), a hike in old age pension, and free electricity for private tube wells.

On 19 January 2024, cotton farmers staged a 'pukka morcha' (permanent sit-in protest), and pitched tents along the road, at Shaheed Chowk (intersection) in Abohar city (Fazilka, Punjab) against the Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) for failing to fulfill its promise of procuring cotton crops from farmers.

On 19 January 2024, a few Anganwadi workers (government worker in rural child care) blocked the convoy of the Forest Minister and held a protest in Uravakonda town (Ananthpur, Andhra Pradesh) as part of their ongoing protest against the state government to press for their various demands. The women police had reportedly slapped some of the women. A woman was injured and taken to the nearby hospital.

On 19 January 2024, three Indian Youth Congress members waved black balloons at the Prime Minister's convoy in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) to protest against the detention of several INC leaders, under preventive custody, during the Prime Minister's arrival in Tamil Nadu.

On 19 January 2024, aspiring pharmacists under the aegis of Sanyukt Sangharsh Samiti (united struggle committee) of pharmacists, nursing, and paramedical cadre held a protest at the State Institute of Health and Family Welfare (SIHFW) in Jaipur city (Rajasthan) demanding the government to accelerate the recruitment process.

On 19 January 2024, around 24 auto-rickshaw drivers, led by a BSP leader, staged a dharna (sit-in protest) outside the office of the Superintendent of Police (SP) in Phagwara city (Kapurthala, Punjab) against the police for registering a cross-case against an auto driver who was assaulted instead of taking action against the assailants.

On 19 January 2024, members of the Sindhi community members held a protest march in front of Gandhinagar police station (Kolhapur, Maharashtra) against delayed and insufficient police response to the crime.

On 19 January 2024, scores of students staged a candlelight protest march at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) in Kanpur city (Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) against the recent suicide of students which the protesters claimed was caused by the fear of termination from Ph.D. and Master's degree programs. The protesters demanded a revision of the evaluation process of the research thesis for such programs.

Around 19 January 2024 (as reported), teachers under the banner of the Computer Teachers' Union staged a protest march in Ludhiana city (Punjab) demanding the provision of benefits under the Sixth Pay Commission and the merger of computer teachers with the education department.

On 19 January 2024, a large group of residents claiming to be mining dependents gathered outside the Kalay village panchayat in Sanguem taluka (South Goa, Goa) to protest against the panchayat's stance on unloading of iron ore at the Kalay railway yard.

On 19 January 2024, members of the Muslim community assaulted Hindu activists from BJP and RSS in Devar Hippargi town (Vijayapura, Karnataka) after members of the Hindu community raised 'Jai Shri Ram' slogans in a Muslim-dominated locality during the distribution of 'Mantrakshate' (sacred grains of rice brought from Ayodhya).

On 19 January 2024, a nine-member gang from a Muslim community assaulted two colleagues (likely a Hindu man and a Muslim woman) in Byadagi town (Haveri district, Karnataka) suspecting them to be involved in a romantic relationship. Police arrested eight suspects involved in the incident.

On 19 January 2024, unidentified persons (likely members of BJP/BJYM based on ongoing political rivalry) attacked members of IYC and INC and vandalised their vehicles in North Lakhimpur town (Lakhimpur, Assam) while they were arranging posters for Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra rally the next day. Rioters also removed banners and posters for the rally. Congress party claimed that Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) were responsible for the attacks which was refuted by Assam's DGP.

On 19 January 2024, members of Ching Tam Apunba Nupi Lup Pallel (likely a Meitei women group based on name and action) and Pallel Meira Paibi Apunba Lup (women torch bearers, likely Meitei based on action) organized a protest with slogans at Pallel Mamang Leikai (locality) in Pallel town (Tengnoupal, Manipur) demanding prompt replacement of the Security Advisor of Manipur, continued custody of 2 Kukis involved in the killing of Meitei SPDO (coded separately) and sufficient deployment of state forces at Moreh amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 19 January 2024, members of Manipur unit of Communist Party of India staged a protest rally with slogans from CPI Irawat Bhawan Complex in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding resignation of Manipur's Chief Minister citing his failure in controlling state violence amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters were not allowed to proceed further by police forces when they reached Imphal Municipality Corporation area.

On 19 January 2024, Apunba Meira Paibi Lup (women torch bearers, likely Meitei based on action) and Wangjing Gram Panchayat Apunba Club Organisation (WANGGPACO) (likely Meitei based on action) organized a candlelight vigil at Ibudhou Wangjing Lakpa Shanglen within Wangjing town (Thoubal, Manipur) in honour of Meiteis who died during the ongoing conflict amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. WANGGPACO demanded the resignation of the Chief Minister and Security Advisor. Protesters also shouted slogans.

On 19 January 2024, employees of LIC (Life Insurance Corporation) (public sector insurance company) and members of the All India Insurance Employees Association staged a protest and organising a 'signature collection' program at the Kadapa Arts College grounds in Kadapa city (YSR district, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the strengthening of the institution, the withdrawal of tax on health insurance premiums and income tax concession on insurance savings.

On 19 January 2024, residents staged a protest in front of the Tahsildar's (revenue officer) officer in the Agraharam locality in Alur town (Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh) accusing the administration of not supplying essential commodities for nearly three weeks through the Mobile Dispensing Unit. The protesters demanded the authorities to take measures to supply to supply the items on time.

On 19 January 2024, members of a non-governmental organisation called 'Reformers, a Group for Justice' staged a protest in front of the South Goa additional collector in Margao city (South Goa, Goa) against a recent bill passed by the Union government which proposes strict punishment for hit-and-run accident cases.

On 19 January 2024, members of the INC and the IYC staged black flag protests in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) against the Prime Minister when he was visiting the city to inaugurate an event. The police detained 9 protesters.

On 19 January 2024, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization), reached Sahebganj tehsil (Muzaffarpur, Bihar) and staged a protest march blaming the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. TMC claimed the stones were pelted when the campaign was passing through Bihar and not West Bengal.

On 31 January 2024, members of the BJP staged a protest at the Vizianagaram Municipal Corporation in Vizianagaram city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding the YSRCP-led state government to distribute Ayushman Bharat cards which would provide health insurance to beneficiaries. The protesters accused the state government of stopping the card distribution in order to prevent the people from seeing the work that was done by the BJP-led Union government.

On 31 January 2024, a group of farmers from Sattur and Tadasinakoppa villages staged a protest in front of the tahsildar's office in Dharwad city (Karnataka) demanding the administration to take measures to stop stray cattle from entering their fields and destroying their crops. The protesters locked the office and said that they would not open the door until their demands were met.
On 31 January 2024, members of farmer associations staged a protest in Hosapete city (Ballari, Karnataka) demanding an investigation into a farmer leader's death in a road accident.

On 31 January 2024, farmers along with members of the CPI(M) staged a protest outside the cotton purchasing centre in Sadashivpet town (Sangareddy, Telangana) against the Cotton Corporation of India's (CCI) decision to close down the purchasing centre since mill was filled with the cotton due to increased arrivals over the previous days. The protesters accused the CCI of planning to close down the purchasing centre permanently.

On 31 January 2024, councillors including members of the INC staged a protest during the monthly meeting at the Mangaluru City Corporation council hall in Mangaluru city (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) against the irregular supply of drinking water in many wards in the city.

On 31 January 2024, Muslims staged a protest in Sirwar town (Raichur, Karnataka) after they found out that unknown assailants had desecrated a portrait of Tipu Sultan (Indian Muslim ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore). The protesters demanded the authorities to find and arrest the culprits.

On 31 January 2024, members of the Muslim Youth League took out a protest march at Karipur city (Malappuram, Kerala) against the BJP-led Union government's decision to increase the Haj (annual Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca, Saudi Arabia, which is considered to be the holiest city for Muslims) flight rates from Calicut International Airport.

On 31 January 2024, hundreds of students along with members of the KSU, MSF and the Fraternity Movement staged joint protests at the Maharaja's College campus in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) demanding the removal of a professor at the Arabic department. The protesters accused the professor of behaving indecently.

On 31 January 2024, a former TDP MLA and his followers staged a protest in Pedavegi village (West Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) after people made an attempt to illegally mine gravel. The protesters demanded the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) to take action against the accused.

On 31 January 2024, locals staged a protest outside the Mankulam divisional forest office in Mankulam village (Idukki, Kerala) against a Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) for abusing a priest belonging to St. Joseph's church at Anakulam over an incident where wild elephants panicked and fled after crackers were burst during an annual festival at the church.

On 31 January 2024, about 50 people staged a protest in the Thiruvottiyur locality in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) after a cable TV operator died after he crashed his bike into a parked container truck. The protesters demanded the police to stop speeding container trucks and end the practice of illegal parking.

On 31 January 2024, local people staged a protest in Guru Sikharan village (Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh) against the vandalization of a statue of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar (a Dalit champion) on 30 January (coded separately).

On 31 January 2024, INC and AAP Councilors, including an INC former Union Minister, and the INC State/UT President, staged a protest, raising slogans, outside a police station at Sector 17 in Chandigarh city accusing the BJP party of foul play during the Chandigarh Mayoral elections - where a BJP candidate was declared the winner.

On 31 January 2024, members of IYC staged a protest, raising slogans, outside the Mayor's office in Chandigarh city accusing the BJP party of foul play during the Chandigarh Mayoral elections - where a BJP candidate was declared the winner. Protesters were detained.

On 31 January 2024, local people and family members of the deceased staged a protest and placed the deceased's body along the Shadiabad intersection in Rampur Bantara village (Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused who shot and killed a man (an SP leader) earlier in the day (coded separately).

On 31 January 2024, local people and family members of the deceased staged a protest along the National Highway 31 (NH-31) in Daya Chhupra village (Ballia, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a woman who was hit and killed by a tractor.

On 31 January 2024, passengers staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Indira Gandhi International Airport (Delhi Airport) in Delhi - Vasant Vihar (New Delhi, Delhi) against IndiGo airlines over the delay and cancellation of several flights. A video of the incident was circulated online.

On 31 January 2024, local traders, including the INTUC District president, staged a protest rally under the banner of various trade unions from Kala Kendra to the Sub-Divisional Officer's (SDO) office in Banjar town (Kullu, Himachal Pradesh) over various issues including the state government's decision (taken on December 2022) to exclude MNREGA (central government labour scheme) and construction workers from the Labor Welfare Board and discontinue assistance.

On 31 January 2024, hundreds of local people, including a BJP MLA, put up tents and staged a protest, raising slogans, at Trivenighat along the Bilaspur-Solan border near Naina Devi town (Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh) against the Kikar-Navgaon drinking water scheme of Solan. The BJP MLA claimed that the water scheme would deprive other areas (primarily under opposition leaders) of drinking water.

On 31 January 2024, members of various trade unions, including the AITUC General secretary (CPI), staged a massive protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Amritsar city (Punjab) against the suspected exploitation of poor people in rural areas by microfinance organizations.

On 31 January 2024, local people staged a protest, led by a former INC Spokesperson, at Chowk Bazaar (Market) in Lohaghat town (Champawat, Uttarakhand) against the lack of clean drinking water and demanded the provision of Saryu Lift Drinking Water Scheme.

On 31 January 2024, a local activist and his supporters staged a protest, carrying a flower bouquet, at the Municipal Corporation's (MC) Zone D office in Ludhiana city (Punjab) demanding an investigation into the involvement of politicians and others in the ghost employees scam.

On 31 January 2024, local women staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Public Works Department (PWD) office in Berinag town (Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand) against the PWD for failing to complete the construction of the Pabhya-Mantoli-Agar motor road.
On 31 January 2024, residents of Noora village held a protest and blocked the Masaurhi-Gaya road under Masaurhi police station (Patna district, Bihar) over the murder of a 35-year-old man.

On 31 January 2024, Adivasi residents of Habalepada and Nagarmudi Pada held a protest in Mulund city (coded to Mumbai Suburban - Kurla, Maharashtra) against the construction of twin tunnels that will run under the Sanjay Gandhi National Park (SGNP) hills and exit at Khindipada in Mulund.

On 31 January 2024, members of Samta Parishad, OBC Jan Jagran Sangharsh Samiti, Savata Parishad, and other OBC organizations held 'Jode Maro' agitation in which they kicked and burned posters of Buldhana constituency MLA at the district collectorate in Aurangabad city (Maharashtra), during a protest demanding the preservation of reservations for OBCs, nomadic tribes, and special backward classes.

On 31 January 2024, some residents of Himmatnagar housing scheme held a protest at the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) office in Vadodara city (Gujarat) against the notice issued by the VMC asking them to vacate the houses by 3 February.

Around 31 January 2024 (as reported), the former employees of Madhya Pradesh Gramin Bank (MPGB) and senior citizens staged a dharna (sit-in protest) in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) over non-fulfilling of demands including payment of gratuity, payment of earned leave encashment, payment of compassionate allowance and resolution of non-payment of pension to voluntarily retired members.

On 31 January 2024, MSJK members held a protest by burning an effigy at Jammu city (J&K) against Pakistan, China and JuD and JeM chiefs and demanded military action to takeover Pakistan administered Kashmir.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Assam Rifles
text: On 31 January 2024, a mob of around 100 local Kuki women prevented AR personnel from entering D Monomphai village on the outskirts of Moreh town (Tengnoupal, Manipur), opposing the deployment of central security forces in the region, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state. AR personnel were pushed and chased out when they attempted to enter after which they left.

Around 31 January 2024 (as reported), members of Sikkim Krantikari Morcha (SKM) including the chairman of National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC) attacked a member of the Sikkim Democratic Front (SDF) with a rod and injured him in Namchi area (coded to Namchi city, South Sikkim, Sikkim) over unknown reasons (likely political rivalry due to upcoming legislative assembly elections).

Around 31 January 2024 (as reported), members of Mizo Zirlai Pawl (MZP) staged a demonstration and burned effigies of PM and HM of India in Aizawl city (Aizawl, Mizoram) opposing the government's proposed plan to scrap the Free Movement Regime (FMR) and fence the Indo-Myanmar border. MZP claimed that the borders were imposed by the British without consent that divided Mizos into different countries and states and the proposed plan would hamper clan interaction, social affairs, and mutual assistance.

On 31 January 2024, the All India Save Education Committee staged a protest in front of Ujjayanta Palace in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) demanding the cancellation of National Education Policy (NEP). Protesters claimed that the central government distorted history and science in the updated curriculum, disregarding the perspectives of esteemed educators.
On 31 January 2024, villagers blocked the road at a village in Sheikhpura district (Bihar) during a protest against the rape and murder of a 13-year-old girl.

Around 31 January 2024 (as reported), villagers protested at 23 places in Bastar district (coded as Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh) against the Tatkal (temporary) camps formed by the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF).
Around 31 January 2024 (as reported), several villagers held a protest in Silger village (Sukma, Chhattisgarh) against the Tatkal (temporary) camps formed by the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF).

On 31 January 2024, doctors affiliated to the Kerala Government Medical College Teachers Association (KGMCTA) staged a protest in front of the directorate of medical education (DME) in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) against the LDF-led state government's decision to transfer 61 faculty members to newly set-up medical colleges in Konni and Idukki. The protesters demanded the government to withdraw the decision.

On 31 January 2024, more than 500 members of the Tamil Nadu Association for the Rights of All Types of Differently Abled and Caregivers (TARATDAC) and members of the National Platform for the Rights of the Disabled (NPRD) staged a sit-in protest on the Collectorate road in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the government to provide a monthly financial assistance for differently- abled people.

On 31 January 2024, members of the TDP including its Scheduled Caste Cell, Backward Classes Cell and members of the Farmers Committee staged a 'Rythu Karuvu Keka' (Farmers' Cry for Help) protest march from the TDP office to the RDO office in Dhone town (Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the YSRCP-led state government to declare that Dhone and Peapully mandals be declared as drought-prone areas. The protesters marched with bullock carts to mark their protest.

On 31 January 2024, members of the Rayalaseema Women's Association staged a protest in the Rayalaseema region (coded to Kurnool city, Andhra Pradesh) demanding compensation for those who have lost their autos due to accidents and other reasons. The protesters also highlighted an event when a building collapsed and destroyed an auto parked below it.

On 31 January 2024, about 100 people staged a protest in front of the Guduvanchery area in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the release of six people including a village panchayat president's husband, who were arrested by the police on charges of threat and extortion.

On 31 January 2024, family members of a girl who died staged a protest at the Jammalamadugu government hospital in Jammalamadugu town (YSR Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh) after they found that the deceased's body had been invaded by ants due to the non-functioning of the freezer box in the mortuary.

On 31 January 2024, members of the TDP and the YSRCP including an MLA clashed with each other in Muddanur town (Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh) when the YSRCP members pelted stones and threw chairs at a TDP member's residence. The police intervened and detained the rioters. A car was damaged in the clashes.

Around 31 January 2024 (as reported), local contractors staged a protest on the National Highway 765 in Kunta village (Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the YSRC-led state government to clear their pending bills in order for them to continue supplying water to villages in the Yerragondapalem Assembly constituency.

Around 31 January 2024 (as reported), citizens staged a protest in Panaji city (North Goa, Goa) against the Goa State Urban Development Agency's (GSUDA) decision to cut down trees in the St Inez locality for a development project.

On 31 January 2024, residents staged a human chain protest from Nagalapalli to Atchutapuram in Anakapalli district (coded to Atchutapuram village, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the authorities to develop the road.

On 31 January 2024, supporters of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), a protest march, reached Haldwani city (Nainital, Uttarakhand) where they blamed the BJP-led central and state governments for the rise in communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The Yatra which entered 'day 53' on 10 December 2023 began in Bengaluru city under the banner of NBS, RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization). The yatra is scheduled to conclude in New Delhi on 3 March 2024 - likely to pass through 80 districts across 13 states.

On 1 February 2024, a mob of around 50 persons, mostly women, held policemen captive by tying them to a tree and assaulted them when they arrived at Bhimpur village (Nadia district, WB) in relation to a land dispute case and demanded them to settle the case. Police later arrested eight persons including 4 women.
On 1 February 2024, family members assaulted a doctor and vandalised a hospital at Kolkata city (WB) over claimed medical negligence leading to a patient's death.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests in Salem district (coded to Salem city, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests in Namakkal district (coded to Namakkal city, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests in Dharmapuri district (coded to Dharmapuri city, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests in Krishnagiri district (coded to Krishnagiri city, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests in Tamil Nadu state (coded to Chennai) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence.

On 1 February 2024, hundreds of AIADMK members staged a protest at the Fort Maidan in Salem city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK staged a protest in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence. The protesters also raised slogans against a DML minister for making discriminatory comments about a former Chief Minister and AIADMK leader.
On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests in Pollachi town (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the deteriorating law and order in the state.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests at the Coimbatore South taluk office in Coimbatore city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the deteriorating law and order in the state. The protesters also condemned the lack of development works initiated by the DMK.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister and MLAs staged a protest near the BSNL office in Dharmapuri city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister staged a protest in Tiruchengode town (Namakkal, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence. The protesters also raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former MP staged protests in the Vazhavanthankottai and Marakkadai localities in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for not taking action against those responsible for the assault of a Dalit domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister staged protests in Pettavaithalai town (Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for not taking action against those responsible for the assault of a Dalit domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister staged a protest in the Manikundu locality in Dindigul city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for not taking action against those responsible for the assault of a Dalit domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK including an MLA staged a protest at the Anna Statue near the Krishnagiri bus stand in Krishnagiri city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing prices of essential commodities, the law and order issues in the state and against the assault of a domestic worker at a DMK MLA's family residence. The protesters also raised slogans against a DML minister for making discriminatory comments about a former Chief Minister and AIADMK leader.

On 1 February 2024, members of the AIADMK including an MLA staged a protest in Mettupalayam town (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the deteriorating law and order in the state. The protesters also said that the DMK has not managed to exempt students from taking the National Eligibility Entrance Test (Undergraduate) (NEET) (pre-medical test) as was promised in the DMK election manifesto before the state assembly elections.
On 1 February 2024, members of the AITUC staged a protest at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) with a list of demands for working class citizens.

On 1 February 2024, members of the BJP Kisan Morcha and the BJP staged a protest in front of the district collectorate in Ongole city (Prakasam, Andhra Pradesh) accusing the YSRCP-led state government and the Chief Minister of not doing anything for farmers. The protesters said that the government not completed the Pula Subbaiah Veligonda irrigation project, provided compensation to farmers who lost their crops or maintained the already existing irrigation projects.

On 1 February 2024, members of the CPI staged a protest in Manapparai town (Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu) against the decision of a cooperative milk society attached to Aavin (state government milk cooperative) to increase the price of milk. The protesters said that the price increase was done without consultation and demanded a withdrawal of the decision.

On 1 February 2024, members of the Mysuru Kannada Vedike staged a protest in Rajkumar Park in Mysuru city (Karnataka) against the Karnataka Governor's decision to send back an ordinance that proposed the use of Kannada language on signboards. The ordinance was passed by the Karnataka cabinet and aimed to amend the Kannada Language Comprehensive Development Act, 2022, which mandated 60% space on signboards for Kannada language and 40% for other languages.

On 1 February 2024, flower traders staged a protest at the temporary flower market near the Old Bus Stand in Salem city (Tamil Nadu) against the removal of roofing sheets from their shops by other shop keepers who said that the roofing sheets were blocking their visibility.

On 1 February 2024, Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) forest workers under the aegis of the CITU marked 1163 days of protest in Tirupati city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding an increase in their monthly wages. On 1 February, the protesters ended their demonstration after the officials agreed to their demand.

On 1 February 2024, students, parents and the alumni of Jai Hind Government Aided Higher Primary School staged a protest in front of the school in Bellampalli village (Udupi, Karnataka) demanding permanent teachers in the school.

On 1 February 2024, a large number of students along with members of the KSU and the Fraternity Movement staged protests at the National Institute of Technology, Calicut (NIT-C) campus in Kozhikode city (Kerala) against the suspension order given to a student of a Electronics and Communication department after he was involved in a clash between two groups over the Ram Temple inauguration in Ayodhya (coded separately). The KSU protesters drew a map of India outside the campus to mark their protest.

On 1 February 2024, members of the Andhra Pradesh Private Degree College Managements' Association took out a protest rally in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against a notification from the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) which called for the setting up of Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA), Bachelor of Computer Application (BCA) and Bachelor of Management Studies (BMS) courses in colleges. The protesters said that introducing new courses would affect the financial stability of the colleges and demanded that the notification be withdrawn.

On 1 February 2024, villagers staged a protest in the Seelai Pillaiyar Puthur locality near Thottiyam town (Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu) after a person put up defamatory posters against women belonging to another community in the village. The protesters demanded action against the culprit.

On 1 February 2024, locals of Kottangiri staged a protest in Shoolagiri village (Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu) after a farmer was killed in a wild elephant attack when he was on his way back from his cattle shed. The protesters demanded the forest department to take action to stop wild animal attacks.

On 1 February 2024, relatives and family members of a history sheeter who was murdered for unknown reasons (coded separately) staged a protest on the Chennai-Bengaluru highway in Athipet village near Kaveripakkam town (Ranipet, Tamil Nadu) demanding action against the accused.

On 1 February 2024, over 500 people from Kuruppanaickenpalayam and Andikulam panchayats took out a protest march to the municipal office in Bhavani town (Erode, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government's proposal to merge the two panchayats with the Bhavani municipality. The protesters said that the merger would affect their livelihood since the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) (social employment scheme) would not be implemented in the municipality. The protesters demanded the administration to cancel the proposal and submitted a petition to the municipal officials to mark their protest.

On 1 February 2024, about 15 people including the State president of the AAP Youth Wing, and Dainik Rail Yatri Maha Sangh (Daily Rail Commuters Association) President staged a protest and burned an effigy in Mahendragarh city (Haryana) demanding the opening of the Roadways Sub Depot Workshop that was built several years ago.

On 1 February 2024, a large number of farmers from Kisan Sangharsh Morcha (SKM) and BKU (Bhanu) staged a protest, along Jail Road at Neeraj-Shahryar Park in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) accusing the police of misbehavior and lathi-charge when the farmers attempted to stop the convoy of a BJP State minister who had come to inaugurate an exhibition in the area.

On 1 February 2024, many young people staged a protest in the Barnala district (Punjab) condemning the AAP-led state government for arresting a man (a social media/YouTube personality) who was arrested on charges of extortion.

On 1 February 2024, many young people staged a protest in the Mansa district (Punjab) condemning the AAP-led state government for arresting a man (a social media/YouTube personality) who was arrested on charges of extortion.

On 1 February 2024, many young people staged a protest in the Sangrur district (Punjab) condemning the AAP-led state government for arresting a man (a social media/YouTube personality) who was arrested on charges of extortion.

On 1 February 2024, a large number of INC members, led by the former Chief Minister (INC), went on a hunger strike and staged a silent dharna (sit-in protest) at Gandhi Park in Dehradun city (Punjab) demanding landholding rights to displaced people in the Tehri Dam area.

On 1 February 2024, hundreds of workers and members of the Uttarakhand Purv Sainik Kalyan Nigam Limited (UPNL) (Uttarakhand Ex-Servicemen Welfare Corporation) staged a protest march to the District magistrate's office in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) against the state government for failing to fulfill their long-standing demands on better welfare of workers.

On 1 February 2024, members of NSUI and SCS staged a protest at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University's Paliwal campus in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) against the university officials who clashed with students on 24 January (coded separately) and demanded the removal of the Chief Proctor (ABVP State president). The protesters scuffled with the police (likely non-violent) and climbed on the bonnet of the Vice-chancellor's car. The police pulled them down.

On 1 February 2024, defense force candidates gathered under the banner of the AICC ex-servicemen department and staged a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) demanding the implementation of the remaining steps of the recruitment process post the physical examination.

On 1 February 2024, hundreds of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SP) members held a protest outside the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in Pune city (Maharashtra) against the ED's summon to the NCP-SP chief's grandnephew in the Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank (MSCB) case.

On 1 February 2024, Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SP) members held a protest in Kolhapur city (Maharashtra) against the state and the union government over 'anti-farmer' policies adopted by the central government.

On 1 February 2024, hundreds of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SP) held a protest outside the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and NCP-SP office in Mumbai, city (Mumbai Suburban, Maharashtra) against the ED's summon to the NCP-SP chief's grandnephew in the Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank (MSCB) case.

On 1 February 2024, the devotees of Jaganath (Hindu deity) performed 'sankirtan' (narrated the story of lord Jaganath) in front of the district Collector's office in Bhadrak town (Bhadrak, Odisha) during a protest demanding an apology from the district administration for claimed 'disrespect' to Lord Jagannath's idol.

On 1 February 2024, members of the Dalit community and Bhim Army led by councilor initiated a hunger strike and held a protest at Lalbagh's Sagar Tower suburb in Burhanpur city (Burhanpur, Madhya Pradesh), demanding the installation of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar's (a Dalit icon) statue in the area.

On 1 February 2024, residents staged a 'chakka jam' (road blockade) protest in Bamori town (Guna, Madhya Pradesh) demanding the arrest of the accused involved in the vandalism in the Shiva temple (coded separately) and the demolition of their properties.

On 1 February 2024, hundreds of Islamic clerics and members of the Kerala Muslim Jamat (KMJ) took out a protest march at Karipur city (Malappuram, Kerala) against the BJP-led Union government's decision to increase the Haj (annual Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca, Saudi Arabia, which is considered to be the holiest city for Muslims) flight rates from Calicut International Airport. The police did not allow the protesters to enter the airport premises.

Around 1 February 2024 (as reported), DRSF members held a protest at Mungpoo town (Darjeeling district, WB) against a university over lack of administrative staff leading to delay in payment of salaries and disbursement of marksheets and certificates among other issue functional issues.

On 1 February 2024, locals held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over low quality food being served at an anganwadi center (a state sponsored scheme to address malnutrition in children) and demanded proper services.

On 1 February 2024, members of the BJP including the BJP Block chief, BJP District president, and BJYM District president, led a BJP leader (former MLA), staged a protest at the police station in Kasganj city (Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected attack on the former BJP MLA's vehicle earlier in the evening (coded separately).

On 1 February 2024, 1147 Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) members staged the 'Jail Bharo' (fill up the jail), a protest movement, in Nashik city (Maharashtra) against the government's failure to address their demands. Police later took them into custody and transported them to jail.

On 1 February 2024, over hundred members of AASU staged a protest with slogans near the DC office in Nagaon town (Nagaon, Assam) against the state government for attempting to impose English as a medium of instruction for Maths and Science from class 6 onwards in government schools.
On 1 February 2024, a mob vandalized a vehicle at the Badrighat area on the outskirts of Silchar city (Cachar, Assam) that was responsible for speeding and injuring 3 pedestrians.

On 1 February 2024, Margherita AJYCP members staged a 3 hour protest with slogans at Ledo Railway Rangamancha in Ledo town (Tinsukia, Assam) against illegal coal mining within Margherita sub division. Protesters condemned the BJP government for their perceived inability of the former in curbing illegal coal mining.

On 1 February 2024, hundreds of Anganwadi workers (female health workers), helpers and mini workers staged a protest organized by Assam State Anganwadi Workers and Helpers Association for the 1st day in front of the Women and Child Welfare Directorate office at Uzanbazar locality in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Manipur) citing the government's ignorance of their demand to increase the salary of Anganwadi workers to Rs 12,000, helpers to Rs 7,000 and mini workers to Rs 10,250.

On 13 February 2024, farmers affiliated to the CPI-affiliated Tamil Nadu Vivasayigal Sangam (Tamil Nadu All Farmers Association's Coordination Committee) staged a protest in Peravurani town (Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu) in solidarity with the 'Delhi Chalo' (let's go to Delhi) protests organised by the SKM, the KMM and central trade unions to demand pay hikes, restoration of the old pension scheme, minimum support price (MSP) for crops, and the withdrawal of labour law amendments.

On 13 February 2024, farmers affiliated to the Tamil Nadu Farmers' Protection Movement and other farmer welfare associations staged protests in 22 locations across Tamil Nadu state (coded to Chennai) against the DMK-led state government for supplying imported palm oil through public distribution outlets instead of supplying coconut oil and groundnut oil. The police arrested the protesters. The protesters raised slogans against the BJP-led Union government and the DMK-led state government for ignoring the demands of farmers.

On 13 February 2024, farmers from Perur taluk staged a protest by 'laying siege' to an earthmover and two trucks in in Coimbatore city (Tamil Nadu) after they found that the vehicles were being used to take gravel sand from Theethipalayam panchayat by a contractor for the Western Ring Road Project.

On 13 February 2024, farmers staged a protest and 'laid siege' to the District Forest Office in NGO Colony in Tirunelveli city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to take measures to stop wild boars from destroying their crops.

On 13 February 2024, farmers staged a protest at the Four-Road signal point in Palladam town (Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for supplying imported palm oil through public distribution outlets instead of supplying coconut oil and groundnut oil. The police arrested the protesters.

On 13 February 2024, farmers staged a protest on Pollachi road in Sultanpet village (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for supplying imported palm oil through public distribution outlets instead of supplying coconut oil and groundnut oil. The police arrested the protesters.

On 13 February 2024, farmers staged protests in Coimbatore district (coded to Coimbatore city, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for supplying imported palm oil through public distribution outlets instead of supplying coconut oil and groundnut oil.

On 13 February 2024, farmers staged protests in Tiruppur district (coded to Tiruppur city, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for supplying imported palm oil through public distribution outlets instead of supplying coconut oil and groundnut oil.

On 13 February 2024, members of the Kisan Morcha, the BJP, the ABVP and a former minister staged a Rythu Garjana (peasant roar) protest in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for ignoring the plight for farmers. The police detained the protesters.

On 13 February 2024, over 20,000 Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHA) affiliated to the Karnataka Rajya Samyukta Asha Karyakarteyara Sangha and the AIUTUC launched a two-day protest at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) to demand the INC-led state government to fulfil their demands including better work conditions, fair wages, the regularisation of their services, insurance and other benefits.

On 13 February 2024, members of Hindu organisations staged a protest in Bagalkot city (Bagalkote, Karnataka) against the district administration for allowing the 'Tablighi Bade Istema', an event of Muslim organisations on government land. The protesters demanded the administration to cancel the event.

On 13 February 2024, over 50 jeep drivers working with the Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation (CCMC) staged a protest on the CCMC premises in Coimbatore city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to pay their salaries on time.

On 13 February 2024, more than 100 members of the Tamil Nadu Revenue Officers' Association staged a protest by organising a hunger strike in Virudhunagar city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to fulfil their demands including the filling up of vacancies, the implementation of a government order and the revocation of de-promotion orders given to non-graduate Deputy Tahsildars (revenue officers).

On 13 February 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu Revenue Officers' Association staged a protest by organising a hunger stroke in Virudhunagar district (Virudhunagar, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to fulfil their demands including the filling up of vacancies, the implementation of a government order and the revocation of de-promotion orders given to non-graduate Deputy Tahsildars (revenue officers).

On 13 February 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu Revenue Officers' Association staged a protest by organising a hunger strike at the Collectorate in Ramanathapuram city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to fulfil their demands including the filling up of vacancies, the implementation of a government order and the revocation of de-promotion orders given to non-graduate Deputy Tahsildars (revenue officers).

On 13 February 2024, members of Tamil Nadu Revenue Officials' Associations staged a protest by organising a hunger strike at the Collectorate in Tirunelveli city (Tamil Nadu) to demand the DMK-led state governments to fulfil their demands including increased salaries, the filling up of vacancies and other welfare measures.

On 13 February 2024, members of Tamil Nadu Revenue Officials' Associations staged protest by organising a hunger strike in Thoothukudi district (coded to Thoothukudi city, Tamil Nadu) to demand the DMK-led state governments to fulfil their demands including increased salaries, the filling up of vacancies and other welfare measures.

On 13 February 2024, members of Tamil Nadu Revenue Officials' Associations staged protest by organising a hunger strike in Tenkasi district (coded to Tenkasi city, Tamil Nadu) to demand the DMK-led state governments to fulfil their demands including increased salaries, the filling up of vacancies and other welfare measures.

On 13 February 2024, members of Tamil Nadu Revenue Officials' Associations staged protest by organising a hunger strike in Kanniyakumari district (coded to Nagercoil city, Tamil Nadu) to demand the DMK-led state governments to fulfil their demands including increased salaries, the filling up of vacancies and other welfare measures.

On 13 February 2024, lawyers staged a protest and 'laid siege' to the Sankeshwar police station in Sankeshwar town (Belagavi, Karnataka) against the delay in arresting the assailants who had attacked a lawyer in Sollapur village for supporting a group of people (coded separately).

On 13 February 2024, five visually impaired students staged a protest for the second day by organising a hunger strike in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to provide them employment opportunities. The police detained the protesters

On 13 February 2024, teachers staged a protest on the Periyar University premises in Salem city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to take action against the Vice-Chancellor and Registrar of the university over allegations of fund misappropriation and other charges.

On 13 February 2024, aided teachers under the aegis of the Kerala Pradesh School Teachers Association took out a protest march to the Kattappana District Education Office (DEO) in Kattappana town (Idukki, Kerala) against the CPI(M)-led state government for the delay in transferring their salaries.

On 13 February 2024, members of the Yadava Sanghala Ikya Vedika (organisation for the Yadava community) staged a protest at the house of Vizianagaram Zilla Parishad chairperson and a YSRCP leader in Vizianagaram city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding the YSRCP to allocate MLA and MP seats for members of the community.

On 13 February 2024, members of the SFI staged black flag protests in Kanjikode town (Palakkad, Kerala) against the Kerala Governor when he was on his way to inaugurate a project. The police detained the protesters.
On 13 February 2024, members of the SFI staged a protest near the Town Hall in Thrissur city (Kerala) against the Kerala Governor. The police detained 5 protesters.

On 13 February 2024, a large number of IYC members staged a demonstration at the Legislative Assembly in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) against the LDF-led state government for not distributing social welfare pensions to beneficiaries. The demonstrators helped placards and raised slogans and attempted to climb over the barricades. The police used water cannons to disperse the crowd following which the demonstrators threw their flags and sticks and scuffled with the police.

On 13 February 2024, members of the Buddhist and Dalit communities clashed with members of the Arakh community, involving stone pelting, at Pikipur village under the Passgawan police station area (Kheri, Uttar Pradesh) in a suspected case of communal conflict over the vandalization of a statue of Lord Buddha (coded separately). The police intervened and lathi-charged the assailants, which resulted in injuries to many people including 2 policemen.

text: On 13 February 2024, 9000 farmers and farmer leaders, from more than 200 farmer unions, including the Rashtriya Kisan Mazdoor Mahasangh (RKMM) National President, gathered under the banner of SKM (Non-political) and KMM and staged a demonstration as a part of the 'Delhi Chalo' march ('Let's go to Delhi' farmer's march), and pelted stones at the police, and attempted to remove the concrete and metal barricades, at the Khanauri border between Sangrur and Jind, next to Khanauri village (Sangrur, Punjab) over various demands including the implementation of the Swaminathan Commission's recommendations, provision of a law guaranteeing Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops, justice for the victims of the violence at Lakhimpur Kheri on 3 October 2021 (coded separately), waiver of farmers' debts, and pension for farmers and farm laborers. The police detained several demonstrators, and lathi-charged, fired tear gas (including via drones), and fired rubber pellets at the demonstrators. Over 127 people were suspected to have suffered injuries - including over 100 farmers, two journalists (who were covering the event), and 27 police personnel (Rapid Action Force) at both the Khanauri and the Shambhu border area (where a similar demonstration took place) the same day.
