The police detained several demonstrators, and lathi-charged, fired tear gas (including via drones), and fired rubber pellets at the demonstrators. Over 127 people were suspected to have suffered injuries - including over 100 farmers, two journalists (who were covering the event), and 27 police personnel (Rapid Action Force) at both the Shambhu and the Khanauri border area (where a similar demonstration took place) the same day.

On 13 February 2024, around 500 farmers of tractor trailers, led by the BKU (Tikait) District President, under the banner of SKM (Non-political) and KMM staged a protest march as a part of the 'Delhi Chalo' march ('Let's go to Delhi' farmer's protest march) from the Ludhiana district (Punjab) over various demands including the implementation of the Swaminathan Commission's recommendations, provision of a law guaranteeing Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops, justice for the victims of the violence at Lakhimpur Kheri on 3 October 2021 (coded separately), waiver of farmers' debts, and pension for farmers and farm laborers.

On 13 February 2024, farmers (some riding tractors) under the banner of SKM (Non-political) and KMM staged a protest march as a part of the 'Delhi Chalo' march ('Let's go to Delhi' farmer's protest march) and attempted to remove the road barricades (nails strewn on the road) at the Teokar border area between Patiala and Kurukshetra next to Teokar village (Kurukshetra, Haryana) over various demands including the implementation of the Swaminathan Commission's recommendations, provision of a law guaranteeing Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops, justice for the victims of the violence at Lakhimpur Kheri on 3 October 2021 (coded separately), waiver of farmers' debts, and pension for farmers and farm laborers.

On 13 February 2024, farmers and agriculturists staged a protest near Titoli village (Rohtak, Haryana) to show solidarity with the SKM non-political and KMM farmers' leading the 'Delhi Chalo' ('Let's go to Delhi' farmer's protest) and demanded the provision of the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops.

On 13 February 2024, farmers from various unions including KKU and BKU gathered under the banner of SKM (Non-political), KMM, and CITU, and staged a protest march, raising slogans, from Hall Bazaar to Putlighar Chowk in Amritsar city (Punjab) over various demands including the implementation of the Swaminathan Commission's recommendations, provision of a law guaranteeing Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops, justice for the victims of the violence at Lakhimpur Kheri on 3 October 2021 (coded separately), waiver of farmers' debts, and pension for farmers and farm laborers. The protest was carried out as a precursor to the nationwide 'Gramin Bharat Bandh' farmer's strike/protest scheduled for 16 February.

On 13 February 2024, more than 500 farmers under the banner of BKU, SKM (Non-political), and KMM staged a protest march as a part of the 'Delhi Chalo' march ('Let's go to Delhi' farmer's protest march) along the KGP Expressway near Maujpur village (Faridabad, Haryana) over various demands including the implementation of the Swaminathan Commission's recommendations, provision of a law guaranteeing Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops, justice for the victims of the violence at Lakhimpur Kheri on 3 October 2021 (coded separately), waiver of farmers' debts, pension for farmers and farm laborers, and the provision of an access point or an interchange to the Greenfield Expressway. The police stopped the protesters at a toll plaza near the Maujpur village.

On 13 February 2024, local people and members of trade associations staged a protest at the Tikri border area in Bahadurgarh city (Jhajjar, Haryana) against the 'Delhi Chalo' (let's go to Delhi) farmer's protest march.

On 13 February 2024, outsourced workers of the Uttarakhand Purva Sainik Kalyan Nigam Limited (UPNL) (Ex-Servicemen Welfare Corporation) staged a protest 'day 2' in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) the regularization of outsourced UPNL workers as government employees. The protesters are on a Maha Andolan (indefinite strike).

On 13 February 2024, aspiring teachers staged a protest outside the residence of a BJP State minister in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) against the state government whom the protesters accused of failing to address their longstanding demanding the appointment of 6800 reserved category candidates.
On 13 February 2024, members of the Electrical Workmen Union staged a protest outside the SE (electrical) at Sector 9 in Chandigarh city demanding the release of pending salaries.

On 13 February 2024, around 400 local people under the banner of Ali Khud Bachao Sangarsh Samiti (Save the Ali River Tributary Struggle Committee) staged a demonstration and pelted stones and machinery at the police in Navgaon village (Solan, Himachal Pradesh) against the Kikar-Navgaon drinking water scheme which the demonstrators claimed would deprive other areas of drinking water. 7 policemen and one home guard were injured when they attempted to stop the demonstrators from entering the construction site of the water scheme.

On 13 February 2024, Tripura unit of SKM (non-political) organized a protest rally with slogans from Paradise Chowmhuni area in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) against the central government and demanded pay hikes, restoration of the old pension scheme, MSP for crops, and withdrawal of labour law amendments.

On 13 February 2024, around 100 students of Lilong Haoreibi College staged a protest in Lilong town (Thoubal, Manipur) against the failure of authorities in issuing admission cards, leading to students being unable to sit for exams despite payment and document submission. The principal of the college refuted claims and stated that the admission cards were not issued to those who did not fill up the form.

On 13 February 2024, students of Sikkim NIT shifted their protest from outside the Director's office to the main gate of their campus in Ravangla town (South Sikkim, Sikkim) over mental torture, lack of basic amenities, poor hostel and food conditions along with instances of nepotism and favouritism. Their demands included the reinstatement of the former Training and Placement Cell team, establishment of a student body, better communication, transparency, improvement of food and lodging facilities and a formal apology. Protesters were unable to meet the Director to address their demands and concerns.

On 13 February 2024, Meira Paibi activists (Women Torch Bearers, likely Meitei based on protest demands) engaged in a scuffle (likely violent based on injuries) with military forces at Nongada area (coded to Nongada Thongkhong village (Imphal East, Manipur)) protesting against the road block set up by military forces in the Imphal-Ukhrul road after armed clashes between Meitei and Kuki groups (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Military forces attempted to control the situation, and 1 Meira Paibi member was injured.

On 13 February 2024, police forces fired tear gas shells to disperse a large crowd of Meira Paibi activists (Women Torch Bearers, likely Meitei based on protest demands) from Tekcham, Samaram, Sapam and Tentha present at Khongjom police station in Khongjom village (Thoubal, Manipur) to protest against the suspected verbal abuse by Thoubal commando in Tekcham village (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Meira Paibis staged a sit in protest at Khongjom later demanding a public apology and the transfer of the commando.

On 13 February 2024, a large number of assailants (likely Meitei based on the location and name of the deceased) attempted to loot arms from the Manipur Police Training College (MPTC) armoury located in Pangei village (Imphal East, Manipur) and security forces (likely police forces based on the target) opened fire to disperse the crowd which killed 1 and injured 2 others amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Police forces initially fired rounds of tear gas shells but they had to open fire when the situation escalated.

On 13 February 2024, people took out protest marches in various parts of Wayanad district (coded to Kalpetta city, Kerala) in support of the dawn-to-dusk hartal called by a group of farmer organisations under the aegis of the Farmers' Relief Forum with a list of demands including protection from wild animal attacks after a farmer was attacked and killed by a wild elephant in Padamala.

On 13 February 2024, people staged a protest in Pulpally town (Wayanad, Kerala) in support of the dawn-to-dusk hartal called by a group of farmer organisations under the aegis of the Farmers' Relief Forum with a list of demands including protection from wild animal attacks after a farmer was attacked and killed by a wild elephant in Padamala. The protesters detained a few Forest Department officials and asked them to capture a tiger that was spotted near the area.

On 13 February 2024, farmers under the aegis of the Wayanad farmer collective took out a protest march in Kattikkulam town (Wayanad, Kerala) in support of the dawn-to-dusk hartal called by a group of farmer organisations under the aegis of the Farmers' Relief Forum with a list of demands including protection from wild animal attacks after a farmer was attacked and killed by a wild elephant in Padamala. The protesters also demanded compensation for cross loss.

On 13 February 2024, around 200 members of Hindu right-wing organisations attacked members of a Christian Methodist church in Janwada village (Rangareddy, Telangana) over assumed religious enmity. The assailants also vandalised the church and chanted 'Jai Sri Ram' (glory to Lord Ram) slogans. 12 church members were injured in the attack.

On 13 February 2024, members of the general public and the staff of the Sri Seetha Ramachandra Swamy Devasthanam (Hindu temple) staged separate protests in Bhadrachalam town (Khammam, Telangana) against the transfer of a temple executive officer. The protesters demanded the government to withdraw the transfer order and displayed placards, wore black badges and shouted slogans to mark their protest.

On 13 February 2024, 10-15 members of the NSUI staged a demonstration at the VT Colony in Nalgonda town (Telangana) against members of the BRS who were travelling on a bus to attend a public meeting. The demonstrators wore black clothes, threw eggs at the bus and raised slogans against the BRS leaders. The police detained the demonstrators.

On 13 February 2024, supporters of an INC minister clashed with supporters of an INC MLA during a district INC meeting in Kolar town (Karnataka) when the MLA's supporters voiced his opposition to a banner without his leader's photo at the meeting venue. The members of both the groups physically assaulted each other and sustained injuries.

On 13 February 2024, relatives and residents staged a demonstration in Tittakudi town (Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu) after a youngster was found dead on the road with injuries on his face and head. The youngster had been detained by the police earlier that day with three others for being in an inebriated state. The demonstrators said that the death was suspicious in nature and threw stones at the police resulting in injuries. The police arrested six people.

On 13 February 2024, members of Christian churches from nearby villages staged a protest at the Janwada Crossroads in Janwada village (Rangareddy, Telangana) after a Hindu right wing group vandalised a church in Janwada village and assaulted church members (coded separately). The police lathi (baton) charged the protesters.

On 13 February 2024, junior medical students staged a protest at the vice-principal's office in Ramagundam Medical College in Ramagundam city (Peddapalli, Telangana) against senior students for bullying them. The protesters demanded action against the seniors.

On 13 February 2024, members of the UDF including INC MLAs took out a protest march to the Forest Minister's residence in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) demanding his resignation after a farmer was attacked and killed by a wild elephant in Padamala village in Wayanad. The protesters said that the government was not taking any measures to stop wild animal attacks.

Around 13 February 2024 (as reported), residents staged a protest in the Nallagandla locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against the constant noise due to the various ongoing residential and commercial projects in the area.

On 13 February 2024, hundreds of INC members led by MLA and former MLA staged a protest march to the collector's office in Bundi city (Rajasthan) in support of farmers. Police used water cannons to disperse the protesters and briefly detained the MLAs along with several other party members.

On 13 February 2024, about 30 people as a part of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey) staged a protest march from Delhi Bypass Road to the Mini Secretariat in Rohtak city (Uttar Pradesh) against the BJP-led central and state governments over various issues including corruption, communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption. The Yatra which began from Bengaluru city was initiated by RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization) on 10 December 2023, and is scheduled to conclude in New Delhi on 3 March 2024 - likely to pass through 80 districts across 13 states.

On 13 February 2024, Civil Police Officer (CPO) rank holders of the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) launched a protest in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) demanding the LDF-led state government to extend the validity of the CPO rank list which was going to expire next month.

On 13 February 2024, the Revolutionary Workers' Party of India (RWPI) led 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra', a protest march, reached Jaipur city (Rajasthan) over several issues such as price rise, Agniveer scheme and labor rights, etc.

On 14 February 2024, members of the Maratha community and local organizations staged impromptu shutdowns (bandh) and held protests in several parts of Maharashtra (coded to Mumbai city, Mumbai Suburban) as the health of Maratha Shivba Sanghatana leader worsened on the 5th day of hunger strike demanding reservations.

On 14 February 2024, the CPI-ML MLAs of the party led by their legislature party leader held a protest procession in Patna city (Bihar) against the conviction of party's MLA from Agiaon in a murder case.

On 14 February 2024, employees of the Gujarat Secretariat Staff Association and the Gujarat Forest Department held a protest in Gandhinagar city (Gujarat) demanding the reinstatement of the old pension system. The office bearers of the secretariat association also submitted a memorandum to the government.

On 14 February 2024, a large number of BJYM members held a candlelight protest march at Kishtwar city (J&K) on the anniversary of Pulwama attack against the killing of CRPF personnel by JeM militants in 2019 (coded separately) and against Pakistan over support for militants.

On 14 February 2024, locals (likely tribal based on action) held a protest march at Sandeshkhali town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) to demand the arrest of TMC leaders over claimed land encroachment and sexual harassment and assault of predominantly Tribal women. On 14 February 2024, JKNPP members held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) against the municipal corporation over increasing garbage collection tax and claimed corruption.

On 14 February 2024, locals held a protest at Gharkote town (Baramulla district, J&K) to demand repair of a road claimed to be in poor condition leading to a road accident.

On 14 February 2024, members of the AIMC staged a protest in Erode city (Tamil Nadu) against the BJP-led Union government for an increase in the prices of essential commodities. On 14 February 2024, over 300 impaired students staged a protest in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to provide them employment opportunities. The police detained the protesters. Five protesters also continued their hunger strike for the third day.

The protesters questioned whether the university was an educational or a religious institution.

On 14 February 2024, tribals affiliated to the Andhra Pradesh Adivasi Girijana Sangham (Adivasi Tribal Association of Andhra Pradesh) staged a protest at the zilla parishad meeting hall in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding the authorities to provide them with basic amenities including electricity, water, education and roads. On 14 February 2024, over 50 members of the VCK and residents staged a road block protest in front of the district police office in Erode city (Tamil Nadu) against the police for not arresting those who had demolished a temple in Surampatti two months ago (coded separately). On 14 February 2024, members of the SFI staged black flag protests in three locations in Thrissur city (Kerala) against the Kerala Governor while he was on his way to attend a convocation ceremony. The police detained 44 protesters.

On 14 February 2024, residents marked the 50th day of protests at the Coromandel fertilizer plant in the Ennore locality in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the permanent closure of the plant following an ammonia gas leak at the plant in December which led to the hospitalisation of 56 people.

On 1 March 2024, hundreds of people including traders, former panches (village government heads) led by JKAP members including trade wing and OBC wing leaders held a protest at Vijaypur city (Samba district, J&K) to demand restoration of statehood, holding of assembly elections in J&K and to demand release of pending funds for displaced Kashmiris.

On 1 March 2024, members of the IYC and the KSU staged protests in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) demanding action against the accused after a student at the College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences in Pookode died by suicide after being bullied (coded separately). The protesters demanded action against the accused.

On 1 March 2024, members of the IYC and the KSU staged protests in Wayanad district (coded to Kalpetta city, Kerala) demanding action against the accused after a student at the College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences in Pookode died by suicide after being bullied (coded separately). The protesters demanded action against the accused.

On 1 March 2024, villagers staged a protest in Ukkirankottai village (Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu) after unidentified assailants threw petrol bombs and set fire to a freedom fighter's banner in the village (coded separately). The protesters demanded action against the accused.

On 1 March 2024, a BJYM leader and his associates were suspected of hurling derogatory religious remarks and assaulting a man (likely from the Christian community based on the issue), and another person who had come to his rescue, at Rajpur Colony along Tajpur Road in Ludhiana city (Punjab) in a suspected attempt to prevent the construction of a church in the area.
On 1 March 2024, several unidentified persons assaulted a Bajrang Dal member in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) for unknown reasons.

On 1 March 2024, four persons from Muslim community assaulted a 65-year-old Hindu man with a knife at Silkuwa town in Kukshi tehsil (Dhar, Madhya Pradesh) over a dispute over temple repairs. The Hindu man was injured.

On 1 March 2024, family members of a liquor smuggler assaulted 2 policemen, with iron pipes, rods, and sharp weapons, in Umri Kalan village (Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh) when the policemen arrived in the area to investigate the sale of illegal liquor in the area. Both the policemen suffered injuries.

On 1 March 2024, Kashmiri and Punjabi students clashed using stones and bricks at the CT Institute near Shahpur village (Jalandhar, Punjab) over a dispute regarding the suspected molestation of a female student from the Kashmiri community by some Punjabi youths. A video of the incident was circulated online, and communal slogans were also suspected to have been raised during the incident.

On 1 March 2024, members of Bajrang Dal held a sit-in protest outside the Ratibad Police station in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) demanding action against police personnel responsible for the assault on their group member (coded separately). The police booked six of their compatriots and several Bajrang Dal members in the case.

On 1 March 2024, members and leaders of the BJP and ABVP, led by its state vice president (former state minister), staged a protest march from the Una Resthouse to the Municipal Park in Una town (Himachal Pradesh) demanding the resignation of the West Bengal Chief Minister (TMC) over the Sandeshkali (a village in West Bengal) issue in which TMC members and local politicians were suspected of sexually assaulting several women and seizing land illegally. The protesters also demanded the enforcement of the President's rule in the West Bengal state - claiming the deterioration of security. ABVP members also burned effigies near the Mini secretariat.

On 1 March 2024, members of farmer bodies and the Khap panchayat (local community organizations) staged a dharna (sit-in protest) near National Highway 152D next to Charkhi Dadri city (Haryana) against the state government's decision to cancel the passports of farmers taking part in the 'Delhi Chalo', protests called by SKM (Non Political) and KMM, along the Punjab-Haryana border areas.

On 1 March 2024, ASHA workers staged a dharna (sit-in protest) in Karnal city (Haryana) demanding the provision of benefits and salaries on par with government employees - including retirement benefits, insurance, and increased salaries. The police prevented the protesters from marching towards the Chief Minister's camp office.

On 1 March 2024, several contractual workers gathered under the banner of the Theka Mulazam Sangharsh Morcha (Contractual Workers Struggle Front) and staged a protest along the Jail Road in Mohali city (SAS Nagar, Punjab) demanding regularization and the provision of salaries based on the 15th Pay Commission.

On 1 March 2024, milkmen staged protests along Bauner Mor (Turn), and the Agra and Mathura Roads in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) condemning the reduction in the prices of milk being procured from milkmen. The protesters prevented the supply of milk into the city.

On 1 March 2024, outsourced employees staged a protest march at the Government Multi Specialty Hospital (GMSH) in Chandigarh city demanding regularization and the disbursal of salaries on the 7th day of every month.

On 1 March 2024, local people and family members of the missing girl gathered in large numbers and staged a protest along the Khanna-Malerkotla Road in Isru village (Ludhiana, Punjab) against the police whom the protesters accused of failing to take action in the case of a missing girl.

On 1 March 2024, family members of the deceased and the injured staged a protest and placed the deceased's body outside the police station in Barla village (Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected replacement of the tractor-trolley which had hit and killed a bike-borne man and injured another who was riding pillion.

On 1 March 2024, members of the Rashtriya Prajapati Mahasabha (Kumhar/Prajapati Caste Group) staged a demonstration, pelted stones, and damaged police cars at the Sahibabad Industrial area in Ghaziabad city (Uttar Pradesh) when the police stopped the demonstrators from continuing their Sankalp Yatra (Resolution March) from Haridwar to Delhi demanding for reservation as SC and greater representation in politics. The police lathi-charged, seized vehicles, and detained 13 people. Many people suffered injuries.

On 1 March 2024, Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) employees affiliated to the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike Officers and Employees Welfare Association staged a protest at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) demanding the INC-led state government to fulfil their demands including the filling up of vacancies. The protesters also demanded the authorities to stop harassing BBMP employees.

On 1 March 2024, a large number of YSRCP members who were supporters of an MLA staged a protest at a former TDP MLA's residence in Anaparthi town (East Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) accusing the MLA of being corrupt. Members of the TDP staged a counter protest, and the police detained the TDP MLA and dispersed the two groups.

On 1 March 2024, several farmers under the banner of J&K Farmer movement and Bharat Kissan Union held a sit-in protest at Miran Sahib city (Jammu district, J&K) over being evicted from their agricultural lands and claimed that J&K administration had illegally declared their lands as state property, and demanded restoration of article 370. The sit-in has been ongoing as of 23 March 2024.

Around 2 March 2024 (as reported), locals staged a protest with placards at Bagachang village along the Assam-Arunachal border in Biswanath district (coded to Biswanath town, Biswanath, Assam) over authorities' ignorance regarding issues including roads, transport, lack of safe drinking water and other development related issues. Protesters threatened boycott of Lok Sabha elections if their issues were not addressed.

On 2 March 2024, members of the Bank Employees Federation of India (BEFI) staged a protest at the Dharna Chowk in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the YSRCP-led state government to stop outsourcing public sector work to private companies and to recruit people. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest and also demanded the withdrwal of the new pension scheme and other benefits.
Around 2 March 2024 (as reported), a group of residents held a protest at Buhipora town (Kupwara district, J&K) against the power department over failing to repair an electric pole.

On 2 March 2024, members of the BJYM staged a silent protest outside Rameshwaram Cafe in the Rajajinagar locality in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) condemning the IED blast at the cafe the previous day by an unidentified assailant in which nine people were injured (coded separately). The protesters condemned the failure of the INC-led state government to prevent the incident.

On 2 March 2024, members of the BJP including a member of the Udupi City Municipal Council along with members of the All India Fishermen's Association took out a protest march from Malpe to the BJP office in Kadiyali in Mangaluru city (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) demanding the BJP leader to not issue a ticket to the the incumbent MP for Udupi-Chikkamagaluru to contest from Udupi in the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. The protesters demanded that a former MLA or a local be given the ticket to contest instead of an outsider.

On 2 March 2024, opposition councillors including members of the UDF and the AIMC staged protests in front of the Kochi corporation office in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the failure of the authorities to address the issues concerning the waste collection and treatment facilities at the Brahmapuram plant. The protesters also marked the one year anniversary of a major fire at the Brahmapuram plant.

On 2 March 2024, a section of government employees including the Kerala Private School Teachers Association, a Secretariat Action Council representing Opposition unions and an INC MLA took out protest marches in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) against LDF-led state government for the delay in the disbursing their salaries.

On 2 March 2024, hundreds of protesters including UCM members staged a sit-in protest with placards in front of the UCM office at Lamphelpat in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning the vandalism and arson of UCM's office amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 2 March 2024, a large crowd with black flags protested outside Melli police station in Melli town (South Sikkim, Sikkim) demanding the arrest of those responsible for the attack of an SDF leader (coded separately).

On 2 March 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu Land Survey Officials Association staged a protest at the Madukkur police station in Madukkur town (Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu) demanding the arrest of a person who attacked a survery and Village Administrative Officer when they were measuring land in Periyakottai village.

On 2 March 2024, members of the INC took out a protest march to the Kerala Veterinary and Animal Husbandry University in Pookode village (Wayanad, Kerala) after a student at the College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences in Pookode died by suicide after being bullied (coded separately). The protesters accused the police of being biased towards the accused. The police stopped the protesters from entering the campus, however no further information on the kind of police intervention.

On 2 March 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu branch of the Indian Association of Physiotherapy (IAP) staged a protest in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) objecting to physiotherapists being called 'technicians' in the gazette of the State Allied and Healthcare Professionals Council (SAHPC). The protesters also demanded a minimum salary and other benefits.

On 2 March 2024, locals along with a DMK panchayat member staged a protest and 'seized' a bus belonging to the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation Ltd (TNSTC) in Thirumalayampalayam town (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu) against the irregular bus service in the area. The protesters said that everyone was getting affected due to the uncertain bus schedule, and the DMK member accused the officials of creating difficulties on purpose to show the DMK-led state government in a negative light.

On 2 March 2024, a family held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) against the illegal sale of liquor in front of their house by another family. In response the other family armed with a gun and a rod assaulted two brothers who were part of the protest.

text: On 2 March 2024, DYFI members held a demonstration and clashed with police at Basirhat town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) against the TMC-led state government in West Bengal to demand the arrest of TMC leaders over claimed land encroachment and sexual harassment and assault of predominantly Tribal women in Sandeshkhali.

On 2 March 2024, about 24 ABVP members staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Mini secretariat in Una town (Himachal Pradesh) against the First Information Report (FIR) registered against some ABVP members for staging a protest and burning effigies on 1 March (coded separately) - over the Sandeshkali (a village in West Bengal) issue in which TMC members and local politicians were suspected of sexually assaulting several women and seizing land illegally.

On 2 March 2024, a BJP MLA and his associates staged a dharna (sit-in protest) at the LRP police station in Lakhimpur city (Kheri, Uttar Pradesh) demanding the release of 4 young people (affiliated with the BJP party) who were detained for assaulting two other people earlier in the night.

On 2 March 2024, laborers and farmers under the banner of Sanjha Mazdoor Morcha (a group of farm laborers unions) including the Mazdoor Mukti Morcha, Zamin Prapati Sangharsh Committee, Krantikari Pendu Mazdoor Union, and Punjab Khet Mazdoor Union, staged a dharna (sit-in protest) in front of the residence of an AAP State minister in Dirba village (Sangrur, Punjab) demanding the state government to fulfill its promise to provide old age pension and other demands including waiver of loans for farmers and laborers, guaranteed permanent employment for laborers, and provision of education and health services.. The protesters also condemned the excessive police intervention in the ongoing 'Delhi Chalo' farmer's protest, led by SKM (non political) and KMM.

On 2 March 2024, farmers and laborers under the banner of Sanjha Mazdoor Morcha (a group of farm laborers unions) and BKMU staged protests outside the residences of State ministers and MLAs across 13 districts in the Punjab state (coded as Chandigarh city) over various demands including waiver of loans for farmers and laborers, guaranteed permanent employment for laborers, and provision of education and health services.

Similar protests were held in 13 districts of Punjab.

Similar protests were held in 13 districts of Punjab.
On 2 March 2024, members of INC held protests across Chhattisgarh state (coded to Raipur city) against rising inflation in essential items.
On 2 March 2024, members of INC led by Bastar MP held a protest in Raipur city (Chhattisgarh) against rising inflation in essential items.

On 2 March 2024, unemployed people gathered under the banner of the Uttarakhand Unemployed Union and staged a protest at Kanak Chowk in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) against the non-fulfillment of their demands (likely the provision of jobs, based on the context). The protesters argued with the police when they were stopped from marching towards the Chief minister's residence.

On 2 March 2024, evicted Divyang (physically disabled) street vendors held a dharna (sit-in protest) in front of the Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation (BMC) office in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) demanding their rehabilitation in a vending zone. They later submitted a memorandum to the commissioner.

On 2 March 2024, lawyers staged a protest, and burned a symbolic pyre of the police, at the District court in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a lawyer who fell from his apartment during a police raid.

On 2 March 2024, locals, after a fatal accident, held a roadblock protest on Patnagarh-Bolangir road near Ulba village (Balangir, Odisha) demanding the arrest of the accused car driver and adequate compensation to the deceased's next of kin.

On 2 March 2024, a large number of BJP functionaries from the Zaheerabad Lok Sabha constituency staged a protest at the state headquarters in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the BJP leadership not to allot a ticket to a former BRS MP to contest from the Zaheerabad constituency for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. The protesters raised slogans against the former BRS MP and asked that the ticket be given to another BJP member.

Around 2 March 2024 (between 2 - 3 March) as reported, farmers staged a protest in Hosadurga town (Chitradurga, Karnataka) against the INC-led state government for not taking measures to address the water shortage in the area. The protesters also demanded the BJP-led Union government to declare the Upper Bhadra scheme a national project and provide relief funds.

Around 2 March 2024 (as reported), parents staged a protest at the Mandal Parishad Primary School in the 25th ward in Ponnur town (Guntur, Andhra Pradesh) against a teacher's inappropriate behaviour towards the students at the school.

On 3 March 2024, ABVP members held a protest by burning an effigy at Port Blair city (South Andaman district, A&NI) against the TMC-led state government in West Bengal to demand the arrest of TMC leaders over claimed land encroachment and sexual harassment and assault of predominantly Tribal women in Sandeshkhali.

On 3 March 2024, around 1500 members of the YSRCP staged a protest march at the camp office in Kakinada city (East Godavari. Andhra Pradesh) in support of a YSRCP member. The protesters raised slogans in support of the YSRCP member.

On 3 March 2024, members of the Andhra Pradesh Unemployed Joint Action Committee (JAC) staged a protest in Avanigadda town (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) as part of the 'Odarpu Yatra' undertaken to highlight the situation of unemployed youth in the state. The protesters held placards demanded the YSRCP-led state government to fill vacancies through the District Selection Committee exams.

On 3 March 2024, members of the Visakha Ukku Parirakshana Porata Committee (Visakha Steel Conservation Struggle Committee) along with members of political parties including the CPI(M), the JSP and a Mayor belonging to the YSRCP took out a 'Maha Padayatra' protest march from Kurmannapalem to the GVMC statue in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) to mark 1,116 days of protest against the sale of the RINL-Visakhapatnam Steel Plant by the BJP-led Union government.

On 3 March 2024, a number of locals (likely Hindu community based on the context) held a protest march and blocked a road at Jammu city (J&K) over the killing of a cow in Jammu which they claimed was sacrilegious act (coded separately).

On 3 March 2024, an ongoing sit by farmers was joined by DAP leader at Miran Sahib city (Jammu district, J&K) over fertile land being allocated for construction of police station and headquarters and demanded a reversal of the decision.

On 3 March 2024, three members of the BJP assaulted a former BJP member at the BJP office in the Powdikonam locality in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) for a social media post crticising the BJP's selection of a candidate from the Thiruvananthapuram constituency for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. The assailants hit the former BJP member with wooden logs by forcefully keeping his arms on a table.

On 3 March 2024, Imphal Pangei Road Development Committee staged a sit-in protest at Khurai Puthiba Leikai in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning the government for ignoring the poor road conditions from Lamlong bridge to Pangei.

On 3 March 2024, womenfolk staged a sit-in protest in front of the Macha Leima school gate in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning the vandalism and arson of UCM's office, Macha Leima school and finance office amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 3 March 2024, over 200 residents staged a protest by forming a human chain in the Besant Nagar locality in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) in solidarity with the residents of Ennore who have been protesting outside the Coromandel International fertilizer manufacturing unit after an ammonia gas leak on 26 December 2023 resulted in many people getting hospitalised. The protesters also marked the 68th day of the ongoing protest.
Around 3 March 2024 (as reported), locals staged a protest in the North Chennai area in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) against the bad condition of roads and the development work in the area.

On 3 March 2024, unidentified persons suspected to be BJP members based on TMC claim lobbed bombs (likely crude) at the house of a TMC panchayat (village government) in Burirhat village (Cooch Behar district, WB). The gate of the house was damaged but there were no casualties.

On 3 March 2024, BJP OBC unit members held a protest by burning an effigy at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) to demand death penalty for TMC leaders over claimed land encroachment and sexual harassment and assault of predominantly Tribal women in Sandeshkhali.

On 3 March 2024, supporters of a local BJP leader clashed physically as well as with firearms with other BJP members in front of the party office in Gwalior city (Madhya Pradesh) after a dispute between two groups over welcoming a leader turned violent. One person was injured in the clash. Police seized an illegal pistol from the site.

On 3 March 2024, two communities (Patel and Khalasi) clashed at Garas Faliya under Surat city (Gujarat) after an objection from the members of one community against the songs played during a marriage procession snowballed into a clash. The incident left at least five persons injured and many vehicles damaged. Police arrested 39 persons.

On 3 March 2024, scores of farmers from various villages gathered under the banner of AIKS and staged a protest march protest from Mansarovar Park to the Deputy Commissioner's office in Rohtak city (Haryana) demanding compensation for crop loss due to the heavy rains, hail storms, and strong winds.

On 3 March 2024, farmers arrived on 100 tractor-trolleys and staged a protest in Mohna village (Faridabad, Haryana) demanding the provision of an access point or an interchange to the Greenfield Expressway. The protesters canceled their plans to protest along the expressway after heavy police deployment in the area. The protesters have been staging a sit-in protest for over four and a half months.

On 3 March 2024, hundreds of people and members of the Sakal Hindu Samaj, along with a BJP MLA, held the Hindu Jan Aakrosh Morcha, a protest rally, from Gate 8 to Gate 1 in Malwani in Malad city (coded to Mumbai Suburban - Borivali, Maharashtra) demanding laws against religious conversions, and 'love jihad'.

On 3 March 2024, locals, after a road accident involving a 'Mo Bus', held a protest and blocked the Bhubaneswar-Puri road near Garage Chhak in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) demanding strict action against the driver.
On 3 March 2024, lawyers staged a protest, raising slogans, outside the Mangalam apartment in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a lawyer who fell from his apartment during a police raid.

Around 3 March 2024 (as reported), members of the transgender community (LGBTQ+) gathered in large numbers and staged a protest at the police station in Mursan town (Hathras, Uttar Pradesh) against the assault on a member of the transgender community in Karil village on 28 February (coded separately).

On 3 March 2024, tribals & farmers under the aegis of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) held a protest outside the district collectorate in Nashik city (Maharashtra) over various demands including sanctioning more land under the Forest Rights Act, conversion of non-cultivable to cultivable land, etc.

Around 3 March 2024 (as reported), local people staged a protest along the Lahartara-BHU Road in Varanasi city (Uttar Pradesh) against the demolishment of encroachments in the area by the Public Works Department (PWD) for a road widening project. The protesters claimed that they were not compensated for the demolition of their property.

Around 3 March 2024, over 100 Anganwadi workers from various states, staged a protest, as a part of the 'Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra' (Public Rights Journey), in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) against the BJP-led central and state governments over various issues including corruption, communalism, unemployment, inflation, exploitation of the poor, and corruption, and also demanded access to pensions, government employee status, payment of arrears, and minimum salaries. The Yatra which began in Bengaluru city was initiated by RWPI, the Disha Students' Organization, and the Bigul Mazdoor Dasta (labor organization) on 10 December 2023, and passed through 80 districts across 13 states. The police were suspected of detaining protesters, seizing buses, and lathi-charging protesters (at Bawani Industrial Area) in an attempt to prevent them from gathering at Jantar Mantar.

On 3 March 2024, women blocked the road, vandalized, and set ablaze an illicit liquor shop at Badakhiri village in Nischintakoili tehsil (Cuttack, Odisha) during a demonstration against the illegal sale of liquor in their locality.

On 3 March 2024, locals assaulted a group of transgender persons at the Shivaji Park in Tandur town (Vikarabad, Telangana) suspecting them to be child kidnappers. The transgender persons where walking around seeking donations when they were assaulted.

On 3 March 2024, villagers staged a protest during the gram sabha (village meeting) in Sancordem village (South Goa, Goa) demanding the administration to take measures to supply drinking water in the village. The protesters also condemned the sarpanch (village head) for not attending the meeting.

Around 3 March 2024 (as reported), members of the Shadow Council for Madgaon staged a protest in Margao city (South Goa, Goa) against the administration for digging up a newly tarred road to install a sewage pipeline. The protesters highlighted that it was a waste of public money and condemned the irresponsible behaviour of the government.

On 4 March 2024, members of the Andhra Pradesh Velugu Village Organisation Assistants (VOA) Employees Association along with members of the CITU staged a protest at the Gandhi Statue in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding the cancellation of a government circular which announced the termination of an their services when an employee completed 45 years of age. The protesters also demanded the implementation of an HR policy, insurance, uniforms and identity cards.

On 4 March 2024, employees of the Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) staged a protest in Mentada village (Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for not taking measures to improve the PACS and for not making it as efficient and reliable as the cooperative banks in the state.

On 4 March 2024, employees of the Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) launched protests in all 94 societies located in different mandals of Vizianagaram district (coded to Vizianagaram city, Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for not taking measures to improve the PACS and for not making it as efficient and reliable as the cooperative banks in the state.

On 4 March 2024, around 30 people attacked 5 students of St Stephen's High School while they were on their way home after their HSLC examination in Tinsukia district (coded to Tinsukia town, Tinsukia, Assam) over unknown reasons. All 5 students were injured while 3 sustained serious injuries and were taken to Tinsukia Civil Hospital.
On 4 March 2024, a large number of water department workers held a protest amidst an ongoing sit-in at Jammu city (J&K) to demand release of their pending wages and regularization of their services.

On 4 March 2024, scores of Kashmiri Sikhs, Pandits and Muslims from Pakistan administered Kashmir led by AKMMC members held a protest march at Jammu city (J&K) for immediate release of cash relief to the Kashmiri migrants including Muslims, Sikhs and Pandits which had been suspended on verbal orders.

On 4 March 2024, an ongoing sit by farmers was joined by Kissan Tehreek leaders (a local farmer group) who also held a protest march at Miran Sahib city (Jammu district, J&K) over fertile land being allocated for construction of police station and headquarters and demanded a reversal of the decision.

On 4 March 2024, senior citizens staged protests in the district and taluk headquarters in Bagalkote district (coded to Bagalkot city, Karnataka) with a list of demands including a special card for senior citizens, a monthly pension amount of 10000 rupeees and a special law to protect the rights of senior citizens.

The police arrested the accused.

On 24 March 2024, local residents and members of the Omaxe Resident Welfare Association (ORWA) staged a protest in Mullanpur Garibdass town (SAS Nagar, Punjab) demanding better water supply, road maintenance, and waste management in the area.

On 24 March 2024, relatives of Jaipur factory fire victims held a protest and blocked the Agra- Jaipur National Highway at Bassi town (Jaipur, Rajasthan) demanding the arrest of the owner of the factory and compensation for the deceased. The protest ended when officials assured the relatives of action on their demands following the rules.

On 24 March 2024, unidentified persons assaulted a team from the fire department in Sandwa Sombansian village (Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh) when the team arrived in the area to douse the flames at a nearby forest. The police arrested 6 people and seized a gun, cartridges, axes, and other sharp-edged weapons. Police stated that the attack took place over an old dispute.

On 24 March 2024, a group of rioters (likely Muslim based on the reason for violence) clashed with a group of tribal women in the Chengicherla locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) over the installation of speakers to play music while the namaz (Muslim prayer) was going on. The rioters pelted stones at each other and five persons sustained head injuries while a few others received minor injuries.

On 25 March 2024, a large number of members of the AIADMK and the BJP including a Union minister clashed with each other near the District Collectorate in Udhagamandalam city (The Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu) when the AIADMK candidate and the BJP candidate arrived at the Collectorate to file their nomination papers to contest in the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. Both the groups resorted to sloganeering and then clashed with each other. Members of both groups sustained injuries. Police resorted to a baton charge.

On 25 March 2024, BJP and TMC members clashed with each other at Kumirmari city (South 24 Parganas district, WB) over the hoisting of party flags ahead of the general elections. At least five persons including one TMC member were left injured in the clash. Although police registered a case of an old rivalry over a land dispute, locals claimed it was a clash over flags. Police later arrested two persons. TMC claimed BJP members used firearms.

On 25 March 2024, members of the JD(S) including an MLA and the BJP clashed with each other during a joint coordination meeting in Turuvekere town (Tumakuru, Karnataka) after the JD(S) MLA accused a BJP leader of being responsible for his defeat in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. The two groups clashed with each other following this argument.

On 25 March 2024, TMC and ISF members clashed with each other at Jirangachha Bagan Aait village in Bhangar town (South 24 Parganas district, WB) over wall graffiti ahead of the general elections. At least five persons were left injured in the clash. Four persons were later arrested by the police.

On 25 March 2024, locals chased a pick-up van, assaulted the driver, and set the van on fire at Rajganj city (Jalpaiguri district, WB) over a road accident in which a minor died. 2 police personnel were injured trying to control the mob.

On 25 March 2024, members of the BJP staged protests in the Yelahanka locality in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the BJP's decision to allot a ticket to a former minister from the Chikkaballapur assembly constituency for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. The protesters demanded the BJP to allot a ticket to the son of an MLA. The protesters held placards to mark their protest.

On 25 March 2024, members of the CPI(M) including the Chief Minister took out a protest rally and staged a protest in Manchikkal junction in Malappuram city (Kerala) against the BJP-led Union government for implementing the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). The protesters also accused the RSS of treating Muslims as 'second-class citizens' and condemned the INC for not organising protests against the CAA.
On 25 March 2024, power department employees held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) to demand reinstatement of suspended colleagues.

On 25 March 2024, 5000 people from the Ladakhi community under the banner of Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance joined a hunger strike 'climate fast' by a prominent individual at Leh city (Ladakh) to demand statehood for Ladakh, constitutional safeguards, recruitment, job reservation for the youth of Ladakh UT and creation of two separate constituencies for Leh and Kargil.

On 25 March 2024, a student, his parents and members of the SFI staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Haveri city (Karnataka) against the school headmaster of the Government High School of Haranagiri in Ranbennur taluk for not allowing him to write the Secondary School Leaving Certificate (SSLC) examination. The protesters said that the student could not attend classes due to ill health and that the headmaster had denied him a hall ticket to write his exams. The protesters wrote a mock exam to mark their protest.

On 25 March 2024, TDP members staged a protest in Y. Ramavaram village (East Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the TDP leadership to allot a ticket to a former TDP MLA to contest from the Anaparthi constituency in the upcoming Lok Sabha elections instead of giving the ticket to the BJP as part of a TDP-JSP-BJP alliance.

On 25 March 2024, residents of Tirthahalli taluk staged a protest in Heggodu village (Shivamogga, Karnataka) against a multi-crore multi-village water scheme proposed by the government under the Jal Jeevan Mission. The protesters celebrated Holi (Hindu festival) and burned an effigy representing 'bad politics' to mark their protest.

Around 25 March 2024 (as reported), locals staged a protest in front of the Kerala Water Authority (KWA) office in the Karuvelipady locality in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) demanding the authorities to ensure a regular supply of water.

On 25 March 2024, members of Assam AAP staged a sit in protest and burned the effigy of Prime Minister in front of AAP's headquarter at Ganeshguri in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) against the arrest of Delhi's CM by Enforcement Directorate and demanded his unconditional release.

On 25 March 2024, members of AAP, including an AAP MLA staged a protest in front of the Mandawali police station in the Delhi - Patparganj area (East Delhi, Delhi) demanding strict action against the person accused of having raped a minor girl on 23 March. The accused was arrested by the police.

On 25 March 2024, RSS and ABVP members engaged in a physical scuffle with NEHU Students' Union (NEHUSU) at North-Eastern Hill University (NEHU)'s campus in Shillong city (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) over Holi (Hindu festival) celebrations organized by the World Organisation of Students and Youth (WOSY) resulting in the injury of NEHUSU's Vice President. NEHUSU claimed that they were assaulted by around 200 people when they prevented the 2 groups from celebrating Holi citing the prohibition of political gatherings and festivities. ABVP and WOSY claimed that ABVP were invited for the Holi event and NEHUSU instigated the altercation.

On 25 March 2024, around 15-20 young people (likely Hindu based on context), armed with sticks, swords, and axes, assaulted local people, including shopkeepers, and vandalized houses, at Gaushala Mohalla (locality) in Sirsa city (Haryana) over a dispute regarding the application of colors on children during a Holi (Hindu religious festival) celebration. 10 people were injured.

On 25 March 2024, two groups of people (likely Hindu based on the context) clashed - where one group also opened fire - at the Bannadevi area in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) over a dispute related to dancing during simultaneous Holi (Hindu religious festival) celebrations. Around 4 people were injured including one with serious head injuries and another with bullet injuries. One person was arrested by the police.

On 25 March 2024, two groups of people (likely Hindu based on the context) clashed, opened fire, and pelted stones at each other in Katakbara village (Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh) over a dispute regarding the playing of drums and music (by the disc jockey) during simultaneous Holi (Hindu religious festival) celebrations. 4 people were injured including one with bullet injuries.

On 25 March 2024, members of the Hindu community staged a protest at the Bhangeri Mahavatpur area in Roorkee city (Haridwar, Uttarakhand) against the cremation of a woman, whose son had recently converted to Christianity from Hinduism.

On 25 March 2024, members of the Muslim community held a protest near the Markazi Masjid mosque in Majalgaon town (Beed, Maharashtra) against the unidentified person (likely Hindu based on the details) wrote Shri Ram (hail lord Ram), a Hindu religious slogan, on the wall of the mosque and seeking action against the accused.

On 25 March 2024, a group of young people from the Muslim community assaulted and pelted stones at a group of people, including a family, celebrating Holi (Hindu tradition) at the Idgah Kutlupur area in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) in a suspected case of communal violence. The assailants were also suspected of raising pro-Pakistan slogans. A video of the incident was circulated online and 11 people were arrested by the police.

On 25 March 2024, IDPs of Silsako staged a sit in protest with anti eviction placards at Chachal in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) demanding compensation and rehabilitation from the state government. Protesters conveyed their grievances and expressed that they had been protesting for more than one and a half year.

On 25 March 2024, a group of women, during Holi celebrations, assaulted, stripped, and paraded a Scheduled Caste (SC) woman at Bachhoda village of Gautampura police station area (Indore, Madhya Pradesh) over a past dispute.

On 25 March 2024, a group of people from a family staged a protest in front of the Chief Minister's house 2 in Shyamla Hills Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh), claiming that police 'delayed registration of an FIR' in an assault case. They scuffled with the police when the latter tried to remove them from the site.

On 25 March 2024, members of two groups clashed, during Holi celebrations, at Bhogada village under Tigiria police limits in Athagarh town (Cuttack, Odisha) for political rivalry and previous enmity. Five persons, including the sarpanch's (village government head) husband, were injured. A platoon of police force was deployed to control the situation.

The police resorted to a lathi (baton) charge to disperse the protesters.

On 26 March 2024, members of the BJYM staged a protest and attempted to 'lay siege' to a Minister's residence in Karatagi town (Koppal, Karnataka) against the remarks made by the minister against the supporters of the Prime Minister. The protesters demanded the Chief Minister to take action against the minister for his objectionable speech. The police stopped the protesters from entering the minister's house.

On 26 March 2024, farmers from Mallepalli and Pochammavada staged a rasta roko (road block) protest on the Manthani-Godavarikhani main road near Mallepalli village in Manthani town (Peddapalli, Telangana) demanding the officials to take measures to prove water to irrigate their standing crops through the SRSP canal. On 26 March 2024, members of AAP, led by its state joint secretary, staged a protest, raising slogans, in front of a BJP MLA's office in Panipat city (Haryana) condemning the arrest of the Chief Minister of Delhi (AAP national convener) by the Enforcement Directorate on 21 March (coded separately). The police detained 150-200 protesters when they attempted to march towards the Prime Minister's (BJP) residence. The protesters accused the police of using force. Police were also suspected of assaulting journalists covering the protest, one of whom sustained a fracture in his hand.

On 26 March 2024, around 700 members of the BJP, led by its Delhi president, staged a protest march, carrying placards and raising slogans, from Feroz Shah Kotla to the Secretariat in Delhi - Darya Ganj (Central Delhi, Delhi) demanding the resignation of the Chief Minister of Delhi (AAP national convener) who was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate on 21 March (coded separately) over his suspected involvement in a money laundering case linked to excise policy. Around 57 protesters including the BJP Delhi president were detained by the police.

On 26 March 2024, members of IYC and NSUI staged a protest outside the Himachal Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (HPTDC) restaurant at the Ridge Maidan (field) area in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) against a BJP candidate for the upcoming Lok Sabha (lower house of parliament) elections and a BJP MP during a BJP media event.

On 26 March 2024, KSU, Achik NEHU Students' Union, Naga Post Graduate Students' Coordination Committee, All Mizo Post Graduate Students' Union, NEHU Manipuri Students' Union and Arunachal Students' Association staged a protest and burned copies of CAA at North Eastern Hill University (NEHU) in Shillong city (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) condemning the implementation of Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA).

On 26 March 2024, nearly 230 employees went on strike and staged a protest outside the Haryana State Cooperative Supply and Marketing Federation Limited (HAFED) in Panchkula city (Haryana) against the non-fulfillment of their demands which included addressing the issues with the online transfer policy, revocation of charges levied on employees for delay in documentation, and implementation of a cashless medical policy.

On 26 March 2024, local people and traders staged a dharna (sit-in protest) in Rohtak city (Haryana) demanding action against the accused who demolished two shops and the staircase of an adjoining house along the Railway Road earlier in the day (coded separately).

On 26 March 2024, local traders under the banner of the trade board staged a protest in Dharchula town (Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand) against the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) whom the protesters accused of harassing traders during luggage checking at the Nepal and India border. Local businessmen and SSB personnel had clashed over the same issue on 25 March (coded separately)

On 26 March 2024, North Eastern Hill University Student Union (NEHUSU) staged a protest in their campus at Shillong city (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) condemning the clash between ABVP and RSS members with NEHUSU members on 25 March (coded separately).

On 26 March 2024, students (likely including Dalit students based on the context) under the banner of Social Justice Forum staged a sit-in protest, and raised slogans condemning the Hindu upper caste, at Ashoka University in Sonipat city (Haryana) over various demands including the implementation of a caste census at the university, reservation for students from marginalized communities, strict action against the use of hate slogans against lower-caste and marginalized communities, and creation of an annual event titled 'Ambedkar (a Dalit champion) Memorial lecture'. A video of the protest was circulated online.

On 26 March 2024, a mob physically assaulted a Nepali citizen, injuring her along with 3 police personnel who attempted to rescue her, in Haflong town (Dima Hasao, Assam) over suspicions of child lifting. The attacked individual was taken to Haflong Civil Hospital for treatment while a policeman was taken to Guwahati Medical College and Hospital (GMCH). Police forces arrested 7 people till date.

On 26 March 2024, locals and relatives set ablaze a liquor shop in the Jalgaon area under the jurisdiction of the Panagar police station (Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh) after the rape and murder of a minor by inebriated persons.

On 26 March 2024, hundreds of supporters of a potential BJP candidate held a protest outside the party office in Modasa town (Aravali district, Gujarat), opposing the withdrawal of his Lok Sabha candidature from Sabarkantha seat.

On 26 March 2024, 150 local people from 7 villages staged a dharna (sit-in protest), raising slogans, in front of the divisional office of the Executive Engineer (Hydropower department) in Jawali town (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) against the lack of consistent water supply in their areas.

On 26 March 2024, family members of a deceased army man staged a protest along the Nurpur Bedi-Anandpur Sahib Road near Nurpur Bedi village (Rupnagar, Punjab) demanding an investigation into the suicide of the army man, claiming the possibility of foul play in his death. The protesters refused to accept the deceased's body.

Around 26 March 2024 (as reported), a mob attacked 4 individuals including a BJYM member during a celebration at Aurobindo Sangh club in Kashipur, Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) over occupation of the club. The injured claimed that the mob attempted to illegally occupy the club and they had gone to investigate when they were attacked.

Around 26 March 2024 (as reported), locals staged a road block protest and blocked a national highway in Baikhora village (South Tripura, Tripura) after a Tripura State Rifle personnel was suspected of assaulting a civilian who had assisted in transporting another local involved in a road accident. Protesters highlighted the inefficiency of police forces especially the Officer in Charge (OC) who they claimed was also involved in extortion.

On 26 March 2024, hundreds of farmers held a sit-in protest at the dried-up Krishna Canal in Sangli district (Maharashtra) against the state government's apathy towards releasing water into the canal passing through 54 villages of Walva, Palus, and Tasgaon talukas of the district.

On 26 March 2024, members of the BJP-MM and the BJP staged protests in the Chengicherla locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the police to take action against those responsible for the attack on women belonging to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) group for playing music during Holi (Hindu festival) celebrations while the namaz (Muslim prayer) was going on (coded separately).

Around 27 March 2024 (as reported), a group of persons (likely Hindu and affiliated to the Bajrang Dal based on the complaint) assaulted a man (likely Muslim based on the reason behind the attack) in the Charminar area in Hyderabad city (Telangana) for being with a woman belonging a different religious community (likely Hindu based on the reason behind the attack). The rioters caught hold of the man, asked for his details and beat him up. A Bajrang Dal member registered a complaint with the police and the incident was circulated on social media.
Around 27 March 2024 (as reported), BJP members assaulted a TMC member at Chhota Molla Khali area (South 24 Parganas district, WB) ahead of the general elections.

On 27 March 2024, four rioters belonging to the RSS assaulted a DYFI member at the Kamukinkuzhy junction in Kilimanoor town (Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala) over an argument about the placement of posters for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. The DYFI member sustained serious head injuries as well as injuries on his hand. One RSS member was later arrested by the police.

On 27 March 2024, members of the SFI and the ABVP, RSS clashed with each other at the Government Industrial Training Institute (ITI) in Chandanathope town (Kollam, Kerala) after the NDA candidate for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections from the Kollam constituency arrived at the institute as part of his election campaign.
Around 27 March 2024 (as reported), TMC members assaulted BJP supporters at Padmashibpur area (coded as Kolkata city (WB)) as claimed by BJP ahead of the general elections.

BJP claimed that TMC initiated the attack and vandalised their houses and a few motorcycles. At least three persons were left injured in the clash.

On 27 March 2024, TMC and BJP members clashed with each other and vandalised vehicles, houses at Pipla village in Harischandrapur tehsil (Maldah district, WB) over political rivalry ahead of the general elections. The protesters attempted to meet the Chief Secretary to lodge a complaint against an officer who they said had pressurised the deceased to focus on his work.

On 10 May 2024, villagers clashed with a group of seven forest officials in Tungeda village (Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, Telangana) when the forest officials attempted to stop the villagers from occupying forest land. The two groups argued with each other following which the villagers assaulted the forest officials using sticks and axes. The forest officials sustained injuries and the police arrived to disperse the two groups.

On 10 May 2024, members of the Andhra Pradesh Nirudyoga Joint Action Council (unemployment group) staged a protest in the Dwarakanagar locality in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for failing to conduct the Andhra Pradesh (AP) District Selection Committee (DSC) examinations to provide employment to youngsters. The protesters extended its support to the TDP-JSP-BJP alliance for the upcoming state assembly elections.

text: On 10 May 2024, 39 farmers affiliated to the Desiya Thenindiya Nadhigal Innaippu Vivasayigal Sangam (National South Indian River Link Farmers Association) staged a protest in Viluppuram town (Viluppuram, Tamil Nadu) against the railway authorities for not attaching an additional coach to allow the protesters to travel to Varanasi to contest against Prime Minister in the Lok Sabha elections. The Government Railway Police officials and RPF personnel deboarded and detained the protesters at Chengalpattu citing that they had only waitlisted tickets.

On 10 May 2024, family members of a deceased watchman held a protest by blocking a highway at Hiranagar city (Kathua district, J&K) demanding an investigation into his death, which they claimed was a murder.

On 10 May 2024, Nagaland BJP staged a protest rally with placards at Old Daily Market in Dimapur city (Dimapur, Nagaland) condemning the remarks made by the chairman of the Indian Overseas Congress citing racism. The chairman compared South Indians as resembling Africans, West Indians as Arabs, East Indians as Chinese and North Indians as Whites while talking about diversity and democracy of the nation during an interview.

On 10 May 2024, the members of the students wing of AJSU-P gheraoed (surrounded) the Ranchi University (RU) administrative building and held a dharna (sit-in protest) in Ranchi city (Jharkhand), demanding resumption of admission in the intermediate section of constituent colleges of the university.

On 10 May 2024, 3-4 unidentified persons tore the posters of BJP, vandalized the campaign vehicle of LJP (Ram Vilas) and assaulted and injured the driver in Raja Pakar area (Vaishali district, Bihar), over political rivalry during the Lok Sabha elections. They also warned the LJP (RV) and BJP supporters against entering their area for campaigning.

On 10 May 2024, the former president of Murgud town council and Kolhapur district of Balasahebanchi Shiv Sena president and his two supporters assaulted a journalist in Murgud town (Kolhapur, Maharashtra) over his reporting.

On 10 May 2024, some unidentified assailants, including farmers, pelted stones at the convoy of a JJP nominee (sitting MLA) for the Lok Sabha elections in Rojkhera village (Jind, Haryana) in a suspected case of violence motivated by political rivalry, which a JJP leader claimed was carried out by suspected INC members - which the INC party has denied. 6 people were injured and a vehicle was damaged.

On 10 May 2024, local people assaulted 2 policemen (on duty), with sticks and iron rods, at the Kasim Vihar Bangla Basti area in Loni town (Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh) after the arrest of a man over charges of selling illegal drugs. The 2 policemen suffered severe injuries. 17 people were arrested.

On 10 May 2024, members of ABVP, including its metropolitan president, staged a protest at Our Lady Fatima School in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a student who committed suicide - which the protesters claimed was caused by the stress of studies and harassment of students under the guise of discipline.

On 10 May 2024, two groups of lawyers got into an altercation, involving manhandling, at the Fast Track Court of civil judge (senior division) in Varanasi city (Uttar Pradesh) over a dispute regarding the date of the next hearing related to the Gyanvapi case (case involves Hindus claiming that the Mosque is the property of a Hindu idol).

On 10 May 2024, farmers, including the BKU (Ekta Dakaunda Dhaner) state general secretary, staged a protest in Ferozepur city (Ferozepore, Punjab) against a BJP nominee (former state minister) for the Lok Sabha elections. The BKU leader was arrested on 11 May - including over his involvement in older protest events.

On 10 May 2024, 30-40 local people, including members of farmer's organizations, staged a protest, raising black flags, in Amarpur village (Palwal, Haryana) during the visit of a BJP nominee (state minister) for the Lok Sabha elections. The protesters have been demanding the provision of an access point to the upcoming Faridabad- Jewar Airport expressway.

On 10 May 2024, workers staged a protest outside the Ultra track Cement Factory in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) over various demands including dust-protection gear, 30-day salary payment, and rehiring of workers who were dismissed earlier, among others.

On 10 May 2024, around 100 labourers staged a protest at Pathini tea garden under Patharkandi circle (coded to Patharkandhi township, Karimganj, Assam) against the declaration of a sudden suspension of operation in the tea garden. The garden manager left the area and left labourers with unpaid wages for a week after he was assaulted by unidentified assailants.

Around 10 May 2024 (as reported), employees of Krishi Vigyan Kendras under Assam Agricultural University (AAU) staged a sit in protest at Assam Agricultural University in Jorhat town (Jorhat, Assam) against Indian Council for Agricultural Research (ICAR) and Assam Agricultural University (AAU) for the abrupt withdrawal of the employer's contribution to National Pension Scheme (NPS) and non-implementation of ROP & Service Regulations.

On 10 May 2024, members of All Assam Tea Tribes Student Association (ATTSA) staged a road block protest and blocked NH-32 in Digboi town (Tinsukia, Assam) against the sexual assault of a girl from the tea tribe community in Borjan locality. Protesters also gave a 24 hour ultimatum to Digboi police to arrest all the people involved.

On 10 May 2024, local people, including female farmers, staged a protest, raising black flags and slogans, in Majra village (Hisar, Haryana) during the campaign visit of a JJP nominee (sitting MLA) for the Lok Sabha elections. The protesters condemned the remarks made by the JJP leader's husband against the farmer's protest movement.

On 10 May 2024, members of the INC staged a protest in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against a BJP leader and lawyer for resorting to 'blackmail politics' in connection with a sexual harassment case involving a JD(S) MP, and after a woman filed a sexual harassment complaint against the BJP leader. The protesters demanded the police to arrest the JD(S) leader.

On 10 May 2024, members of the Kerala Motor Driving School Instructors and Workers Association staged a protest at the Muttathara testing centre in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) against the new driving test reforms introduced by the LDF-led state government. The protesters blocked the entry to the driving test centre by lying on the ground.

On 10 May 2024, members of the Kerala Motor Driving School Instructors and Workers Association staged protests in many parts of Kerala state (coded to Thiruvananthapuram) against the new driving test reforms introduced by the LDF-led state government.

On 10 May 2024, members of the Kerala Motor Driving School Instructors and Workers Association staged a protest in the Athani locality in Thrissur city (Kerala) against the new driving test reforms introduced by the LDF-led state government. The protesters dug a grave on the test ground to mark their protest.

On 10 May 2024, members of the Kerala Motor Driving School Instructors and Workers Association staged a protest in Thamarassery town (Kozhikode, Kerala) against the new driving test reforms introduced by the LDF-led state government. The protesters made porridge at the test venue to mark their protest.

On 10 May 2024, members of the INC and the BRS including a Corporator clashed with each other in the Vengalrao Nagar locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) while both groups were campaigning for the Lok Sabha elections. The INC members damaged the windscreen of the BRS Corporator's car. Police dispersed both the groups.
On 10 May 2024, locals held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) over sewerage water being drained into Devika river and demanded action on the lapse.

On 10 May 2024, 56 ward attenders and group 'D' workers under the aegis of the AICCTU, staged a protest for the third day at the Victoria Hospital in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) after their contracts were terminated in an arbitrary manner despite working at the hospital for 10-25 years. The protesters also highlighted the non-payment of their salaries for over two months. Police detained several workers and five members of the AICCTU.

On 10 May 2024, members of the TDP assaulted members of the YSRCP including an MLA in Nuzvid city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) when the YSRCP members and TDP members were participating campaigning in the same area for the upcoming state assembly and Lok Sabha elections. The two groups argued with each other leading to a clash, and a YSRCP member sustained injuries.

On 11 May 2024, forest department officials assaulted men, women and children from 15 non-tribal landless families in Pekucharra forest area (North Tripura, Tripura) to force them out of the makeshift shelters constructed on reserved forest areas (coded separately) as a part of an eviction drive.

On 11 May 2024, overnight, a mob of villagers physically assaulted a group of around 50 men at Ga Dhowa Sar (Badamar Sar) under Mangaldai police station limits (coded to Mangaldai town, Darrang, Assam) after they stole money from another villager. One of the men succumbed to his injuries and died at Mangaldai Civil Hospital.

On 11 May 2024, local villagers, mostly women, marched to district headquarters in Bijapur town (Chhattisgarh), during a protest claiming that the clash which took place a day earlier (coded separately) was a fake encounter and the individuals killed were innocent villagers.

On 11 May 2024, scores of people, including sarpanches (village chiefs), Khap leaders (local community leaders), ASHA workers, female wrestlers, and farmers and AIKS leaders, staged a protest march on tractors through nearly 30 villages under the Badhra tehsil (Bhiwani, Haryana) condemning the BJP and the JJP for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protest and for failing to address their demands. The protesters declared that they would vote against BJP and JJP nominees for the Lok Sabha elections and showed their support for the INDIA (an alliance of opposition parties) nominee.

On 11 May 2024, 15-20 students (likely from the Muslim community based on the issue) staged a protest and engaged in a scuffle (likely non-violent based on lack of injuries) with the university staff, raising slogans, at Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) condemning the removal of diniyat (study of religion) questions from the Indo-Islamic subject entrance examination and demanded it re-incorporation. The protesters accused the university security of intervening and misbehaving with the protesters when they attempted to meet the Vice-chancellor.

On 11 May 2024, members of the Mid-Day Meal Workers' Union, including the CITU district president, staged a protest in front of the District Administrative Complex (DAC) in Panchkula city (Haryana) demanding regularization of jobs and a minimum wage of 26000 rupees (monthly).

On 11 May 2024, farmers staged a protest, raising flags and slogans, in Jalalabad city (Fazilka, Punjab) during the visit of a BJP nominee (former state minister) for the Lok Sabha elections. Around 11 May 2024 (as reported), students gathered in huge numbers under the Sukhpura police station area (Ballia, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused who shot and injured a former student leader earlier in the day near Patkhauli Purab village (coded separately).
