On 11 May 2024, family members staged a protest at a hospital in Hapur city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against a man (advocate) whom the protesters accused of pushing an elderly man who fell and received head injuries - which led to his death.

On 11 May 2024, local people staged a protest at the Tehsil (local administrative unit) office in Multhan village (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) demanding compensation to residents for damages caused by the sudden water leakage at Multhan Hydro Project.

Around 11 May 2024 (as reported), residents held a protest meeting in Tirtol town (Jagatsinghapur, Odisha) against the incumbent BJD Jagatsinghpur Lok Sabha nominee over her lack of engagement with voters.

On 11 May 2024, farmers staged a protest along the Malout Road in Muktsar city (Sri Muktsar Sahib, Punjab) during the visit of a BJP nominee (former state minister) for the Lok Sabha elections. The police detained some protesters.

The protesters demanded the INC-led state government to build a tree park or a playground for children and preserve the environment.

On 11 May 2024, members of the Samastha Kerala Sunni Students Federation (SKSSF) and the Fraternity Movement staged protests in Malappuram city (Kerala) against the insufficient number of seats in higher education institutions in the Malabar districts. The protesters demanded the LDF-led state government to increase the number of seats.

On 11 May 2024, members of Hindu organisations including the VHP along with members of the JD(S) took out a protest march from the bus stand circle to police station in Mandya city (Karnataka) against the police for issuing show cause notices to a few members of Hindutva organisations for participating in the of Hanuman flag row protest in Keragodu in Mandya district (coded separately). On 11 May 2024, people and lawyers staged protests in several constituencies in West Godavari district (coded to Bhimavaram city, Andhra Pradesh) against the implementation of the Andhra Pradesh Land Titling Act, 2023. Protesters burned copies of the legislation to mark their protest.

On 11 May 2024, youth leaders belonging to the Veerashaiva Lingayat Samaj staged a protest near the railway station gate in Gulbarga city (Kalaburagi, Karnataka) condemning the desecration of a banner featuring the portrait of Basaveshwara (Indian philosopher and Lingayat social reformer) by unidentified miscreants for unknown reasons (coded separately). Protesters demanded the police to take action.

On 11 May 2024, members of the National Federation of Indian Women (NFIW), the women's wing of the CPI staged a protest in the Kuratheru locality in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against a Youtuber who had been arrested for making 'derogatory' remarks against women police personnel in an interview.
On 11 May 2024, Shiv Sena (UBT) faction members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against overcharging by liquor sellers and demanded cancellation of licenses of such sellers.

On 11 May 2024, members of various organisations including the Indian Christian Women's Movement, Dravidar Kazhagam (DK), Poovulangin Nanbargal (Friends of the Earth), AIDWA, the Neelam Cultural Centre, lawyers, journalists and members of the Church of South India (CSI) staged a protest and a candlelight vigil in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) to mark one year of the ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal communities in the state of Manipur. The protesters condemned the BJP-led Union and state governments for not taking action to stop human rights violations in the state.

On 11 May 2024, nearly 600 girl students staged a protest on the premise of Bangalore University's (BU) Jnana Bharathi campus in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the water shortage and frequent power outages in the hostel. The protesters held empty buckets and mugs to mark their protest.

On 11 May 2024, family members of a deceased minor girl held a protest at a local hospital in Budhal tehsil (Rajouri district, J&K) over her death due to a landslide claimed to have been caused by negligence of Shri Girraj Ji Infra Heights private limited company engaged for upgradation of Budhal-Mahore road.

On 11 May 2024, residents, relatives and family members of a mason who died in a traffic accident after his two-wheeler hit rocks that had been placed around drying paddy staged a protest on the Tiruvannamalai - Tindivanam High Road in in Kannakurkkai village (Tiruvannamalai, Tamil Nadu) demanding action against those who had left the paddy on the highway to dry.

On 11 May 2024, residents staged a protest on the Gudiyatham Main Road in Ullli village (Vellore, Tamil Nadu) demanding the panchayat (village government heads) officials to ensure a regular supply of water for household consumption after the wells and borewells in the village dried up.

On 11 May 2024, citizens and members of civil society organisations staged a '#GrowASpineOrResign' protest in front of the Karnataka Office of The Chief Electoral Officer in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) as part of a nationwide protest demanding the Election Commission of India to take action against the hate speech complaints against the Prime Minister and other violations by BJP leaders while campaigning for the Lok Sabha elections.

Around 11 May 2024 (as reported), residents staged a protest in the JJR Nagar locality in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) after their homes were inundated with sewage water after the recent rains. The protesters said that the officials were not taking action to solve the waterlogging issue in the area.

On 11 May 2024, dozens of villagers staged a protest in Narimanam village (Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu) demanding the Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd. (CPCL) to compensate them for the land that the company had acquired. The protesters blocked officials from conducting land survey work in the village and the police detained around a hundred protesters in Narimanam and Gopurajapuram villages.

(CPCL) to compensate them for the land that the company had acquired. (CPCL) to compensate them for the land that the company had acquired. The protesters blocked officials from conducting land survey work in the village and moved the survey stones. Police detained about a hundred demonstrators.

On 11 May 2024, members of the INC including an MLA, members of the IUML and the RMPI staged a protest in Vadakara town (Kozhikode, Kerala) against the LDF-led state government's communal campaigning during the Lok Sabha elections. The protesters said that the LDF was attempting to create a divide among the citizens.

On 11 May 2024, members of Shiv Sena (UBT) and Balasahebanchi Shiv Sena clashed and raised slogans for and against the incumbent Prime Minister in Aurangabad city (Maharashtra) when the participants of both the pre-election rallies converged at the same place. Both rallies were held before the last day of campaigning ahead of the fourth phase of the Lok Sabha elections.

On 12 May 2024, several hundred labourers of Doloo Tea Estate staged a protest rally and a meeting inside the tea estate near Silchar city (Cachar, Assam) demanding authorities to replant around 41 lakh-plus tea bushes uprooted between May 12 and 14 for the construction of the proposed Greenfield airport.

On 12 May 2024, members of the BJP were suspected of assaulting a man (journalist) during the rally of the Union Home Minister (BJP) in RaeBareli city (Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh) after the journalist questioned members of the BJP whether the women at the rally were paid to attend the event. The journalist had earlier interviewed many women at the rally - through whom he learned that they were paid to attend the event. The journalist was hospitalized due to injuries.
On 12 May 2024, supporters of BJP and MVA candidates clashed in Ahmednagar Lok Sabha constituency (Maharashtra) ahead of voting for the fourth phase of Lok Sabha elections.

On 12 May 2024, two men were killed in a clash with sticks and axes in Nazirabad village (Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh) over a land dispute over farming on government land. At least nine others were also severely injured.

On 12 May 2024, some members of SAD (B faction) were suspected of assaulting a member of SAD-A, with an iron rod, in Bassi Pathana city (Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab) while the SAD-A member was on a campaign visit for the Lok Sabha elections. The man suffered a head injury.

On 12 May 2024, local people assaulted a young man and paraded him - after shaving his head and making him wear a garland of shoes - under the Pachokhara police station area (Firozabad, Uttar Pradesh) over suspicions of the man's involvement in an illicit relationship with a woman from the village. A video of the incident was circulated online.

On 12 May 2024, local youths chased a car and vandalized it at Khamti ghat area of Dibrugarh (coded to Dibrugarh town, Assam) after they found a suspected stolen cow in the car. The suspected smugglers escaped.

On 12 May 2024, members of a family tied 2 Dalit men (laborers) to an electric pole and assaulted them, and hurled casteist slurs, in Bahrampur village (Agra, Uttar Pradesh) over a dispute regarding the removal of wires installed by the assailants on disputed land.

On 12 May 2024, farmers staged a protest in front of the police station in Sadiq village (Faridkot, Punjab) condemning the detention of the Kirti Kisan Union (KKU) state general secretary and two other farmer activists earlier in the morning for carrying out a protest at Bihle Wala village on 11 May (coded separately) - the police also accused the detainees of.threatening BJP leaders.

On 12 May 2024, farmers staged a protest in Anandpur Sahib city (Rupnagar, Punjab) condemning the BJP and local BJP leaders for the excessive intervention in the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protest and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

On 12 May 2024, local people, including Hindu priests, and members of the Panda (a learned Hindu devotee) community, staged a protest at the Shri Badrinath Dham (temple) in Badrinath town (Chamoli, Uttarakhand) against the VIP darshan (paying religious homage) system at the temple.

On 12 May 2024, local people, accompanied by an INC MLA, staged a protest at the police station in Bhagwanpur area (Haridwar, Uttarakhand) demanding action against the suspected kidnapping of a girl from Akbarpur Kalson village.

The protesters condemned the INC for not procuring paddy at the Minimum Support Price (MSP) and for failing to give the 500 rupees bonus that was promised to farmers before the state assembly elections.

On 16 May 2024, farmers staged a road block protest in Malkapet village (Rajanna Sircilla, Telangana) against the INC-led state government for not purchasing their paddy despite opening purchasing centres two months ago. The protesters demanded the authorities to procure their paddy.

On 16 May 2024, members of the INC and the MYL staged protests outside the Government Medical College Hospital in Kozhikode city (Kerala) against a doctor for accidentally operating on a patient's tongue instead of removing her sixth finger. The protesters demanded action against the doctor for medical negligence.

On 16 May 2024, members of the IYC staged a protest march to the Pantheerankavu police station in Pantheeramkavu town (Kozhikode, Kerala) demanding the police to arrest a man who was accused of domestic violence. The protesters said that the accused had left the country and attempted to break the barricades in front of the police station.

On 16 May 2024, members of several Muslim organisations staged a protest in Malappuram city (Kerala) against the decision to invite volunteers to supply food at the State Haj Camp in Karipur from only the Kerala Muslim Jamat and its subsidiary groups including the Sunni Yuvajana Sangam (SYS) and the Sunni Students Federation (SSF). The members questioned why their organisations were excluded.

On 16 May 2024, women held a protest at Battala area in Sandeshkhali area (North 24 Parganas district, WB) over the claimed attempt at sexual assault of a woman by suspected TMC supporters (coded separately) and demanded justice.

On 16 May 2024, over 50 women residents of Anna Nagar staged a protest at the Corporation premises in Hosur city (Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu) demanding the officials to transfer the Corporation Commissioner over the water crisis in the city. The protesters held empty water cans and raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 16 May 2024, locals including a large number of women held a protest at Salehar village (Jammu district, J&K) over the installation of smart power meters claiming they led to inflated power bills and against general inflation in essential items.
On 16 May 2024, locals held a protest at Sananghat village (Kathua district, J&K) against the groundwater department over lack of maintenance for two out of order handpumps leading to water scarcity.
On 16 May 2024, locals held a protest at Mandla village (Kathua district, J&K) against the groundwater department over lack of maintenance for out of order handpumps leading to water scarcity.

On 16 May 2024, hundreds of residents staged protests outside the office of the City Municipal Council and at the residence of the Deputy Commissioner in Raichur city (Karnataka) against the drinking water shortage in the city. The protesters demanded the officials to ensure a regular supply of water and held empty pots to mark their protest.

On 16 May 2024, residents launched a protest by organising a hunger strike in front of the Kerala Water Authority (KWA) office in Vengoor village (Ernakulam, Kerala) demanding action against the officials after a jaundice outbreak in the area. The protesters condemned the officials for not ensuring that the water supplied to the area was clean.

On 16 May 2024, scores of BJP members including an MLA staged a protest in Hubballi city (Dharwad, Karnataka) demanding the authorities to arrest and punish a man who was accused of murdering a girl for rejecting his romantic proposal. The protesters said that there was a 'breakdown of law and order' in Karnataka under the leadership of the INC-led state government. The police arrested the protesters.

On 16 May 2024, hundreds of students staged a protest on the hostel premises of a private engineering college in the Heelalige locality in Chandapura on the outskirts of Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the college authorities after a student died by suicide in her college hostel room. The protesters accused the authorities of not providing basic amenities.

On 16 May 2024, villagers (likley Hindu based on the reason of the protest) staged a protest in Anganathavalasai village (Tirupattur, Tamil Nadu) demanding the authorities to grant them permission to construct a compound wall for a temple that was situated on 'poramboke' (government owned) land. The protesters 'laid siege' to the officials' vehicles with the demand to measure the land to construct the wall.

On 16 May 2024, Patwaris (government registrars) staged an indefinite sit-in protest at the divisional office complex of the Canal Department in Abohar city (Fazilka, Punjab) against the AAP-led state government whom protesters accused of taking coercive action against Patwaris for refusing to issue false reports claiming that 100 percent of the canal water were supplied to villages at the furthest points.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Prison Guards
text: On 16 May 2024, eight prisoners staged a demonstration inside the Puzhal Central Prison in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) claiming that they were innocent and demanding the jail authorities to release them. The demonstrators raised slogans, broke tube lights and inflicted injuries on their bodies. The prison officials overpowered the demonstrators and brought the situation under control.

On 16 May 2024, Meira Paibi activists (women torch bearers) staged a protest in Waroiching village (Imphal West, Manipur) against the government's plan to replace Gorkha Rifles amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal communities in the state.
Around 16 May 2024 (as reported), five persons assaulted a man and called him 'gay' in the Vasant Valley area in Kalyan West (Thane, Maharashtra) over his Instagram post.

On 16 May 2024, members of the YSRCP staged a protest in front of the Pedavegi police station in Pedavegi village (West Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) after a former TDP MLA and his supporters forcibly took away a TDP member who was arrested in connection with a murder from the police station. The protesters demanded the police to arrest the accused within 24 hours.
On 16 May 2024, ZoRO organized a protest rally in Lunglei district (coded to Lunglei town, Mizoram) condemning the Central government's decision to scrap the Free Movement Regime (FMR).

On 17 May 2024, local residents and women staged a protest with banners in Mijikajan TE SSP village (Biswanath, Assam) against the construction of a school on a historically significant playground that had been a local centre for sports and recreational activities for generations.

On 17 May 2024, half a dozen panches (village government heads) and local councilors clashed with a contractor and his supporters in Pakwara village (Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh) over a dispute regarding the poor quality of the material used for the construction of a road.

On 17 May 2024, a few people assaulted the INC nominee (NSUI in-charge) for the Lok Sabha elections and a female AAP councilor near the Karte Nagar AAP office in the Delhi - Shahdara area (North East Delhi, Delhi) in a suspected case of politically motivated violence. The assailants also smeared black ink at the AAP leaders. A video of the incident was also circulated online.

Around 17 May 2024 (as reported), a BJP MLA and his supporters, marched and held a protest at the office of the superintendent of police (SP) in Agar city (Agar Malwa, Madhya Pradesh) after a claimed instance of corruption by policemen surfaced, demanding immediate action against accused, and restitution of the bribe amount. Two policemen were suspended after the protest.
On 17 May 2024, cotton farmers blocked the highway in front of the Krishi Mandi in Khargone city (Madhya Pradesh) over delay in the distribution of BT cotton seeds.

On 17 May 2024, students of Eureka Academy Thounaojam staged a protest march with placards and slogans in and around Thounaojam village (Kakching, Manipur) demanding Scheduled Tribe status for the Meitei community amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal communities in the state.

On 17 May 2024, members of the BJP-MM (women's wing), led by its state president, staged a protest near the Chief Minister's (AAP) residence in Delhi - Civil Lines (Central Delhi, Delhi) against the suspected assault on an AAP MP (former chairperson of Delhi commission for women) by the personal assistant of the Chief Minister on 13 May (coded separately). The protesters demanded the resignation of the Chief Minister.

On 17 May 2024, residents from the Sama and Alkapuri areas of the city staged a protest at the Sama sub-divisional offices of the Madhya Gujarat Power Company (MGVCL) in Vadodara city (Gujarat), demanding the removal of the new smart meters and the reinstallation of older models.
On 17 May 2024, locals of the Hazira area gathered outside the residence of the Energy Minister and held a protest in Gwalior city (Madhya Pradesh) over water shortage in their area.
On 17 May 2024, locals blocked roads and set alight a private school in Patna city (Bihar) during a demonstration after the dead body of a student was found.

On 17 May 2024, hundreds of members of the Malankara Syrian Knanaya Archdiocese including lay people, priests and bishops staged a protest at the Church headquarters in the Chingavanam locality in Kottayam city (Kerala) in support of a the Metropolitan (church head) who had been suspended by the Patriarch of Antioch for 'anti-Church activities'.

On 17 May 2024, employees of the Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd (RINL), members of the CITU and the JMS Union staged a protest in front of the executive director's office in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding the management to release their wages.

On 17 May 2024, farmers held a protest by padlocking the gates of the department handling the irrigation related facilities for Ravi and Tavi rivers at Hiranagar city (J&K) over lack of water for irrigation in their fields and demanded immediate cleaning of the rivers to ensure proper flow of water.

On 17 May 2024, dozens of farmers led by a former panch (village government head) held a protest at Logate town (Kathua district, J&K) over lack of water for irrigation in their fields and demanded immediate cleaning of the rivers to ensure proper flow of water.

On 17 May 2024, scores of workers of the Jindal Stainless Ltd (JSL) staged a protest at the company's Kottavalasa unit office in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the management's decision to close down the unit. The protesters wore black badges and raised slogans demanding the company to withdraw its decision.

On 17 May 2024, Ladakh Buddhist Association members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand statehood for Ladakh, constitutional safeguards, recruitment, job reservation for the youth of Ladakh UT and creation of two separate constituencies for Leh and Kargil.

On 17 May 2024, a group of women led by filmmaker under the banner of TMC teacher's wing held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) against the governor over claimed sexual harassment of a woman staffer at the governor's official residence.

On 17 May 2024, people staged protests in Dharwad city (Karnataka) demanding the authorities to arrest a man who was accused of murdering a girl for rejecting his romantic proposal. The protesters demanded a government job and compensation for the victim's family, and said that there was a 'breakdown of law and order' in Karnataka under the leadership of the INC-led state government.

On 17 May 2024, people staged protests in Belagavi city (Karnataka) demanding the authorities to arrest a man who was accused of murdering a girl for rejecting his romantic proposal. The protesters demanded a government job and compensation for the victim's family, and said that there was a 'breakdown of law and order' in Karnataka under the leadership of the INC-led state government.

On 17 May 2024, family members and relatives of a girl who died while undergoing a medical procedure to remove the plate implants in her leg staged a protest at the Corporate Orthopaedic (MJ Naidu) Hospital in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) accusing the doctors of medical negligence. The protesters demanded action against the doctors and the hospital management.

On 17 May 2024, three people intercepted, stripped, tied to a bike, and dragged a 60-year-old near Amrora village (Garhwa district, Jharkhand) over claimed involvement in cow smuggling. Police later arrested one of the accused.

On 17 May 2024, several men tied a Dalit couple to a pole, garlanded them with shoes, and assaulted them in Kilora village under Mungaoli police station limits (Ashok Nagar district, Madhya Pradesh) over the couple's son's involvement in a molestation incident a few months ago.

On 17 May 2024, villagers gathered, set alight a thatched structure, and ransacked the police station in Araria town (Bihar) after a 'couple' committed 'suicide' in police custody (coded separately). Three policemen were injured. Two civilians were injured in police firing.

On 17 May 2024, farmers staged a protest, raising slogans, in Balluana village (Bathinda, Punjab) against a BJP nominee (former state minister) for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been staging protests condemning the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

On 17 May 2024, local people, mostly from the Rai Sikh community, led by the president of Seed Farm Abadkar (settlers) Sangharsh Committee, staged a massive protest, raising slogans, at the Seed Farm area in Abohar city (Fazilka, Punjab) during the visit of a former INC MLA who arrived in support of the INC nominee (former MP) for the Lok Sabha elections. Protesters have been demanding fair compensation to local people and farmers for the land acquired by the state government for the development of a highway bypass under the Bharat Mala Project.

On 17 May 2024, family members of a man who died in a boar attack staged a protest in front of the Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences (MIMS) mortuary in Mandya city (Karnataka) demanding the INC-led state government to provide them a compensation amount of 25 lakh rupees, a government job and a monthly pension amount for his sick wife.

On 17 May 2024, members of the District Bar Association went on strike and staged a sit-in protest outside the Court complex in Amritsar city (Punjab) condemning the police for failing to take action against the accused involved in the assault on a lawyer and his wife.

On 17 May 2024, members of SKM, KKU, BKU (Doaba), and Jamhoori Kisan Sabha (farmer union) staged a protest, raising slogans, in Barian Kalan village (Hoshiarpur, Punjab) during the campaign visit of a BJP nominee for the Lok Sabha elections. The protesters condemned the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.
On 17 May 2024, Shiv Sena UBT faction members held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) to demand a total ban on liquor sale near religious places.

On 17 May 2024, students staged a protest at the PES University campus in the Chandapura locality in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) after a first-year student died by suicide at the college hostel. The protesters demanded an investigation into the incident.

On 17 May 2024, many students (12th standard) staged a protest at Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) against the school administration whom the protesters accused of giving lower marks and failing students. The protesters demanded a revaluation.

On 17 May 2024, members of the Tibetan community and Tibetan Women's Association staged a protest march, raising flags, from McLeodganj to Kacheri crossing in Dharamsala town (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) against the Chinese government whom the protesters accused of abducting and imprisoning the Panchen Lama (a Buddhist religious head) - including others - and demanded their release.
On 17 May 2024, residents under the banner of Downtown Coordination Committee held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) against inflated power bills and demanded relief.
Around 17 May 2024 (as reported), daily wage workers staged a protest in Ponda city (North Goa, Goa) demanding the Ponda Municipal Council to pay their pending wages.

On 17 May 2024, scores of local people staged a protest, raising slogans, staged a protest at the Shakti Nagar area in Dera Bassi city (SAS Nagar, Punjab) against the Municipal Council whom the protesters accused of failure to address the lack of water supply in the area.

On 17 May 2024, 2 groups of political party supporters (likely Shiv Sena (UBT) and BJP based on context) clashed at BJP office in the Mulund city (coded to Mumbai Suburban - Kurla, Maharashtra) during a demonstration by Shiv Sena (UBT) over claimed money distribution by BJP ahead of the fifth phase of Lok Sabha elections. Police arrested five Shiv Sena (UBT) members. Shiv Sena (UBT) members also pushed the policemen and tried to take away the seized cash.

On 17 May 2024, Sammilita Sanskritik Mancha, comprised of 32 socio-cultural organisations, organized a rally in Silchar city (Cachar, Assam) in remembrance of the 1961 language movement in Barak valley where several other protest demands were made. Members of an organization named Chorus raised pro-Palestine slogans, while other organization members demanded for the official recognition of Bhasa Sahid (language martyrs during the Bengali language movement of 1961 in Assam) and to make the report public, some condemned the National Register of Citizens (NRC) and over 100 workers of Doloo tea garden demanded for the return of their lands after Assam government evicted them to build an airport.

On 17 May 2024, farmers staged a protest and locked the Agriculture Sub-market in Athmakur (M) village (Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Telangana) against the officials for not procuring their paddy. The protesters said that they had been waiting for 40 days for the officials to buy their grains.

On 17 May 2024, farmers staged a protest in Ramayampet village (Medak, Telangana) demanding the officials to purchase their grain. The protesters accused the officials of negligence and said that they were being made to wait for many days at the purchase centres.

On 17 May 2024, farmers staged a protest in Papannapet village (Medak, Telangana) demanding the officials to purchase their grain. The protesters accused the officials of negligence and said that they were being made to wait for many days at the purchase centres.

On 17 May 2024, farmers staged a rasta roko (road block) protest in Bodmatpally village (Medak, Telangana) demanding the officials to purchase their grain. The protesters accused the officials of negligence and said that they were being made to wait for many days at the purchase centres.

On 17 May 2024, farmers staged a rasta roko (road block) protest on the Medak-Bodmatpally road in Minpur village in Papannapet mandal (Medak, Telangana) demanding the officials to purchase their grain. The protesters accused the officials of negligence and said that they were being made to wait for many days at the purchase centres.

On 18 May 2024, locals vandalised two vehicles and assaulted forest officers and the police at Nodhabari village near Belakoba forest range (coded as Belakoba city (Jalpaiguri district, WB)) when attempting to retrieve the body of a person killed in a wild elephant attack.

On 18 May 2024, hundreds of BJP members took out a march and staged a protest at the Hosamani Siddappa Circle in Haveri city (Karnataka) ) against the increasing cases of crimes against women in the state. The protesters condemned the breakdown of law and order in the state and demanded the home minister to resign.

On 18 May 2024, hundreds of BJP members, BJP-MM members and a former MLA staged a protest at the Chennamma Circle in Belagavi city (Karnataka) against the increasing cases of crimes against women in the state. The protesters condemned the breakdown of law and order in the state and raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 18 May 2024, members of the BJP Raitha Morcha (farmer's group) staged a protest outside of the new deputy commissioner's office in Siddhartha Nagar in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding the INC-led state government to dispose the drought relief funds released by the BJP-led Union government in an effective manner. The protesters also shouted slogans against the state government for not clearing the arrears due to the Farmer Producers Organization and for not giving incentives to milk producers.

On 18 May 2024, members of the BJP including an MLA staged a protest at the Belthangady police station in Belthangady town (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) against the arrest of the taluk BJYM president in connection with an illegal quarrying case.

On 18 May 2024, members of the BJP and members of the Basavajyoti Youth Foundation (Hindu group) staged a protest in Chikodi town (Belagavi, Karnataka) against the increasing cases of crimes against women in the state. The protesters condemned the breakdown of law and order in the state and raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 18 May 2024, clergy and believers of the Knanaya diocese staged a protest in Kottayam city (Kerala) against the Patriarch of Antioch's (church head) decision to suspend the Metropolitan of the Malankara Syrian Knanaya Archdiocese.

Around 18 May 2024 (as reported), farmers staged protests in Raikal village (Jagtial, Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to procure their paddy without any delay or restrictions. The protesters said that their produce which was stored at procurement centres were submerged in the water due to sudden rain.

Around 18 May 2024 (as reported), farmers staged protests in Konaraopet village (Rajanna Sircilla, Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to procure their paddy without any delay or restrictions. The protesters said that their produce which was stored at procurement centres were submerged in the water due to sudden rain.

On 18 May 2024, numerous farmers, villagers and a Deputy Sarpanch (village head) staged a protest in Loutolim village (South Goa, Goa) against the proposed Borim Bridge and bypass project. The protesters said that they will not give away their ancestral land for any government project.

On 18 May 2024, fisher sellers staged a protest on the Marina Loop Road in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) against the city corporation officials for damaging 10 shops while the officials were clearing encroachments on the footpath. The protesters demanded the officials to show them the official order and said that they had not received any prior notice.

On 18 May 2024, members of the IYC took out a protest march to the Chief Minister's residence in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) citing a breakdown of law and order in the state. The protesters cited the increasing cases of deaths due to criminal gangs and crimes against women. The protesters demanded the Chief Minister to resign and burned his effigy to mark their protest.

On 18 May 2024, hundreds of members of various communities and organisations including the Ambiger community, led by religious leaders, members of Gangamata community, members of the Koli and Sunagar communities, an INC municipal councillor, a Lingayat Panchamasali seer and others staged protests and took out a march in Hubballi city (Dharwad, Karnataka) condemning the killing of a young woman by a man for rejecting his romantic proposal. The protesters questioned why the INC-led state government was slow to take action and burned old tyres and formed a human chain to mark their protest.

On 18 May 2024, contractors of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) staged a protest at the Corporation's Head Office in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the administration to clear their pending bills. The protesters said that they would halt all monsoon-related civil works until they get paid.

On 18 May 2024, lawyers including members of the Central Bar Association went on a strike and staged a sit-in protest, raising slogans, along the Road outside the Collectorate in Shahjahanpur city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the arrest of the accused involved in the assault on the brother of a lawyer (over personal enmity).

On 18 May 2024, writers, activists, a poet, a senior lawyer, members of the KRRS, representatives of women, Dalit, farmers' and workers' organisations under the aegis of the Karnataka Rajya Janapara Chalavaligala Okkoota (Federation of Karnataka State People's Movements) staged a protest at the Mahaveera Circle in Hassan city (Karnataka) demanding the INC-led state government to arrest a JD(S) MP who was accused of sexually assaulting women and minor girls.
On 18 May 2024, a large number of women led by MSJK members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against poor supply of water and power in the Jammu region.

On 18 May 2024, nearly 100 people including students and family members staged a protest at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the suicide of four students at PES University in the last ten months. The protesters demanded the government to intervene and investigate the matter.

On 18 May 2024, members of the students' union staged a protest by entering the Vice-Chancellor's residence on the University of Hyderabad campus in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against the administration's order to hold the annual university festival after the university re-opened for the academic session instead of holding it during the vacation.

On 18 May 2024, the women of L.K. Nagar held a protest in Vadodara city (Gujarat) against high electricity bills from Madhya Gujarat Vij Corporation Limited (MGVCL)'s newly installed smart electricity meters.

On 18 May 2024, residents of Chasa Barabati village held a protest in Champeswar panchayat in Narasinghpur block (Cuttack, Odisha) against the BJD's incumbent MLA from Baramba seat over drinking water crisis.

On 18 May 2024, relatives of a murdered Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) leader held a sit-in protest in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh), demanding the arrest of the accused after unidentified persons stabbed and killed the divisional vice president of BJYM at the gate of Bhopal Central Jail (coded separately).

On 18 May 2024, the father of a baby who died during the delivery process along with family members staged a protest at the government hospital in Wardhannapet town (Warangal Rural, Telangana) accusing the hospital of medical negligence. The protesters said that the doctor on duty left the hospital and had instructed two nurses to perform the delivery by following instructions on the phone.

On 18 May 2024, a former BRS minister along with his brother-in-law and followers staged a protest in the Petbasheerabad locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against some individuals who they said was taking over land that belonged to them by erecting fences. The protesters agued with the police and removed the boundary fence. Police detained the protesters.

On 18 May 2024, hundreds of villagers vandalized the Kalinga Institute of Social Sciences (KISS) premises at Lunibahal village under the Harbhanga block (Boudh district, Odisha) during a demonstration over several issues including the construction of an illegal road encroaching upon pasture land, no employment to local youths and exploitation of tribal children in the name of admission to the institution.

On 18 May 2024, 6-7 people, including members of a family, tied a man with ropes and assaulted him to death at Uttam Nagar locality in the Delhi - Vikaspuri area (West Delhi, Delhi) over suspicions of stealing. The deceased's family members claimed the assailants ran a bike over the deceased's genitals and rubbed salt on his wounds. The police arrested 3 accused - including a minor.

On 18 May 2024, hundreds of AASU activists staged a road block protest near ONGC Colony Tinali in Sivasagar town (Sivasagar, Assam) against the poor condition of Bhuban Gogoi (BG) Road connecting Sivasagar and Nazira.

On 18 May 2024, Tripura BJP staged a protest march from their party office in Krishnanagar to other areas in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) condemning the opposition parties for their accusations against the BJP party. The protest was in response to the series of protest organized by CPI(M) and INC (coded separately).

On 18 May 2024, Tripura BJP staged protests across Tripura (coded to Agartala city, West Tripura, Tripura) condemning the opposition parties for their accusations against the BJP party. The protest was in response to the series of protest organized by CPI(M) and INC (coded separately).
On 18 May 2024, Tripura BJP staged a protest at BMS Maidan in Dharmanagar town (North Tripura, Tripura) blaming the opposition parties for obstructing development in Tripura.

On 18 May 2024, CPI(M) staged a protest march from Rabindra Murthy in Kabiguru Park to various locations and halted at the starting point in Khowai town (Khowai, Tripura) as a part of a week long protest demanding employment opportunities, food security, electricity infrastructure upgrades, teacher shortages, irrigation, housing, access to clean drinking water, and urgent repairs of deteriorating roads.

On 18 May 2024, CPI(M) and INC staged protests in different parts of Tripura (coded to Agartala city, West Tripura, Tripura) over unsatisfactory results of students from Vidyajyoti schools during the CBSE exams. Protesters accused the former CM and some education department officials of misappropriating funds under the Vidyajyoti scheme.

On 18 May 2024, farmers staged a road block protest and blocked the national highway in Baikhora village area (South Tripura, Tripura) against the Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) of Baikhora police station for his suspected extortion from farmers. Protesters lifted the blockade after the Officer-in-Charge (OC) assured prompt action against the ASI.

On 18 May 2024, Meira Paibi (women torch bearers) activists staged a protest with placards and slogans at Heirok Part II in Heirok village (Thoubal, Manipur) against murder charges against Periphery Protection Force (PPF)'s convener. Protesters demanded the removal of all charges.

On 18 May 2024, SFI and TSF staged a protest outside Siksha Bhawan in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) over unsatisfactory results of students from Vidyajyoti schools during the CBSE exams. Protesters held the former CM with some education department officials accountable for misappropriating funds under the Vidyajyoti scheme.

On 18 May 2024, Asom Sankhayalaghu Sangram Parishad (organization for the welfare of minority communities in Assam) staged a protest near Clock tower in Biswanath town (Biswanath, Assam) against the rise in prices. Police forces stopped protesters from burning the effigy of Food, Civil Supplies & Consumer Affairs Minister and seized it from them.

On 19 May 2024, BJD members assaulted BJP members at Betara Chhak under Bhanjanagar police limits (Ganjam district, Odisha) ahead of the fifth phase of Lok Sabha and state elections. Five BJP members were injured.

On 19 May 2024, a BJP councilor and his associates assaulted a tea stall vendor and his wife at the Sahibabad area in Ghaziabad city (Uttar Pradesh) over a dispute regarding payment for food items. The vendor and his wife also claimed that the assailants extorted money, vandalized their tea stall, and stole jewelry. The Councilor was later arrested.

On 19 May 2024, a suspected member of INC and his supporters assaulted a BJD member and his family at Mayabarha village under Sadar police limits (Balangir district, Odisha) ahead of the fifth phase of Lok Sabha and state assembly elections.

Around 19 May 2024 (as reported), a group of five to seven men (likely Muslims) assaulted a surveyor and school principal at Syed Sultan mosque in the Dariapur area of Ahmedabad city (Ahmadabad, Gujarat) for unknown reasons.

On 19 May 2024, five men from the Thakor community used caste-based slurs, assaulted three members of a Dalit family with sticks, and vandalized their car with sticks and stones in Hathnoli village under Nadiad (Kheda, Gujarat) for taking out a procession on the occasion of tonsuring ceremony.

On 19 May 2024, locals assaulted a 17-year-old accused at the site of a fatal accident in Pune city (Maharashtra) after he attempted to escape from the spot. The locals later handed him over to the police.

On 19 May 2024, two factions participating in a JKNC rally clashed with each other using sharp-edged weapons at Mendhar town (Poonch district, J&K) over an unspecified reason during the Lok Sabha elections. Three persons were left injured in the clash. Its unclear if the rioters were JKNC members.

On 19 May 2024, BJP and BJYM members held a protest at Shopian city (J&K) against the killing of a former BJP sarpanch (village government head) in Shopian (coded separately) claiming there was negligence in the security arrangements and the attack on a tourist couple by militants in Pahalgam (coded separately).

On 19 May 2024, BJP and BJYM members held a protest at Anantnag city (J&K) against the killing of a former BJP sarpanch (village government head) in Shopian (coded separately) claiming there was negligence in the security arrangements and the attack on a tourist couple by militants in Pahalgam (coded separately).

On 19 May 2024, hundreds of BJYM members held a protest by burning effigies at Kacchi Chavni area in Jammu city (J&K) against Pakistan over the killing of a former BJP sarpanch (village government head) in Shopian (coded separately) claiming there was negligence in the security arrangements and the attack on a tourist couple by militants in Pahalgam (coded separately).

On 19 May 2024, farmers staged a protest, raising slogans, in Jandwal village (Hoshiarpur, Punjab) during the visit of a BJP nominee for the Lok Sabha elections - who was accompanied by another BJP leader (former MLA). The protesters condemned the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

Around 19 May 2024 (as reported), members of BKU staged a protest in Amargarh city (Sangrur, Punjab) during the visit of a BJP nominee for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been staging protests condemning the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

On 19 May 2024, members of BKU (Ugrahan) staged a protest, raising black flags, in Khurd village (Sangrur, Punjab) during the visit of a BJP nominee (former MLA) for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been staging protests condemning the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

On 19 May 2024, members of the INC led by the leader of the opposition held a protest at Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC) in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the withdrawal of the increase in the rate of property tax in the city.

On 19 May 2024, resident doctors staged a protest outside of the vice chancellor at the Shri Guru Ram Rai Institute of Medical and Health Sciences in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) against the suicide of a student who the protesters claimed was pressurized and harassed by his professor.

On 19 May 2024, at least 300 people from Shirgao including devotees of the goddess Laira (Hindu deity) staged a protest on the Margao-Karwar highway and took out a protest march to the Bicholim police station in Bicholim city (North Goa, Goa) demanding the arrest of two woman social activists who were accused of hurting religious sentiments after they posted on social media saying that members of the temple management committee had harassed a woman over a property matter. The protesters accused the activists of hurting religious sentiments and demanded the police to arrest them.

On 19 May 2024, a large number of Hindu devotees (on a religious pilgrimage) staged a protest at the Chardham Yatra (Hindu religious pilgrimage) Transit Camp in Rishikesh city (Dehradun, Uttarakhand) and demanded the commencement of the temporary registration for the Chardham Yatra.
On 19 May 2024, shopkeepers held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) over frequent power cuts in the area and demanded consistent supply of power.

On 19 May 2024, farmers and members of BKU (Doaba, Qadian, and SBS), NBS, Dehati Mazdoor Sabha (farmer/labor union), and Jamhoori Kisan Sabha (farmer union) gathered under the call of SKM and staged a protest march to the venue of a BJP event in Phillaur town (Jalandhar, Punjab) during the visit of a BJP MP. The protesters condemned the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.
On 19 May 2024, local women staged a protest in Badethi village (Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand) demanding the closure of a liquor shop in the area.

On 19 May 2024, tribal woman of Ekkuvaguddi hamlet including a ward member staged a protest in Rompalle village (Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the Collector and the Integrated Tribal Development Project (ITDP) Project Officer to solve the water accessibility issues in the village. The protesters carried water containers on their heads to mark their protest.

On 19 May 2024, hundreds of locals gathered at the spot of the BJD-BJP clash and staged a road blockade on the Bhanjanagar-Dasapalla road Bhanjanagar police limits (Ganjam district, Odisha) in a protest demanding the arrest of the accused persons involved in the clash (coded separately).

On 19 May 2024, relatives, after a fatal accident, blocked the National Highway under the Civil Line police station area and held a protest in Morena city (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the arrest of the accused and demolition of their houses.

On 19 May 2024, villagers, after a cow carcass was found, blocked the main road and held a protest in Barotha village (Dewas, Madhya Pradesh) demanding the immediate arrest of other suspects and the demolition of their houses. Police had arrested one accused.

On 19 May 2024, some villagers laid pots, buckets, and utensils on the road and surrounded Biju Janata Dal (BJD) MLA candidate for the Baramba constituency for an hour at Manapur village (Cuttack, Odisha) during a protest over lack of drinking water.

On 19 May 2024, residents staged a road roko (block) protest on the Salem-Muthunaickenpatti road in Chellapillaikuttai village in Omalur taluka (Salem, Tamil Nadu) against the panchayat officials after a boy accidentally touched a switchboard while playing cricket with his friends on the street and was electrocuted. The protesters accused the officials of negligence for placing the switchboard at a lower level near an electric pole.

On 19 May 2024, residents staged a protest in the Penamaluru locality in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against the Penamaluru police for detaining a minor boy and taking him to the police station based on a complaint that he had hit a woman with a cricket ball while he was playing with other children at an apartment complex.

On 19 May 2024, hundreds of local people, including environmental activists, staged a protest at Khalanga Reserve Forest near Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) against the decision to install a water treatment plant in the reserve which would lead to the felling of thousands of trees.

On 19 May 2024, family members of the deceased staged a protest and placed the deceased's body outside the police station in the Sachendi area (Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused involved in the murder of a man who was killed for marrying a woman against the wishes of her family.

On 19 May 2024, members and leaders of AAP, including the Chief Minister (AAP national convener), 2 MPs (AAP), and 2 state ministers (AAP), staged a 'Jail Bharo' (occupy the jail) protest march toward the BJP headquarters in Delhi - Darya Ganj (Central Delhi, Delhi) against arrest of the personal assistant (aide) of the Chief Minister over the suspected assault on a female AAP MP on 13 May (coded separately). The protesters also condemned the BJP-led central government whom the protesters accused of targeting opposition parties. The police detained several protesters.

Around 19 May 2024 (as reported), members of Hindu Suraksha Dal staged a protest with banners, slogans and burned an effigy of West Bengal's CM at AOC point in Karimganj town (Karimganj, Assam) over her claimed disrespectful comments towards sadhus (Hindu holy persons) of Bharat Sevashram Sangha and the Maharajs of Ramakrishna Mission.

On 19 May 2024, Kakching Lamkhai Welfare Board (likely Meitei based on geography) staged a sit in protest with placards at Kakching Lamkhai in Kakching town (Kakching, Manipur) against the gun attack at a hotel (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal communities in the state. Shops in the locality were also closed from morning till dusk as a sign of protest.

On 19 May 2024, locals (likely Meitei based on protest demand), All Thanga Peoples' Organisation, Thanga Apunba Meira Paibi Lup (women torch bearers) and SC Girls' Hostel Thanga Wangma High School Relief Camp staged a sit in protest with placards at Thanga Khoirom Mandop in Thanga village (Bishnupur, Manipur) demanding Manipur government to provide assistance to a displaced person who was attacked on May 8 (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters also demanded justice for the victim.

On 19 May 2024, IDPs from Hiyangthang Kamakhya Pemton (KP) College relief camp (likely Meitei based on location) staged a sit in protest in the premises of their camp in Hiyangthang town (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding Manipur government to provide assistance to an IDP who was attacked by unidentified armed assailants (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters also demanded prompt justice for the victim.

On 19 May 2024, Assam WMC, Manipuri Basti Meira Paibi (Women Torch Bearers), Manipuri Rajbari Students' Union (MRSU), United Manipuri Association Assam (UMAA) and Achanba Lup (AL) staged a sit in protest at Manipuri Rajbari in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) demanding Scheduled Tribe (ST) status for the Meitei community in Assam amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal communities in the state.

On 19 May 2024, Khullem Leikai Meira Club (women torch bearers), Uripok Apunba Lup and Uripok Nupi Apunba Lup (all Meitei groups) staged a sit in protest at Khullem Leikai Meira Shang in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) against the attack on 3 labourers (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

Around 19 May 2024 (as reported), hundreds of people, mostly tribal women, staged a protest rally organized by Joint Action Committee Against Molestation (JACAM) along National Highway 102 in Senapati district (Senapati, Manipur) demanding justice for the sexual assault of a female student. Protesters lifted the blockade when the accused was arrested.

On 19 May 2024, family members of the deceased staged a protest along the road at the Uttam Nagar locality in the Delhi - Vikaspuri area (West Delhi, Delhi) demanding action against the accused who assaulted and killed a man over suspicions of stealing on 18 May (coded separately).

On 19 May 2024, members of the Satnami community (Dalit Caste group) held a protest and staged a roadblock in Manakoni village (Baloda Bazar, Chhattisgarh), demanding the arrest of perpetrators who vandalized religious symbols (Jait Kham) of the community on 15 May (coded separately).

On 20 May 2024, members of AAP were suspected of assaulting a female journalist and her cameraman at the AAP office in Delhi - New Delhi city (Delhi) after the journalist attempted to enter the AAP office for an interview. The journalist also claimed that AAP members broke the cable of the camera.

On 20 May 2024, members of the BJP and BJD clashed at the polling booth in Beruanbadi village under Bhanjanagar block (Ganjam district, Odisha) during the fifth phase of Lok Sabha and simultaneous state elections. BJD members attempted booth capturing but were stopped by BJP supporters leading to the clash. Police reached the spot and brought the situation under control. No casualties.

On 20 May 2024, members of the BJP clashed with SP members at a polling center in Sarai Holi village (Fatehpur, Uttar Pradesh) claiming that the members of other castes, besides the Yadav community, were stopped from casting votes for the Lok Sabha elections. Police dispersed the crowd.

On 20 May 2024, the nephew of a former Rajasthan minister and INC member along with supporters vandalized a club, and private vehicle and assaulted employees, including a Dalit, in Jaipur city (Rajasthan) for unknown reasons. The former minister has denied the involvement of his nephew.

On 20 May 2024, members of INC and BJP clashed during the voting in Little Angel School in Mumbai - Sion city (coded to Mumbai City, Maharashtra) during the fifth phase of Lok Sabha elections. No casualties.

On 20 May 2024, the RJD nominee for the Saran Lok Sabha seat was hackled and supporters (likely RJD and BJP) clashed in Chapra city (Saran, Bihar) during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. This triggered a fatal clash the next day (coded separately).

On 20 May 2024, suspected TMC supporters assaulted a BJP leader and his supporters outside a polling booth at Gayeshpur area (Nadia district, WB) in Bongaon constituency during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. They were left injured in the incident. BJP claimed TMC was trying to stop people from voting.

On 20 May 2024, TMC members assaulted some BJP members and stopped voters from voting at Amdanga town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. BJP members were left injured in the incident.

On 20 May 2024, BJP claimed that TMC assaulted their supporters and captured couple of booths in the Sasthitala area in Howrah district (coded as Amta city (Howrah district, WB)) during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. Two BJP supporters suffered head injuries.
On 20 May 2024, TMC and BJP members clashed with each other at Arambagh town (Hooghly district, WB) during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. One TMC member was killed in the clash.
On 20 May 2024, TMC and BJP members clashed with each other at Uluberia town (Howrah district, WB) during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. No casualties.
On 20 May 2024, TMC and BJP members clashed with each other at Howrah town (Howrah district, WB) during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. No casualties.

On 20 May 2024, TMC and BJP members engaged in a clash at Swarupnagar town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. Four BJP members were left injured in the clash.

On 20 May 2024, TMC and BJP members clashed with each other at Khanakul area (Hooghly district, WB) over polling booth agents being stopped from accessing the booths during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. Police also recovered two crude bombs in the area. A BJP panch (village government head) was left injured in the clash.
On 20 May 2024, TMC members engaged in a scuffle (likely violent) with CPI(M) members at Kardah town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections.

Around 20 May 2024 (as reported), villagers tonsured the head and assaulted a rape accused at a village under the Lalsot police station (Dausa district, Rajasthan) after he was caught sexually assaulting a disabled woman. The villagers later handed him over to the police.

text: On 20 May 2024, locals tied an ITBP soldier to the tree and assaulted him at Jangipara town (Hooghly district, WB) over claimed attempt at sexual assault of a woman in the same area (coded separately) during the Lok Sabha elections.

On 20 May 2024, a group of people killed an autorickshaw driver carrying voters to the polling booth in Sarsara village under Bargarh Sadar police limits (Odisha) over political rivalry, during the fifth phase of Lok Sabha and simultaneous state elections. Police claimed that the killing was non-political as opposed to the locals who did think it was political.

On 20 May 2024, members of the AAP staged a protest outside the Bangalore Development Authority's (BDA) Koramangala complex in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the BDA's decision evict traders from the complex and lease out properties to private developers for 65 years.

On 20 May 2024, members of AISA and other student organizations staged a protest in front of the Arts Faculty at Delhi University in Delhi - Civil Lines (Central Delhi, Delhi) condemning the university administration's police on mandatory attendance and hosting parent-teacher meetings (PTMs). The protesters also demanded the provision of admit cards for students who were debarred from examinations at Shaheed Bhagat Singh College.

On 20 May 2024, residents of Nadupat belonging to the Scheduled Caste (Arunthathiyar) (Dalit) community staged a protest at the Collectorate in Dindigul city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the authorities to arrest the upper caste assailants who had attacked and killed a Dalit man (coded separately) and charge them under the Goondas Act. The protesters also demanded the installation of closed-circuit television cameras in every street in the village, a full-time ration shop and housing schemes.
On 20 May 2024, locals led by a BJP leader held a protest at Kathua city (J&K) over supply of contaminated water in their area.

On 20 May 2024, members of the BJP including an MLA staged a protest in front of Vikasa Soudh in Belthangady town (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) against the arrest of the taluk BJYM president in connection with an illegal quarrying case.

On 20 May 2024, members of the CITU and the AITUC staged protests and superintendent engineer's cabin at the Kerala Water Authority (KWA) office in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against a French multinational company (MNC) called the Suez Group which had won the bid for a big drinking water supply project in the city. The protesters said that the company's business model would make drinking water expensive for citizens and raised slogans to mark their protest when the company's representative visited the KWA office.
On 20 May 2024, CPI(M) members held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over increase in power bills and demanded fair pricing for consumers.

On 20 May 2024, farmers staged protests in Karur district (Tamil Nadu) against the LDF-led Kerala government for constructing a check dam across the Silandhi river. The protesters said that the dam would obstruct the flow of water into the Amaravathi river in Tamil Nadu.

On 20 May 2024, farmers staged protests in Tiruppur district (Tamil Nadu) against the LDF-led Kerala government for constructing a check dam across the Silandhi river. The protesters said that the dam would obstruct the flow of water into the Amaravathi river in Tamil Nadu.

On 20 May 2024, members of the Akhila Bharatha Raitha Krishi Karmika Sanghatane (All India Farmers Agricultural Organization) staged a protest outside the office of the Nanjangud taluk administration in Nanjangud town (Mysuru, Karnataka) demanding the INC-led state government to distribute the drought relief funds released by the BJP-led Union government in an effective manner and to compensate farmers for the crop losses caused by the pre-monsoon rains.

On 20 May 2024, members of farmer unions staged a protest in Kheri Saffa village (Jind, Haryana) against a JJP nominee (MLA) for the Lok Sabha elections. The protesters condemned the JJP and the JJP nominee for failing to take action against the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

On 20 May 2024, farmers under the banner of BKU (Ekta Ugrahan) staged a protest, raising black flags and slogans, in Kokri Kalan village (Moga, Punjab) during the visit of a BJP nominee (MP) for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been staging protests against the BJP and its nominees condemning them for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

On 20 May 2024, medical employees staged a protest in Amritsar city (Punjab) against the assignment of election duties to a large number of medical employees including nurses and doctors - which the protesters claimed would hamper the provision of medical care to patients.

On 20 May 2024, doctors staged a protest, raising slogans, at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in Rishikesh city (Dehradun, Uttarakhand) demanding strict action against a nursing officer who sexually harassed a female doctor. The accused was suspended from his duties and arrested by the police on 23 May.

On 20 May 2024, 300 people from Shirgao including devotees of the goddess Laira (Hindu deity) took out a protest march to the Bicholim police station in Bicholim city (North Goa, Goa) demanding the arrest of a woman social activist who was accused of hurting religious sentiments after she posted a video referring to the devotees of Shree Devi Lairai (Hindu deity). The protesters demanded the police to arrest the activist.
On 20 May 2024, INC members held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) to demand police action over defacement of posters of an INC leader outside the party office (coded separately).

On 20 May 2024, local people and members of INC staged a protest, raising black flags and slogans, in Kaza town (Lahul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh) during the visit of a BJP nominee for the Lok Sabha elections - who was accompanied by other BJP leaders, including the BJP Leader of Opposition. The protesters condemned an old social media post on Dalai Lama (Buddhist religious head) posted by the BJP nominee on X (formerly Twitter) which the protesters claimed was derogatory. The BJP Leader of Opposition claimed that the protesters pelted stones which resulted in an injury - however, evidence regarding the same is awaited.

On 20 May 2024, a local INC MLA and a group of citizens held a sit-in protest at Yerwada police station in Pune city (Maharashtra) demanding accountability and fair treatment to victims of a fatal hit-and-run case involving a minor driving a Porsche in an inebriated state.

On 20 May 2024, INC members including elected ministers and former panches (village government heads) held a protest at Ranbir Singh Pura city (Jammu district, J&K) against power shortage and increases in electricity bills burdening the farmers.
On 20 May 2024, all Bengal Trinamool Railway Hawkers Union affiliated with INTTUC held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over claimed harassment of hawkers at the railway station.

On 20 May 2024, members of the JD(S) staged a protest in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the Deputy Chief Minister and a BJP leader for their suspected involvement in highlighting a case in which a JD(S) MP is accused of sexual harassment.

On 20 May 2024, cab drivers including members of the Ola Uber Drivers' and Owners' Association staged a protest at the Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the Bangalore International Airport Limited's (BIAL) decision to collect a fee from private and commercial vehicles entering the arrival area of KIA.

On 20 May 2024, 181 job aspirants from families who were evicted for the construction of the Vallarpadam container trans-shipment terminal, under the aegis of the Moolamppilly Coordination Committee (MCC) staged a protest in in front of the district collectorate in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) demanding the government to honour the promise of granting the evictees government jobs. The protesters submitted job applications to mark their protest.

On 20 May 2024, contractors of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) staged a protest at the Corporation's Head Office and other zonal and circle-level offices in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the administration to clear their pending bills. The protesters said that they would halt all monsoon-related civil works until they get paid.

On 20 May 2024, Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL) staged a protest in Ludhiana city (Punjab) demanding actions against the accused involved in the assault on PSPCL employees on 18 May (coded separately).

On 20 May 2024, horse-mule operators staged a protest in Janki Chatti village (Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand) against the Energy Corporation whom the protesters accused of negligence which led to the electrocution and death of a horse.

On 20 May 2024, employees went on strike and staged a sit-in protest at a Chheda Electricals Private Limited factory in Libberheri village (Haridwar, Uttarakhand) over various demands including an increase in salaries, weekly leaves, and government holidays.

On 20 May 2024, classmates of the deceased boy staged a sit-in protest at the Chhaprauli area in Noida city (Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused who ran over a boy - leading to his death - with a car over a minor dispute.

On 20 May 2024, teaching and non-teaching staff of aided private schools and members of the District unit of the Aided Schools Union staged a protest in Amritsar city (Punjab) against the failure of the state education department to resolve the issue of suspension of funds under the grants-in-aid scheme, and the lack of funds and grants for operating aided schools.

On 20 May 2024, TMC members staged protests at booths in Hooghly district (coded as Chinsurah city (Hooghly district, WB)) over claimed intimidation of voters by BJP along with central forces during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections.

On 20 May 2024, TMC members held a protest at Bizpur town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) over claimed attempts by BJP to create disturbance during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections. BJP claimed TMC members were attempting to rig the polls.

On 20 May 2024, TMC members held a protest at Titagarh town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) against a BJP candidate and stopped him (likely without using force) from entering a polling booth during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections.

On 20 May 2024, TMC members led by a minister held a protest and the BJP members led by a minister held a counter-protest in Hooghly constituency (coded as Chinsurah city (Hooghly district, WB) over political rivalry during the fifth phase of the Lok Sabha elections.

On 20 May 2024, hundreds of locals, mostly women, from three villages staged a procession with banners, posters, and the rhythmic beat of traditional drums in Bokaro city (Jharkhand), during a protest over their demands for inclusion of their villages either in the panchayat system or the local municipal body.
On 20 May 2024, over 100 female students held a protest by blocking a road at Gitaldaha town (Cooch Behar district, WB) against the delay in processing of their applications for a scholarship scheme.
On 20 May 2024, relatives and locals, after the murder of the paan shop owner, blocked the road and held a protest in Jabalpur city (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the arrest of the accused involved.
On 20 May 2024, the villagers held a protest outside the polling booth in Kusumbha village at Katkamdag block (Hazaribagh, Jharkhand) over their unfulfilled demand for a bridge near the coal sliding.

On 20 May 2024, passengers staged a protest at the airport in Tirupati city (Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh) after a Star Air flight to Kalaburagi was cancelled at the last minute due to a technical issue. The protesters demanded the airline to make alternate travel arrangements and a refund of their ticket fares.

On 20 May 2024, residents and members of the Tirumala Hills owners' welfare association staged a protest in the Manikonda locality in Hyderabad city (Hyderabad, Telangana) after a 10-year-old tree in the area was cut down by a resident. The protesters demanded the authorities to take action against the culprit.

On 20 May 2024, residents of various villages gathered and staged a protest, raising slogans, at the intersection in Padariya village (Budaun, Uttar Pradesh) against the frequent power cuts in the nearby villages. A Junior Engineer (JE) who was surrounded by the protesters fled the protest site.

On 20 May 2024, local people from Nagla Indra village staged a protest at the power plant in Gangiri village (Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh) against the poor supply of electricity at the Nagla Indra village.

On 20 May 2024, local people staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Patram Gate area in Bhiwani city (Haryana) against the supply of contaminated water in the area and condemned the Public Health Engineering Department officials whom the protesters accused of disregarding their complaints.

On 20 May 2024, people from various localities staged a protest along the Sardar Jhadu Singh Chowk (intersection) Road in Charkhi Dadri city (Haryana) against the lack of power supply in the area after a power cable got burnt.
On 20 May 2024, residents of various colonies staged a protest along Jhajjar Road in Rohtak city (Haryana) against the lack of supply of clean drinking water in the area and irregular power supply.

On 20 May 2024, ABVP members held a demonstration by burning tyres at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over the suicide of a research scholar and demanded the arrest of a professor claimed to be responsible for it.

On 20 May 2024, a huge crowd of Hindu devotees (on a religious pilgrimage) staged a demonstration, raising slogans, and vandalized the barricades and counters at the Chardham Yatra (Hindu religious pilgrimage) Transit Camp in Haridwar city (Uttarakhand) condemning the failure of the local administration to commence the temporary registration of pilgrims for the Chardham Yatra.

On 20 May 2024, local people staged a demonstration and set ablaze the motorcycle of the police outpost in charge and damaged his car in Satrao village (Deoria, Uttar Pradesh) after a man who was suspected of having been assaulted by 3 policemen earlier in the day died later in the evening (coded separately) while undergoing treatment at a hospital.

On 20 May 2024, voters raised slogans against the incumbent BJD MLA and scuffled with the MLA's supporters at booth no. 92, set up at Gopabandhupalli Primary School in Rourkela city (Sundergarh, Odisha) against his visit to the polling booth. Police escorted the MLA out of the pooling booth.

On 20 May 2024, a group of 6-7 physically assaulted an elderly man at Bogijuli in Maz Gaon area (Sonitpur, Assam) over suspicions of selling marijuana. He was taken to the hospital for treatment after passersby intervened.

Around 20 May 2024 (as reported), tea garden workers and ACMS staged a protest at Deamoolie TE (Tinsukia, Assam) against the tea garden manager for his authoritarian practices and for removing names from the roster for absences due to medical reasons. Protesters also demanded for the reinstatement of labourers who were removed and to fill vacant spots.

Around 20 May 2024 (as reported), hundreds of tea garden workers and ACMS staged a protest and closed the garden, burned an effigy of Andrew Yule Company's director in Tingkhong town (Dibrugarh, Assam) demanding their pending wages and rations.

On 20 May 2024, thousands staged a protest rally with placards organized by Western Angami Youth Organisation (WAYO) from Paramedical junction on NH-29 to Phoolbari in Kohima city (Kohima, Nagaland) against the death of Mezomia Mechu Krotho (MMK)'s president and Political Assistant to DC of Kohima who was assaulted by 2 men.

Around 20 May 2024 (as reported), tea garden workers staged a protest at Bamunbari tea estate near Moranhat (coded to Moranhat town, Charaideo, Assam) against the Government of India, Assam and Andrew Yule Company over anti-labour policies and poor working conditions. Protesters also burned effigies of Prime Minister of India, Chief Minister of Assam, Labour Minister of Assam and Andrew Yule management.

Around 20 May 2024 (as reported), tea garden workers staged a protest at Khowang tea estate in Khowang town (Dibrugarh, Assam) against the Government of India, Assam and Andrew Yule Company over anti-labour policies and poor working conditions. Protesters also burned effigies of Prime Minister of India, Chief Minister of Assam, Labour Minister of Assam and Andrew Yule management.

Around 20 May 2024 (as reported), students of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Model College staged a protest with slogans in their campus at Amjonga village (Goalpara, Assam) against their principal and female caretaker of their hostel for issues such as cutting off electricity at midnight, locking students in their rooms, fear of safety, monthly contributions, threats and mistreatment among others.

On 20 May 2024, students of Manipur college formed a chain and staged a protest with slogans near Pishumthong along Mayai Lambi in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) over lack of infrastructure and shortage of teachers.

Around 20 May 2024 (as reported), locals of 9 villages under Chawmanu assembly constituency staged a road block protest and blocked Manu-Chawmanu road (coded to Chawmanu town, Dhalai, Tripura) condemning issues of poor road conditions, shortage of clean drinking water, electricity and mobile network coverage.
