Around 22 May 2024 (as reported), hundreds of locals protested at Dhupdhara police station in Dhupdhara town (Goalpara, Assam) demanding stringent punishment for the killers of a minor and demanded justice for the victim.

On 22 May 2024, Indian Youth Congress members held a protest on the RNT Marg campus of Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya (DAVV) in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh), demanding an FIR against those involved in the examination paper leak case in the university.

On 22 May 2024, some unidentified people assaulted a young man and dragged him around after tying him to a truck near Muktsar city (Sri Muktsar Sahib, Punjab) over suspicions of stealing food grain. The young man was admitted to the hospital with injuries.

On 23 May 2024, one group fired at another group during a clash at Jogian area in Bishnah tehsil (Jammu district, J&K) over a land dispute. One person was left injured in the clash. Police later arrested one person.

On 23 May 2024, members of BJD and BJP clashed with stones and glass bottles at Tardinga village under Athagarh Assembly constituency (Cuttack, Odisha) when BJP members were campaigning for the party candidate by distributing money and liquor. Two BJD supporters, including a minor, were injured. Police arrested three BJP members after the incident.
On 23 May 2024, BJP members pushed barricades and clashed with police during a political rally at Kolkata city (WB) when they attempted to them from conducting the rally.

On 23 May 2024, a group of five cow vigilantes assaulted and killed a Muslim man (based on the name) in Banaskantha district (coded to Palanpur, Gujarat) when he was transporting buffaloes to a cattle fair. Police later arrested 2 accused persons involved in the killing.

On 23 May 2024, members of the BJP Other Backward Class (OBC) Morcha (unit), led by the BJP OBC state president, staged a protest and burned an effigy outside Banga Bhawan (building) in Delhi - Chanakya Puri (New Delhi, Delhi) against the West Bengal Chief Minister and the INDIA (an alliance of parties in opposition to BJP's NDA) whom the protesters accused of policies that are anti-Dalits, OBCs, and tribals.

On 23 May 2024, about 30-35 councilors, mostly from the BJP, and cutting across party lines, staged a protest 'Day 2' at the District headquarters in Ghaziabad city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the withdrawal of the strict action taken against a BJP councilor who was accused of assaulting a vendor and his wife on 19 May (coded separately).On 22 May 2024, councilors, cutting across party lines, staged a protest at the District headquarters in Ghaziabad city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the withdrawal of the strict action taken against a BJP councilor who was accused of assaulting a vendor and his wife on 19 May (coded separately). The protesters scuffled (likely non-violent) with the police when they attempted to march towards the police commissioner's residence.

On 23 May 2024, members of the BJP including an MP and OBC Morcha President staged a protest at the Jyothiba Phule statue in the Amberpet locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against the proposal to implement reservations for Muslims under the Backward Classes (BC) quota. The protesters asked the BC community members to support the BJP in order to ensure that their rights were safeguarded.

On 23 May 2024, members of the BRS staged a rasta roko (road block) protest with the body of a BRS functionary who was killed by unidentified assailants (coded separately) in Chinnambavi village (Wanaparthy, Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to take measures to stop political violence in the state. The protesters also demanded capital punishment for the accused and raised slogans against an INC minister to mark their protest.

On 23 May 2024, farmers under the banner of Pagdi Sambhal Jatta Kisan Sangharsh Samiti (a farmer group) staged a '3-day' sit-in protest outside the police station and burnt effigies in Jakhal town (Fatehabad, Haryana) against a BJP nominee (former MP) for the Lok Sabha elections and a BJP MP whom the protesters accused of driving recklessly during a demonstration near Sant Nagar village on 12 May (coded separately). The protesters accused the police of taking action on the complaint (against the farmers) registered by the BJP nominee, while no action was taken on their complaint.

On 23 May 2024, members of BKU (Ugrahan) staged a protest rally in Patiala city (Punjab) during the campaign rally of the Prime Minister of India (BJP) for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been staging protests condemning the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands. The protesters were allotted a designated spot in the city to stage their protest.

On 23 May 2024, locals led by a former panch (village government head) held a protest by blocking a highway at Koreponu area in Hiranagar tehsil (Kathua district, WB) over a road accident involving a dumper in which two persons were killed and demanded that dumpers no longer be allowed.

On 23 May 2024, villagers, members of the Loutolim Tenants Association, a former Sarpanch (village head) and social activist and a Deputy Sarpanch (village head) staged a protest in Loutolim village (South Goa, Goa) against the proposed Borim Bridge and bypass project. The protesters said that they will not give away their ancestral land for any government project.

On 23 May 2024, city INC leaders held a protest at the office of Divisional Commissioner and Lokayukta in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) demanding a CBI probe into the 'fake bill scam' of Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC).

On 23 May 2024, UDF and INC councillors staged a protest in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the Kochi Corporation for not cleaning the drains in the city before the onset of the monsoon season. The protesters removed weeds from the Karanakkodam drain to mark their protest.

On 23 May 2024, members of the KRV staged a protest at the tahsildar's office in Hubballi city (Dharwad, Karnataka) demanding the transfer of the police commissioner for failing to maintain the law and order in the city and for not stopping the increasing cases of crimes against women. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 23 May 2024, residents and hotel owners held a protest at Gagangeer-Choonadagi area (coded as Gangangir town (Ganderbal district, J&K)) against the power cuts imposed by the local power department and demanded 24 hour supply for running their business.

On 23 May 2024, members of NSUI led by the district president burned the effigy of Madhya Pradesh CBI and held a protest at Tower Chowk in Ujjain city (Madhya Pradesh) over its investigation into the nursing college scam.

On 23 May 2024, two groups of parishioners of the CSI congregation staged protests and counter protests in front of the Mateer Memorial CSI Church at the LMS Junction in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) over who would be in charge of the church administration. The two groups supported two different bishops and shouted slogans against each other.

On 23 May 2024, farmers under the banners of SKM, KMM, and SKM (Non-political), including those who have been protesting at the Punjab-Haryana border area (ongoing), staged a dharna (sit-in protest) along the Rajpura Road at the Toll plaza next to Dharehi Jattan village (Patiala, Punjab) when they stopped from marching towards Patiala city where the Prime Minister of India (BJP) was conducting a campaign rally for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been staging protests condemning the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

On 23 May 2024, farmers under the banners of SKM, KMM, and SKM (Non-political), including those who have been protesting at the Punjab-Haryana border area (ongoing), staged multiple dharnas (sit-in protest) along the Pehowa, Samana, Sangrur, Sirhind and Nabha Roads in the Patiala district (Punjab) when they stopped from marching towards Patiala city where the Prime Minister of India (BJP) was conducting a campaign rally for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been staging protests condemning the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

On 23 May 2024, members of the TPDK staged a protest in Coimbatore city (Tamil Nadu) against a comment made by the Prime Minister in relation to the treasure room keys of the Puri Jagannath Temple while he was campaigning for the Lok Sabha elections in Odisha. The protesters demanded that the Prime Minister to apologise for his words.

On 23 May 2024, local women staged a protest and placed carts along the Shani Bazaar (market) Road in Haldwani city (Nainital, Uttarakhand) against the prolonged lack of supply of drinking water in the area.

On 23 May 2024, around 170 girls residing at the Ambedkar Post Matric Hostel along with members of the SFI staged a protest outside the residence of the Assistant Commissioner of Lingsugur Revenue Division in Lingsugur town (Raichur, Karnataka) accusing the hostel authorities of not providing basic amenities and good quality food despite repeated requests.

On 23 May 2024, family members of a deceased father-son duo and villagers held a protest at the SP office in Neemuch city (Madhya Pradesh), claiming inaction and negligence by the police in Manasa after the death of the duo due to electrocution on May 13.

On 23 May 2024, locals held a protest at Nandigram city (Purba Medinipur district, WB) against TMC over the death of a BJP woman in an attack in the same area (coded separately) during the Lok Sabha elections.
On 23 May 2024, scores of family members of railway employees held a protest by blocking a railway line at Jammu city (J&K) over lack of water supply in the railway colony.

On 23 May 2024, local people staged a protest and placed stones along the Lalganj-Kalwari Road in Kolkam Kalan area (Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a motorcycle-borne man and his who were hit and killed by a truck. The man's daughter also suffered serious injuries.

On 23 May 2024, farmers affiliated to the Tamil Nadu Vivasaygal Sangam (Tamil Nadu Farmers Association) along with members of the CPI(M) staged a protest outside the Sub-Collector's office in Hosur city (Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu) against the laying of a gas pipeline by the Gas Authority Of India Ltd (GAIL) for a gas pipeline project. The protesters demanded the officials to stop the protest and were arrested by the police.

On 23 May 2024, INC councillors took out a protest march from the Thekke Gopura Nada to the Mayor's chamber at the Thrissur Corporation in Thrissur city (Kerala) against the delay in cleaning the drainage canals in the city which had led to heavy flooding in the heavy rains. The protesters carried the water hyacinths that were collected from the water canals to mark their protest and threw the weeds on the corporation campus. The police arrested the protesters.

On 23 May 2024, farmers staged a demonstration along the road in Pasiana village (Patiala, Punjab) against a BJP nominee (MP) for the Lok Sabha elections and clashed with the police. Both the BJP nominee and the demonstrators were on their way towards Patiala city where the Prime Minister of India (BJP) was conducting a campaign rally for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been staging demonstrations condemning the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' demonstrations and for failing to address their long-standing demands. The police intervened and used mild force to disperse the demonstrators which resulted in minor injuries to a few policemen and a demonstrator.

Around 23 May 2024 (as reported), a group of people staged a demonstration at the Burail police outpost in Chandigarh city for unidentified reasons. The demonstrations were also accused of manhandling (likely violent) the police outpost in charge when he tried to intervene. A video of the incident was circulated online.

On 23 May 2024, a large number of Meira Paibi (Women Torch Bearers) of Lamphel Khunou tore a signboard, removed barricades placed by Regional Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) on the northern entrance to the mortuary and physically assaulted an unarmed civil security in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) claiming that RIMS defied a court order allowing public usage of the road and blocked it. RIMS denied claims.

On 23 May 2024, hundreds of tea garden labourers staged a protest in front of Powai Tea Estate garden office near Powai village (Tinsukia, Assam) demanding regular power supply at their quarters, better healthcare facilities and termination of a staff appointed from outside the tea garden.

On 23 May 2024, locals staged a road block protest for 2 hours and blocked the main road going through Mangalkhali village within Jubarajnagar village (North Tripura, Tripura) condemning the poor road constructions and demanded immediate repairs. The blockade was lifted after a representative of a road contractor gave assurances to protesters.

On 23 May 2024, around 300 people staged a demonstration at the police outpost in Khelmati village (Sonitpur, Assam) after an arrested man died in police custody and condemned police forces for torturing him despite his innocence. The demonstration turned violent as police and CRPF personnel used lathi charges and tear gas, while demonstrators pelted stones. One police officer and two journalists were injured, a police vehicle was damaged, and one demonstrator was arrested.

On 23 May 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu Vivasayigal Sangam (Tamil Nadu Farmers Association) staged a protest by organising a mass petition submission outside the sub-collector's office in Krishnagiri city (Tamil Nadu) against the proposal to lay down a GAIL (Indian state-owned energy corporation) pipeline through their farmlands.

On 23 May 2024, members of the Akka Foundation Trust (non-profit organization) staged a silent protest at the Sangolli Rayana Circle in Hubballi city (Dharwad, Karnataka) against the INC-led state government for not taking any measures to recycle plastics. The protesters demanded a ban on single-use plastic, the responsibility to take back plastic waste produced by food manufacturers and the use of plastic waste in road construction.

On 23 May 2024, a mob engaged in a physical altercation with police forces injuring 1 police personnel in Khalsamari area within South Salamara police station limits (coded to Hatsingimari town, South Salamara-Mankachar, Assam) during a police operation against a group of individuals who had forcefully seized 8 buffaloes. 3 were arrested.

On 23 May 2024, residents and members of the Aam Aadmi Party held a protest in Jamshedpur city (East Singhbhum, Jharkhand) against the installation of poles at the JEMCO ground near the Gurudwara gate.

On 24 May 2024, members of BJD clashed with BJP members with swords in Bhagabanpur village in Bhapur block (Nayagarh, Odisha) ahead of the sixth phase of Lok Sabha and simultaneous state elections. There were no casualties. The Inspector General of police, however, has denied the occurrence of violent incidents.

On 24 May 2024, members of BJD clashed with BJP members with swords in Birdi village in Khandapada block under Khandapada Assembly constituency (Nayagarh, Odisha) ahead of the sixth phase of Lok Sabha and simultaneous state elections. Three persons were injured. Inspector General of police has denied the occurrence of violent incident. Police detained two persons.

On 24 May 2024, members of two rival parties (likely BJP and BJD based on context) clashed in Handuguda village in Chhendipada block (Angul district, Odisha) ahead of the sixth phase of Lok Sabha and simultaneous state elections. 1 person was injured in the clash.
On 24 May 2024, TMC and BJP members engaged in a clash at Dantan town (Paschim Medinipur district, WB) during the Lok Sabha elections. No casualties.
On 24 May 2024, unidentified persons heckled (likely violent) a BJP candidate at Haldia town (Purba Medinipur district, WB) during the Lok Sabha elections.
On 24 May 2024, unidentified persons assaulted a BJP polling agent and forced him to leave the booth at Ghatal town (Paschim Medinipur district, WB) during the Lok Sabha elections.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Central Industrial Security Force
text: On 24 May 2024, women pelted stones at a BJP candidate's vehicle and central forces convoy (likely CRPF given they form the bulk of the forces) at Garbeta town (Paschim Medinipur district, WB) during the Lok Sabha elections. The BJP candidate and CISF personnel were left injured in the incident.

On 24 May 2024, a mob vandalized a car in the Zenda Chowk area of Kotwali police limits in Nagpur city (Maharashtra) after it hit three persons. The police detained three people, including the driver, after the incident.

On 24 May 2024, ABVP members held a sit-in protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over the suicide of a research scholar and demanded the arrest of a professor claimed to be responsible for it.
On 24 May 2024, CPI(M) members held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) to demand a reduction in power bills.

On 24 May 2024, a large number of farmers (on buses), including the BKU (Doaba) president, staged a protest, wearing black badges, along the road close to Bath Castle near Pragpur village (Jalandhar, Punjab) when they were stopped from marching towards Jalandhar city where the Prime Minister of India (BJP) was conducting a campaign rally for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been staging protests condemning the BJP-led central government for the excessive intervention during the farmer's 'Delhi Chalo' protests and for failing to address their long-standing demands.

Around 24 May 2024 (as reported), hundreds of bar and pub owners wearing black T-shirts held a protest in Pune city (Maharashtra) against the clampdown on their businesses after a fatal hit-and-run case involving a minor driving a Porsche in an inebriated state.

On 24 May 2024, street vendors held a protest at Muthi town (Jammu district, J&K) against the municipal authority over the anti-encroachment drive and being removed from the area where they have been operating for the last 20-30 years.
On 24 May 2024, MSJK members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the power department over the billing system, fluctuation of power and frequent power cuts.

On 24 May 2024, members of Bajrang Dal and RSS (likely members of Cow Protection Groups based on the issue) staged a protest in Baripur village (Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh) after the carcasses of bovine animals were found in the field. The protesters claimed that smugglers were slaughtering cows in the area.

On 24 May 2024, members of the All Gujarat Students' Union (AGSU) held a protest at the MSU head office in Vadodara city (Gujarat) demanding an increase in the quota for local students from Vadodara from 70 percent to 90 percent.
On 24 May 2024, TMC supporters held a protest at Bankura district (WB) against BJP candidates during the Lok Sabha elections.
On 24 May 2024, TMC supporters held a protest at Purulia district (WB) against BJP candidates during the Lok Sabha elections.
On 24 May 2024, TMC supporters held a protest against BJP candidates by blocking a BJP candidate's convoy at Ghatal town (Paschim Medinipur district, WB) during the Lok Sabha elections.

On 24 May 2024, members of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) from Ajayapuram village in Anakapalli district and members of the Andhra Pradesh Girijana Sangham (tribal group) staged a protest in Cheemalapadu village (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against the administration for not paying the entire amount of their Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) (social employment scheme) wages despite having worked for six days of the week. The protesters held spades and rakes to mark their protest.

On 24 May 2024, VHP along with members of the Bangiya Sanyasi Samaj (a Hindu religious body) held a protest march as part of 'Sant Swabhiman Yatra' at Kolkata city (WB) against the TMC-led state government's chief's claimed statement insulting priests at Ramakrishna Mission and Bharat Sevasharam Sangha.

On 24 May 2024, VHP along with members of the Bangiya Sanyasi Samaj (a Hindu religious body) held protest marches as part of 'Sant Swabhiman Yatra' across WB (coded as Kolkata city (WB)) against the TMC-led state government's chief's claimed statement insulting priests at Ramakrishna Mission and Bharat Sevasharam Sangha.

On 24 May 2024, VHP along with members of the Bangiya Sanyasi Samaj (a Hindu religious body) held a protest march as part of 'Sant Swabhiman Yatra' at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) against the TMC-led state government's chief's claimed statement insulting priests at Ramakrishna Mission and Bharat Sevasharam Sangha.
On 24 May 2024, hundreds of locals in Bairagarh locality blocked road and held a protest in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) against unscheduled power cuts.
On 24 May 2024, residents gathered and staged a two-hour-long protest at Gumashta Nagar electricity zone in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) against unscheduled power cuts.

On 24 May 2024, family members and students took out a protest rally and attempted to 'lay siege' to the Maruthi College of Nursing in Bhadrachalam town (Khammam, Telangana) demanding a fair investigation into the suspicious death of a first year nursing student. The protesters attempted to manhandle a college management representative, and the police intervened and brought the situation under control.

On 24 May 2024, a hundred residents blocked a national highway, threw stones and burned tires in Gamadi village (Sabar Kantha, Gujarat) during a demonstration against the death of a local in a road accident. Three police personnel sustained injuries. A police van was also set alight by the mob. Police used tear gas shells to disperse the crowd.

On 24 May 2024, suspected Kuki assailants attacked 2 Meitei men with slingshots from the hillside of Houkip Punji area along NH-37 while they were on their way to Jiribam town (coded to Jiribam town, Jiribam, Manipur) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state. The shots hit the rear side of the car window.

Around 24 May 2024 (as reported), locals physically assaulted a man in Gandhigram town (West Tripura, Tripura) who sexually molested a minor on the pretext of asking her for mangoes. He was later handed over to the police.

On 24 May 2024, local women staged a protest, carrying empty utensils and raising slogans, at the Dayalbagh area's Jageshwar Nagar in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) against the Municipal Corporation for failing to address the shortage of water in the area.

On 24 May 2024, the Ahmedabad unit of BJP's OBC Morcha held a protest and beat the effigy of the West Bengal Chief Minister with slippers in Ahmedabad city (Ahmadabad, Gujarat) against her non-acceptance of the Calcutta High Court order that canceled all OBC certificates issued in Bengal after 2010. Police reached the spot and stopped them from burning the effigy. There was no physical interaction between police and protesters, and the latter continued raising slogans.

On 24 May 2024, family members staged a protest outside the Mankameshwar Furnace Factory at the Talanagari area in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) and placed bodies on the road, demanding compensation for the death of 3 factory workers who died in an accident at the factory. The protest concluded after compensation was provided to the deceased's families.

On 24 May 2024, INC leaders, including an MP (nominee for Lok Sabha elections), former MLAs, and the former deputy chief minister, staged a protest in front of the Municipal Corporation office in Amritsar city (Punjab) against poor civic infrastructure including mismanagement of road development, garbage-lifting, and sewerage.

On 24 May 2024, supporters of two rival parties clashed swords and other sharp-edged weapons at Bhapur block in Khandapada assembly constituency (Nayagarh district, Odisha) over distribution of cash and liquor in the area, ahead of sixth phase of Lok Sabha and simultaneous state assembly election. Four persons were injured in the clash.

On 24 May 2024, hundreds of hostlers held a protest at the VIT (Vellore Institute of Technology) campus in the Ashta area of Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh), over acute water shortage on campus. The protest ended after the administration provided assurances to the students.

On 24 May 2024, a large number of people, including members of SKM, staged a protest, raising black flags and slogans, in Binewal village (Hoshiarpur, Punjab) during the visit of a BJP nominee (BJP state vice-president) for the Lok Sabha elections. The protesters condemned the BJP for being 'anti-farmer'.

On 24 May 2024, local people and family members (likely Sikh based on relation to the deceased) of the deceased staged a dharna (sit-in protest) at the crossing in Chabal Kalan town (Tarn Taran, Punjab) against the death of a man (deputy chief of a Gurudwara) (coded separately).
On 24 May 2024, local people staged a protest in front of the local electricity office in Chormar Khera village (Sirsa, Haryana) against the frequent power cuts in the area.

On 24 May 2024, around 15 people were suspected of assaulting a female journalist and her team, and tearing her clothes, near Bamheta locality in Ghaziabad city (Uttar Pradesh) when they arrived in the area to investigate and cover a suspected case of 'illegal constructions'.

On 24 May 2024, at least six persons, including a minor, were injured in a group clash at Harijan Sahi of Taradinka village in Athagarh block (Cuttack, Odisha) over distribution of cash and liquor in the area, ahead of sixth phase of Lok Sabha and simultaneous state assembly election. Distribution of cash and liquor to voters is a common tactic employed by electoral candidates.

On 24 May 2024, students of various colleges, after the fatal Porsche car crash in Pune, held a candle march protest in Jabalpur city (Madhya Pradesh), demanding justice for the slain duo who originally hailed from the city.

Around 24 May 2024 (as reported), unidentified assailants assaulted and killed a man (deputy chief of a Gurudwara (Sikh temple)) near Kakka Kandiala village (Tarn Taran, Punjab) for unidentified reasons.

On 24 May 2024, supporters of two rival parties clashed at Subuddhipara village under Pipili block (Puri, Odisha), ahead of sixth phase of Lok Sabha and simultaneous state assembly election. Four men, including Mangalpur panchayat samiti member, were injured in the clash.

On 24 May 2024, members of various organisations under the banner of Tamil Nadu People Liberation Movement staged a protest in Thanjavur city (Tamil Nadu) against the Tamil Nadu Governor for issuing an invitation to the Raj Bhavan with an image of Thiruvalluvar (poet) in saffron (Hindutva colour) robes. The protesters condemned the Governor for misrepresenting the Tamil poet.

On 24 May 2024, a group of people (including likely from the Muslim community based on the identity of the deceased) vandalised the Channagiri police station in Channagiri town (Davanagere, Karnataka) after a carpenter who was detained by the police died in police custody (coded separately). The rioters destroyed eight police vehicles and injured at least 11 police officers. The police resorted to a lathi (baton) charge and tear gas to disperse the rioters.
On 24 May 2024, TMC members clashed with BJP members at Garchakraberia town (Purba Medinipur district, WB) during voting for the Lok Sabha elections. Central forces resorted to baton charge.

On 24 May 2024, more than a dozen persons abused and shot at a couple at their shed near the Chai Tola area in Kursela village (Katihar, Bihar) over a land dispute. The injured couple is stable. Police detained nine persons.

On 25 May 2024, Punjab Water Supply and Sewerage Board (PWSSB) employees staged a sit-in protest, raising slogans, at the Municipal Corporation (MC) office in Abohar city (Fazilka, Punjab) against a MC councilor whom the protesters accused of misbehaving with a PWSSB employee.

On 25 May 2024, students and members of the SCS, including the SCS metropolitan president, closed the Institute of Social Sciences and staged a dharna (sit-in protest), raising slogans, at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against a professor who was accused of molesting students.

Around 25 May 2024 (as reported), residents along with members of the INDIA alliance, including AAP and INC, held a protest in Anand city (Gujarat) over the installation of smart meters. The protesters claim that the users are paying unreasonably high electricity charges due to technical issues with the smart meters and demanded its removal.

On 25 May 2024, local people assaulted a young man with sticks at the Khadar area (along the Ramganga river) in the Bareilly district (Uttar Pradesh) for hunting a peacock. The man later died due to his injuries. A video of the incident was circulated online.

On 25 May 2024, residents of Subhash Nagar locality gathered in large numbers and staged a protest at the power sub-station in Bareilly city (Uttar Pradesh) against the frequent power cuts in the area.

On 25 May 2024, nearly 50 farmers staged a protest, raising slogans, in Bhallaiana village (Sri Muktsar Sahib, Punjab) before the visit of the Rajasthan chief minister (BJP) who was scheduled to campaign in the area in support of a BJP nominee (MP) for the Lok Sabha elections. Farmers in the state have been protesting against the BJP-led central government whom they accused of excessive intervention during the 'Delhi Chalo' farmer's protest and for failing to address their long-standing demands. Protesters were detained by the police.

On 25 May 2024, intern doctors staged a protest at Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College in Chamba town (Himachal Pradesh) against the suspected harassment of a female intern by the attendant of a patient. The protesters demanded better security provisions at the medical college.

On 25 May 2024, local people staged a protest for the second day and refused to cast their votes for the Lok Sabha elections, close to the polling center, near Chormar Khera village (Sirsa, Haryana) condemning frequent power cuts in the area. Locals ended their protest after the local authorities installed a transformer in the area.

Around 25 May 2024 (as reported), residents along with members of the INDIA alliance, including AAP and INC, held a protest in Dahod city (Dohad, Gujarat) over the installation of smart meters. The protesters claim that the users are paying unreasonably high electricity charges due to technical issues with the smart meters and demanded its removal.

On 25 May 2024, local people (likely from the Hindu community based on the issue) staged a protest close to the Rahpura underpass near Fatehganj West town (Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh) against the vandalization of the statue of Lord Hanuman (Hindu God) (coded separately).

Around 25 May 2024 (as reported), residents along with members of the INDIA alliance, including AAP and INC, held a protest in Godhra city (Panchmahal district, Gujarat) over the installation of smart meters. The protesters claim that the users are paying unreasonably high electricity charges due to technical issues with the smart meters and demanded its removal.

On 25 May 2024, members of the Valmiki community staged a protest at the Valmiki Ashram (religious dwelling) along Hariana Road in Hoshiarpur city (Punjab) against the suspected illegal construction of a wall at the ashram by a group of people who claimed that they owned the land on which the ashram was built.

Around 25 May 2024 (as reported), residents along with members of the INDIA alliance, including AAP and INC, held a protest in Jamnagar city (Gujarat) over the installation of smart meters. The protesters claim that the users are paying unreasonably high electricity charges due to technical issues with the smart meters and demanded its removal.

On 25 May 2024, Pune citizens under the aegis of Team Swacch Kalyani Nagar (TSKN) held a candle light protest march, in response to a fatal driving and driving car crash case, in Pune city (Maharashtra) demanding justice for two victims.

On 25 May 2024, local people staged a protest and refused to cast their votes for the Lok Sabha elections in Kol village (Azamgarh, Uttar Pradesh) demanding better roads and the provision of a bridge.

On 14 June 2024, students from many districts, led by the NSUI medical wing, held a protest outside the JP Hospital in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) over the non-declaration of the 2023 PNST exam results.

On 14 June 2024, women staged a protest in Madampalayam village (Erode, Tamil Nadu) against the officials for not allotting work to them under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) (social employment scheme).

On 14 June 2024, the intervening night of 13 June 2024 - 14 June 2024, four persons from the Kshatriya Rajput community assaulted their OBC neighbor to death with sticks and axe in Parsona village (Bhind district, Madhya Pradesh) over an unapproved relationship involving the accused's daughter and the victim's grandson.

On 14 June 2024, hundreds of people (likely Hindus based on context) blocked roads and forced businesses to shut down in Jaora town (Ratlam district, Madhya Pradesh) after the severed head of a calf was found dumped inside Jagannath Mahadev temple. Police had to fire tear gas shells to disperse the protesters.

On 14 June 2024, members of a Hindu right-wing group set ablaze a truck carrying cattle on the outskirts of Jaora town (Ratlam district, Madhya Pradesh) after the vehicle overturned leading to the death of 14 cows.

Around 14 June 2024 (as reported), villagers staged a protest in Ronihal village (Vijayapura, Karnataka) against the lack of power supply at night. The protesters said that there were frequent crocodile sightings in the area and the lack of electricity was proving to be a risk for them.

On 14 June 2024, members of the Association of University Teachers (AUT) staged a protest in front of the Regional Joint Director, Directorate of College Education in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against the non-payment of salaries to several teachers and employees of 10 colleges that were previously affiliated to the Bharathidasan University and were converted into government colleges in 2019. Police detained 75 protesters.

On 14 June 2024, relatives of a girl belonging to the General Caste group who had eloped with a boy belonging to the Scheduled Caste community vandalised a CPI(M) office on Reddiyarpatti Road in Tirunelveli city (Tamil Nadu) after CPI(M) functionaries conducted the couple's wedding at the office. The rioters attempted to take the girl away and broke the glass partition inside the office.

On 14 June 2024, beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) Housing for All (HFA) beating drums entered the gallery of the municipal corporation headquarters and held a dharna (sit-in protest) in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) over non-allotment and possession of houses in the Bagmugalia and Ganga Nagar HAF projects.

On 14 June 2024, villagers staged a protest in Chinnaporla village (Narayanpet, Telangana) demanding action against villagers who had beaten a farmer to death over a land dispute (coded separately). The protesters condemned the police for not taking action on time despite the victim's attempts to contact them.

On 14 June 2024, 40 to 50 local villagers assaulted a Forest Range Officer, (FRO) a section officer and two other staff members of the Forest Department in the Kalpole forest area in Kalpol village (Nizamabad, Telangana) when the officials attempted to stop the villagers from tilling land inside the forest area. The rioters twisted the arm of the FRO, hurled stones at the section officer and beat up the two other officers. The officers sustained injuries.

On 14 June 2024, locals and traders led by a former minister of BJP held a protest by blocking a highway at Jammu city (J&K) against National Highway Authority of India over construction of the flyover claiming it would affect their livelihoods adversely.

On 14 June 2024, cow vigilantes pursued and clashed with cow smugglers, who opened fire at them, along the Mumbai-Delhi Expressway near Ferozpur Jhirka town (Nuh, Haryana). One man (cow vigilante) suffered a serious bullet wound to the abdomen. Both groups were from the Hindu community, the cattle traders belonged to the Bagri caste group.

On 14 June 2024, Hindu right wing members clashed with some Muslim youth at the APMC yard in Dharwad city (Karnataka) after the Hindu right wing members stopped the Muslim youth for transporting cattle. Three Hindu youth sustained injuries.
On 14 June 2024, local people assaulted 2 men at Palauli village under the Sakran police station area (Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh) after he was caught breaking into a house and stealing.

On 14 June 2024, students staged a protest in front of the college administration building at the Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH) campus in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the administration to reimburse the fee and mess charges that were due to them. The protesters also demanded the administration to not to withhold their exam hall tickets.
On 14 June 2024, members of ABVP staged a protest at the Agricultural University in Palampur town (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) against the fee increment.

On 14 June 2024, tribals under the aegis of Sarva Adivasi Samaj (All Tribal Society) held a 'jail bharo' (fill the prison) protest in Manpur town (Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh) to demand the release of tribal leader and also against claimed atrocities in Bastar division. State president of Sarva Adivasi Samaj also submitted a memorandum addressed to the director general of police listing their demands.

On 14 June 2024, employees, including the AITUC district president, gathered under the banner of the Mid-Day Meal Workers Union and staged a protest at Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Club Park in Kanina town (Mahendragarh, Haryana) over various demands including an increase in honorarium and the provision of employee status.

On 14 June 2024, local people and BKU (apolitical) members, led by its district president, staged a protest, raising slogans, in front of the powerhouse at Majhr Shila village near Gadarpur city (Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand) against the frequent power outages in the area.

On 14 June 2024, BKU (Shankar) members staged a dharna (sit-in protest) outside the Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) electricity office in Hasanpur city (Amroha, Uttar Pradesh) demanding the replacement of an electricity transformer at Chakouri village.

On 14 June 2024, BKU (Charuni) members, led by its district president, staged a protest at the Collectorate in Moradabad city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the resolution of an issue (land compensation) associated with a land located at Century Paper Mill.

On 14 June 2024, residents and farmers from various villages staged a sit-in protest at the electricity sub-station in Jhojhu Kalan village (Charkhi Dadri, Haryana) against the electricity shortage in their villages and demanded the replacement of the lineman.
On 14 June 2024, local people and farmers staged a protest, raising slogans, in Ratera village (Bhiwani, Haryana) against the water shortage in the area.

On 14 June 2024, local people, led by the village head (local government head), staged a protest near Netua Dairy in Nand Lal Chhapra village (Kushi Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) demanding the resolution of the waterlogging issue in the area.

On 14 June 2024, Auxiliary Nurses and Midwives (ANM) staged a protest at the Community Health Center (CHC) in Nichlaul town (Maharajganj, Uttar Pradesh) accusing the CHC superintendent and clerk of harassment.

On 14 June 2024, seers of various mutts (Hindu religious organisations) staged a protest in Hassan city (Karnataka) demanding the authorities to take action against an actor and his associates who were accused of murdering a fan for sending derogatory messages to the actor's female friend.

Around 14 June 2024 (as reported), the MP Forest Employees Union members, led by the provincial president, held a protest in Jawad town (Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh) against the suspension of Jawad forest ranger over a land dispute between revenue and forest department. They also submitted a memorandum to the collector.

On 14 June 2024, employees staged a protest at the National Health Mission (NHM) office in Jhajjar city (Haryana) over various demands including revision of salaries on the line of the seventh pay scale and regularization of employees.

On 14 June 2024, a group of people under the banner of Uttarakhand Rajya Aandolankari Manch (Uttarakhand National Revolution Platform) staged a protest at Deen Dayal Park in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) over various demands including equal pension, and 10 percent horizontal reservation.

On 14 June 2024, sanitation workers staged a sit-in protest along the Budaun Road at the Saraura area in Ujhani town (Budaun, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against a transporter and his son whom the protesters accused of misbehaviour with sanitation workers and obstruction of work.

On 14 June 2024, a group of people under the leadership of a former BRS MLA staged a protest in front of the District Cooperative Bank branch in Lingampet village (Kamareddy, Telangana) against the bank officials for putting down red flags for land auction on a piece of agricultural land owned by a farmer for failing to repay a loan taken from the bank and for also selling the land to another person.

On 14 June 2024, members of the Adivasi Teachers Association and tribal leaders staged a protest in Gudoor village (Mahabubabad, Telangana) after a teacher was killed when an overloaded lorry fell on him while he was having tea with a police constable and another relative. The protesters demanded compensation for the kin of the deceased.

On 14 June 2024, family members and locals held a protest and shut down the school gates at Dowada village under Amet police station (Rajsamand district, Rajasthan) demanding immediate suspension of a school teacher who had eloped with a Class 12 girl student. Police reached the spot and tried to calm down the protestors.
On 14 June 2024, several members of the chamber of commerce held a protest at Jaina town (Bokaro, Jharkhand) over the irregular water supply in the area.

On 14 June 2024, a large number of local people staged a protest in Harigarh village (Jind, Haryana) against the opening of a liquor vend. The protesters placed the liquor crates outside the shop - which was later put back into the shop.

On 14 June 2024, local people staged a protest at the New Nandwani Nagar area in Sonipat city (Haryana) against the Municipal Corporation whom the protesters accused of discrimination in the implementation of development works.
On 14 June 2024, local people staged a protest, raising slogans, along the road near Piplu Narsingh Temple in Bangana town (Una, Himachal Pradesh) against the opening of a liquor shop in the area.
On 14 June 2024, residents of Dewra Damodarpur village staged a protest at the Collectorate in Azamgarh city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding a stop to the construction of a boundary wall at the village.

On 14 June 2024, many local people staged a protest at the Collectorate in Sultanpur city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding compensation for the family members of the deceased who was killed when a building collapsed at the Ghasiari Mandi (market) area.

On 14 June 2024, family members of the deceased staged a protest along the Lakhimpur-Milpurva Road in Phool Behar village (Kheri, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a young woman who the protesters claimed was murdered and demanded action against the accused.
On 14 June 2024, residents of Dharupur village staged a protest at the Collectorate in Sultanpur city (Uttar Pradesh) against the village head and secretary whom the protesters accused of corruption.
On 14 June 2024, local people staged a protest and surrounded the block officials in Noora Pur village (Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh) demanding the construction of a culvert on the Nawabganj canal.

On 14 June 2024, villagers along with the parents of a minor girl who was raped and killed by a migrant worker staged a protest on the Rajiv Rahadari (state highway) in Katnapally village (Peddapalli, Telangana) demanding the police to take action against the accused. The protesters also condemned the rice mill owner for not providing a proper shelter for the families and workers.

On 14 June 2024, local people staged a demonstration and held hostage 2 Public Health Engineering Department officials who were forced to sit under the sun in Dhad village (Hisar, Haryana) against the water shortage in the area.

On 14 June 2024, members of the Hindu Sangharsh Samiti (Hindu Struggle Committee) staged a protest 'day 2' at the Collectorate in Muzaffarnagar city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the revocation of the district banishment of a young Hindu leader.

On 14 June 2024, members of VHP staged a protest, raising slogans, at the police station in Allahabad city (Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh) against the police whom the protesters accused of arbitrary action.
On 14 June 2024, police aspirants held a protest in Pune city (Maharashtra) demanding an increase in the age limit for recruitment to fill 17,471 constabulary posts in the state police.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Assam Rifles
text: On 15 June 2024, a mob (likely Meitei, based on similar coded events), comprising of mostly women, stopped 4 trucks carrying construction materials to Churachandpur district and burned 2 of them at Tronglaobi village (Bishnupur, Manipur) resulting in police forces firing tear gas shells and mock bombs to disperse the crowd amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Sikh regiment, police forces and fire services were able to save the other 2 vehicles.

On 15 June 2024, 3 suspected BJP supporters vandalized Gournagar RD Block office, broke computers, furniture and physically assaulted government officials in Kailashahar town (Unakoti, Tripura) over suspected political tensions related to the upcoming Panchayat elections. 3 people were arrested and the injured employees were taken to Unakoti District Hospital for treatment.

On 15 June 2024, unidentified persons hurled bombs at the house of a INTTUC leader's house while his family was present in the house at Beraberia town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) after the Lok Sabha elections. There were no casualties however the house was left damaged.

On 15 June 2024, a large number of transport drivers led by an INTTUC leader held a protest march at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over the murder of a person during a dispute between two sides and demanded justice.
On 15 June 2024, locals led by JKNPP members held a protest at Dhanori area in Udhampur district (J&K) against the water department over lack of water supply in the area.

On 15 June 2024, Chandrapur Anchalik Chatra (students) Santha staged a sit-in protest on the road in Chandrapur town (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) condemning poor road conditions especially during monsoons and demanded road constructions.

On 15 June 2024, members of the Muslim community clashed (likely violent based on similar events) with members of the BJP, the BJYM and the Bajrang Dal in Medak town (Telangana) after the BJP and Bajrang Dal members found cows in the Jambikunta village and set them free ahead of Bakrid (Muslim festival).

On 15 June 2024, 6 people from two communities (likely from the Hindu and Muslim communities based on the issue) clashed with each other at Sector 23 in Dwarka area in Delhi - Najafgarh (South West Delhi, Delhi) over a dispute regarding who gets to fill the water first (likely from a common tap at a slum area). 3 people were seriously injured.

On 15 June 2024, members of the Muslim community were suspected of assaulting a Bajrang Dal member and his friend and snatching their motor bike, near the State Bank of India in Aonla city (Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh) in a suspected case of communal violence. Police however claimed there was no incident of snatching.

On 15 June 2024, assailants suspected to be members of the TDP, JSP and the BJP pelted stones at a former YSRCP Chairman's residence on the Main Road in Punganur town (Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh) against a YSRCP MLA's proposed visit to the town. The rioters demonstrated, tried to forcibly enter the house and made allegations of corruption against the YSRCP leader.

On 15 June 2024, assailants suspected to be members of the TDP, JSP and the BJP assaulted a former YSRCP MPTC in Edigapalli village (Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh) against a YSRCP MLA's proposed visit to Punganur town over allegations of corruption.

On 15 June 2024, members of ABVP staged a protest and burned the Pakistan flag in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) condemning the attack on a bus carrying Hindu pilgrims in the Rajouri district (Jammu and Kashmir) on 9 June and demanded strict action against the accused.

On 15 June 2024, a large number of TDP, JSP and BJP members staged protests in Punganur town (Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh) against a YSRCP MLA's proposed visit to the town. The protesters highlighted allegations of corruption against the YSRCP leader shouted 'Go Back' slogans to mark their protest.

On 15 June 2024, members of NSUI staged a torch light protest march in Delhi - New Delhi city (Delhi) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET exams and demanded an investigation into the issue.

Around 15 June 2024 (as reported), members of VHP and Bajrang Dal held a protest and burned the effigy of terrorism in Kawakol town (Nawada, Bihar) against the attack on Hindu pilgrims in Reasi, Jammu and Kashmir (coded separately).

On 15 June 2024, members of the BJP staged a protest, carrying and smashing earthen pots, near the office of an AAP state minister in the Delhi - Kalkaji area (South East Delhi, Delhi) condemning the AAP for failing to address the water crisis in the city.

On 15 June 2024, local people from Banjar village, including a BJP MLA, staged a dharna (sit-in protest) outside the Mini Secretariat in Kullu city (Himachal Pradesh) demanding the advancement of the work for widening the Aut-Luhri Highway.

On 15 June 2024, farmers from many villages, led by a BKU leader, staged a sit-in protest at the police chowki (outpost) in Biralsi village (Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh) against the lack of water at the Kaalarpur canal.

On 15 June 2024, members of Hindutva groups along with members of the BJP including an MLA and a former MLA staged a protest in front of the Dharwad Suburban police station in Dharwad city (Karnataka) demanding the police to take action against the Muslim youth who assaulted and injured three Hindu right wing members after they were stopped from transporting cattle (coded separately).

On 15 June 2024, members of the CPI(M) staged a protest in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the authorities to protect the rights of street vendors after a street vendor died during an eviction drive in the city. The protesters also demanded the DMK-led state government to create vending zones in the city.

On 15 June 2024, members of CYSS staged a protest and burned an effigy at the new bus stand in Kurukshetra city (Haryana) against the claimed irregularities in the NEET examinations and demanded a CBI inquiry into the issue.

On 15 June 2024, local people and family members of the deceased staged a protest along the highway at the Lalta Road crossing in Pura village (Chitrakoot, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused involved in the death of a man (likely a Dalit laborer based on the context) who was assaulted, on 11 June, for failing to fetch water on time (coded separately). The protesters also demanded compensation for the deceased's family.

On 15 June 2024, farmers of Thimmak Palli village staged a protest in front of the Chinnamalla Reddy Village Electricity Substation and on the Medak-Kamareddy main road in Chinnamallareddy village (Kamareddy district, Telangana) against the authorities for the delay in installing transformers for electricity connections in agricultural fields. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 15 June 2024, members of the KSU staged a protest in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) demanding the BJP-led Union government to cancel the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) over allegations of malpractice and corruption. The protesters also demanded in investigation into allegations of irregularities by the National Testing Agency (NTA) which conducted the NEET exam.

On 15 June 2024, Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) (female health) workers staged a protest at the Commissioner of Health and Family Welfare's office in the Koti locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to increase their salaries and to pay their salaries on the first day of every month as was promised in the INC's election manifesto before the state assembly elections.

On 15 June 2024, students under the aegis of the AISF staged a protest near the humanities building at the Osmania University campus in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to appoint vice-chancellors in state universities, fill up vacancies and provide free canteen and hostel facilities to students.

On 15 June 2024, local people and members of the Mahamaya Temple Committee (likely from the Hindu community based on context) staged a protest, raising slogans and carrying utensils, in front of the Water Resources Department office in Lad Bharol village (Mandi, Himachal Pradesh) against the shortage of drinking water in the area.

On 15 June 2024, members of INC, including its district and city presidents, staged a protest at the Collectorate in Sultanpur city (Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET examinations and demanded a high-level inquiry into the issue.

On 15 June 2024, members of INC staged a 'Matka Phod' (break the water pot) protest in the Delhi - Krishna Nagar area (East Delhi, Delhi) condemning BJP and the AAP and the BJP for failing to address the water crisis in the city.

On 15 June 2024, members of INC, including its state chief, staged 'Matka Phod' (break the water pot) protests at 280 blocks across Delhi (coded as Delhi - New Delhi city (Delhi)) condemning BJP and the AAP and the BJP for failing to address the water crisis in the city.

On 15 June 2024, INC and LDF councillors staged protests in front of the Kerala Water Authority (KWA) office in Piravom town (Ernakulam, Kerala) demanding the municipality officials to ensure a regular supply of drinking water.

On 15 June 2024, flood-affected residents led by Narmada Bachao Andolan leader started an indefinite hunger strike protest in Kheda village of Badnawar tehsil (Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh) against the devastation caused by the Sardar Sarovar Dam and demanded the complete rehabilitation of dam oustees. Officials from the Narmada Valley Development Authority (NVDA) and the local administration visited the protest site to unsuccessfully discuss the demands.

On 15 June 2024, approximately 200 members of the Vidarbha Rajya Andolan Samiti (VRAS) held a 'Power March' from Kharbi Chowk to the Kharbi Power House, raised slogans, and burned a symbolic prepaid meter, during a protest march, in Nagpur city (Maharashtra) against increased power tariff and the state government's decision to install prepaid meters.

On 15 June 2024, members of the KSU along with an INC MLA staged a protest by organising a day-long fast outside the Deputy Director of Education in Kozhikode city (Kerala) demanding the LDF-led state government to allot more Plus One batches in the Malabar districts to address the shortage of seats.

On 15 June 2024, students along with an INC MP staged a day-and-night protest for the sixth day at the Government Medical College in Palakkad city (Kerala) demanding the authorities to provide better facilities at the college and to appoint permanent faculty.

On 15 June 2024, residents and commuters staged a protest in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the authorities to repair an escalator that connected the Madras Export Processing Zone (MEPZ) over GST road to the Sanatorium bus stand, the suburban railway station and Siddha Hospital.

On 15 June 2024, members of SCS and medical students, led by the SCS national president, staged a protest at King George's Medical University in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET exams and demanded a re-examination.

On 15 June 2024, members of the Kerala Pradesh School Teachers' Association (KPSTA) took out a protest march to the District Education officer's (DEO) office in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the LDF-led state government's decision to increase the number of school working days to 220.

On 15 June 2024, a large number of people including members of Bajrang Dal and VHP staged a protest, raising slogans, at the police station in Allahabad city (Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh) against the police whom the protesters accused of arbitrary action.

On 15 June 2024, members of Hindu organizations, including VHP, the VHP district vice president, and city president of Hindu Raksha Dal (Hindu group), staged a protest, raising slogans, and burned an effigy at Bugrasi Chowk (intersection) in Siana city (Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh) condemning the attack on a bus carrying Hindu pilgrims in the Rajouri district (Jammu and Kashmir) on 9 June.
On 15 June 2024, local women from Daulatpur Kalan village staged a protest at the Block office in Siana city (Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh) against the issue of water logging in the village.

On 15 June 2024, dozens of residents, gathered at the assault site, and held a candlelight protest march in the Aundh area of Pune city (Maharashtra) against the fatal assault by criminals on a resident for money two days ago.

On 15 June 2024, family members of the deceased staged a protest along the Chandpur Road in Chuchaila Kalan village (Amroha, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a boy who the protesters claimed was murdered by his friends.

On 15 June 2024, residents of various villages staged a protest march (on tractor trolleys), raising slogans, to the Collectorate in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) against the implementation of the Highway Facility Green Belt project in the area - which the protesters claimed will result in the demolition of the houses of many people.

On 15 June 2024, residents of Atarsuma village staged a protest at the Collectorate in Sultanpur city (Uttar Pradesh) against the police administration whom the protesters accused of constructing a police station on land allocated for a road in the village.

On 15 June 2024, local people staged a protest along the Maskanwa-Gaurachok Road in Bhopatpur village (Gonda, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a man who died during a collision between two motor bikes.
On 15 June 2024, local people staged a protest, carrying and breaking water pots, in Bawani Khera town (Bhiwani, Haryana) against the shortage of drinking water in the area.

On 15 June 2024, residents of Chandpur village staged a dharna (sit-in protest) at the Collectorate in Muzaffarnagar city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against members of a family whom the protesters accused of assaulting them over the registration of a case against a member of the assailants family.

On 15 June 2024, local people staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Shivpuri locality in Orai city (Jalaun, Uttar Pradesh) after a man was electrocuted while going to the balcony. The protesters claimed that electric cables were close to the balconies of houses in the area, leading to fear and incidences of electrocution. There was an altercation between the protesters and a lineman.

On 15 June 2024, some local people staged a protest at the Akbar Nagar area in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) against the demolition driver carried out by the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) in the area.

On 15 June 2024, local people and family members of the deceased staged a protest and placed the deceased's body along the Banda Highway near Lohgara village (Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh) demanding the demolition of the house of the accused involved in the shooting and killing of a young man and demanded compensation for the family members of the deceased.

On 15 June 2024, members of INC led by the incumbent Member of Parliament, and a Member of the Legislative Assembly clashed with police in front of the Police Commissioner's office in Rajkot city (Gujarat) during a demonstration over various demands including removing the head of Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the game zone fire incident, and Rs 1 crore compensation for the affected families. Police detained a large number of INC members.

On 15 June 2024, a large number of students gathered, burned effigies, and tires, and held a demonstration in Patna city (Bihar) demanding the cancellation of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test-(Undergraduate) examination.

On 15 June 2024, some police aspirants shaved their heads and crouched like chickens in Pune city (Maharashtra) during the 2nd day of their protest to demand an increase in the age limit for recruitment to fill 17,471 constabulary posts in the state police.

On 15 June 2024, members of the Hindu Sangharsh Samiti (Hindu Struggle Committee) staged a protest 'day 3' at the Collectorate in Muzaffarnagar city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the revocation of the district banishment of a young Hindu leader.

On 15 June 2024, local traders staged a protest sit-in protest, raising slogans, in Firozabad city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against a policeman whom the protesters accused of assaulting and extorting money from a local trader (coded separately).

Around 15 June 2024 (as reported), people staged protests in Karnataka state (coded to Bengaluru city, Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the INC-led state government's decision to extend the exemption given to the Information Technology (IT) and Information Technology enabled Services (ITeS) sector from the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act.

Around 15 June 2024 (month of), dairy farmers staged a protest at the Tandra gate on the Srisailam-Hyderabad highway in Kalwakurthy city (Nagarkurnool, Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to release their payments and clear their dues.

Around 15 June 2024 (month of), West Siang District Olympic Association (WSDOA) staged a sit in protest in West Siang district (coded to Aalo town, Arunachal Pradesh) condemning the prolonged delay in the construction of West Siang stadium.

On 16 June 2024, BJP members led by a legislator held a sit-in protest at Kulti city (Paschim Bardhaman district, WB) over claimed stoppage of water supply by TMC controlled municipal authorities to the area after the Lok Sabha elections to BJP held areas.

On 16 June 2024, job card holders held a protest at Kahara town (Doda district, J&K) against the Rural Development Department over delay in release of pending wages for MGNREGA work (a rural employment scheme).

Around 16 June 2024 (as reported), locals, students and Meira Paibi activists (women torch bearers) staged a protest rally with placards under the banner 'Stop Desertification of Green Fields' from Nongpok Sekmai NESA ground to Ukhongsang Kangjeibung Lampak in Nongpok Sekmai village (Thoubal, Manipur) condemning the negative effects of quarrying activities on the environment and raised awareness for its protection.

On 16 June 2024, Democratic Students' Alliance of Manipur (DESAM) staged a protest and burned the effigies of Education Minister, Education Director and Education Commissioner in front of Oriental College at Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning the state government for not adhering to NEP 2020 guidelines in the recruitment of 1,140 pre-primary teachers and demanded the release of those arrested during a similar DESAM protest on June 13 (coded separately).

On 16 June 2024, Democratic Students' Alliance of Manipur (DESAM) staged a protest and burned the effigies of Education Minister, Education Director and Education Commissioner at Pangei Bazar (market) in Pangei village (Imphal East, Manipur) condemning the state government for not adhering to NEP 2020 guidelines in the recruitment of 1,140 pre-primary teachers and demanded the release of those arrested during a similar DESAM protest on June 13 (coded separately).

On 16 June 2024, candidates of All Manipur State Power Development Company Limited (MSPDCL) and Manipur State Power Company Limited (MSPCL) examination staged a protest rally in different parts of the city and culminated in front of the Chief Minister's residence in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning the delay in the announcement of exam results. Protesters were stopped at Nupi Lan Complex and a few of them were allowed to submit their memorandum to the CM's secretary.

On 16 June 2024, residents held a protest at Chingus town (Rajouri district, J&K) against illegal mining in the area claiming it was causing damage to local infrastructure and essential water resources.

On 16 June 2024, five members of a family attacked three members of another family with sharp weapons in Bhutadihi village (Nayagarh district, Odisha) after an argument turned an old dispute over land into a group clash. A 42-year-old man was killed and two others were injured.
