On 22 July 2024, truck drivers staged a protest on national highway 66 near Shirur village (Uttara Kannada, Karnataka) demanding the authorities to allow them to leave the area after a landslide blocked the highway and left the drivers stranded for eight days.

Around 22 July 2024 (as reported), new students of Kabi Nazrul Mahavidyalaya staged a sit in protest in their campus at Sonamura town (Sepahijala, Tripura) over the imposition of specific subjects for the new semester and claimed that they were not aware of the requirements prior to their admissions.

On 22 July 2024, members of the AMMK staged a protest in Thoothukudi city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for increasing the price of electricity and for failing to control inflation and the drug menace in the state.

On 22 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including former ministers staged a protest at the Allithurai Anna Ground in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government's proposal to merge 27 panchayats from the Srirangam, Manachanallur, Lalgudi and Tiruverumbur MLA constituencies with the Tiruchirappalli Municipal Corporation. The protesters said that the residents would not be eligible to work under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGS) (social employment scheme) and would have to pay higher taxes if the proposal was implemented.

On 22 July 2024, members of AMMK staged a protest near the District Collectorate in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increase in electricity charges and the deteriorating law and order situation in the state.

Around 22 July 2024 (as reported), members of the Shahigara colony, after the death of two boys by drowning, held a protest and refused to accept the bodies in Veraval city (Gir Somnath, Gujarat) demanding a solution to the water logging problem in the colony. The families agreed to take the bodies after the administration assured a permanent solution for the water drainage issue.

On 22 July 2024, YSRCP MLAs and MLCs staged a protest on the premises of the Andhra Pradesh Legislature in Amaravati city (Guntur, Andhra Pradesh) against the 'political murders' in the state after the TDP-JSP-BJP alliance came to power. The protesters wore black scarfs, displayed placards and demanded the imposition of President's Rule in the state. The police stopped the protesters, tore placards and banners resulting in an altercation (likely not violent as no injuries were inflicted).

On 22 July 2024, students including members of NSUI and ABVP held a protest at Jai Narayan Vyas University in Jodhpur city (Rajasthan) demanding the holding of student union elections. Police baton charged the protestors. Six persons were injured. Police detained five students.

On 22 July 2024, members of the OBCs community started an Arakshan (Reservations) Bachao OBC Jan Akrosh Yatra, a protest march, from Wadigodri village under Ambad tehsil (Jalna, Maharashtra) to protest OBC reservation by countering the hunger strike in Antarwali Sarathi village by the founder of Shivba Sanghatana.

On 22 July 2024, a group of upper caste students assaulted two Scheduled Caste (Dalit) students on the school premises in Kallimandayam village (Dindigul, Tamil Nadu) for not 'paying respects' to the upper caste group members while the students were playing kabaddi (contact team sport).

On 22 July 2024, 43 staff members launched a sit-in protest at the Government Arts and Science College campus in Kurumbalur town (Perambalur, Tamil Nadu) demanding the authorities to release their pending salaries. The staff members ended the protest on 12 August 2024.

On 22 July 2024, members of the Powerloom Units and Allied Industries Joint Action Committee (JAC) launched a relay hunger strike and a sit-in protest in Sircilla town (Rajanna Siricilla, Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to fulfil their demands which included releasing all pending dues, providing employment opportunities and electricity subsidies. The protesters marked the tenth day of the protest on 31 July 2024.

On 23 July 2024, civic volunteers (under the command of the state police) held a protest at Pundibari town (Cooch Behar district, WB) over claimed assault of a volunteer by a sub-inspector without any provocation. Police claimed the volunteer was intoxicated.

On 23 July 2024, AAP MPs staged a protest, carrying placards, at the Parliament premises in Delhi - Parliament Street (New Delhi, Delhi) against the BJP-led central government for misusing central agencies and mistreating the AAP national convener (Delhi Chief Minister) who is currently in jail over corruption charges in an excise police case.

On 23 July 2024, AIDWA members, led by its state secretary, staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) against the BJP-led central government over various issues including the suspected irregularities in the NEET exam and the privatization of healthcare services.

On 23 July 2024, BGRD members staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Ludhiana city (Punjab) demanding action against the accused involved in beef smuggling and the sale of beef in the city.

On 23 July 2024, Kanwariyas (Hindu pilgrims) assaulted 2 scooter-borne people along the National Highway 58 (NH-58) near Krishna Public School in Meerut city (Uttar Pradesh) after the scooter hit a Kanwariya and broke his Kanwar (a pot holding with water for religious purposes).

On 23 July 2024, members of the Dalit community staged a protest in Ghaziabad city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the arrest of the chairperson of Gyansthali Vidyapeeth College whom the protesters accused of abusing a student using casteist slurs.
On 23 July 2024, a large number of mid-day meal workers (health workers) and sanitation workers held a protest at Kathua city (J&K) to demand an increase in wages at par with other regions.

On 23 July 2024, INC members held a protests across districts at J&K (coded as Srinagar city, J&K) against the BJP-led central government over increase in militant attacks and amendments to the J&K reorganization act giving more powers to the governor before the assembly election.
On 23 July 2024, IYC members held a protest at Domana town (Jammu district, J&K) against the BJP-led central government over increase in militant attacks in J&K.
On 23 July 2024, JKNPP members led by a former minister held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) against the power department over the installation of smart power meters and lack of power supply.

On 23 July 2024, Cooperative Department employees gathered from across the state went on a 'pen-down strike' and staged a protest, raising slogans and burning an effigy, at the District Administrative Complex in Hoshiarpur city (Punjab) against the AAP-led state government, demanding the release of arrested employees who the protesters claimed were implicated over false charges by the Vigilance Bureau - the protesters also accused the Vigilance Bureau of harassment.

On 23 July 2024, members of the Pharmacy Officer Association went on strike and staged a protest at the Civil Hospital in Fatehabad city (Haryana) demanding a revision in the pay scale and recruitment for vacant posts.

On 23 July 2024, MSJK members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against inflation in essential items including power bills, lack of basic amenities and demanded that fuels be brought under the goods and services tax regime.

On 23 July 2024, people from the Muslim community staged a protest at the Inder Lok locality in the Delhi - Tri Nagar area (North West Delhi, Delhi) against the setting up of Kanwariya (Hindu religious pilgrims) camps in the area. A video of the incident was circulated online.

On 23 July 2024, students and NSUI members, led by the NSUI state-in-charge, staged a protest, carrying placards and banners, in front of the Shastri Bhavan (government building) in Delhi - Parliament Street (New Delhi, Delhi) against the suspected irregularities in the NEET exams and demanded re-examination.
On 23 July 2024, Yuva Rajput Sabha (A Rajput caste group) held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand restoration of statehood for J&K.

On 23 July 2024, members of the Punjab Students' Union staged a protest march and a dharna (sit-in protest) in front of the residence of an AAP MLA in Faridkot city (Punjab) against the state government's decision to implement the BSc Agriculture at Government Brijindra College in self-finance mode.
On 23 July 2024, locals held a protest by blocking a road at Merth village (Kathua district, J&K) against the administration over rain water flooding their houses damaging their equipment.
On 23 July 2024, scores of locals held a protest by blocking a road at Chankhan area in Sopore town (Baramulla district, J&K) against the water department over lack of water supply.
On 23 July 2024, residents held a protest by blocking a road at Mirgund town (Baramulla district, J&K) over lack of water supply in their area.

On 23 July 2024, local people assaulted an elderly man (shopkeeper) with slippers and tore his clothes in Hasanpur city (Amroha, Uttar Pradesh) who was caught while attempting to rape a minor Dalit girl.

On 23 July 2024, INC members held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) against the BJP-led central government over increase in militant attacks and amendments to the J&K reorganization act giving more powers to the governor before the assembly election. Police detained the leaders of the protest.

On 23 July 2024, local people tied a man to a tree and assaulted him at Nar Singh Colony under the Pathrala police station area (Bathinda, Punjab) who was accused of misbehaving with local people despite repeated warnings. The man had come to the village to meet his girlfriend.

On 23 July 2024, over 15-20 people including family members of the deceased assaulted a neurosurgeon and his team members with rods, chairs, and sticks, and vandalized medical equipment at a private hospital in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a man which the assailants claimed was caused by the hospital's negligence. The assailants also condemned the high medical fees. A video of the incident was circulated online.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force
text: Around 23 July 2024 (as reported), Kuki women of Sangaikot sub division dismantled bunkers belonging to 49 ITBP personnel in Churachandpur district (Churachandpur, Manipur) for the perceived inability of the personnel in ensuring peace and security in the area amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state.

On 23 July 2024, students of Noagaon Krishnanagar Higher Secondary School staged a protest in their campus near Govind Ballabh Pant Hospital in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) against their headmistress over the transfer order of their English teacher and the perceived restrictive policies and environment created by her in the school.

On 23 July 2024, hundreds of AIADMK members including a former minister staged a protest in Attur town (Salem, Tamil Nadu) as part of a state-wide protest against the DMK-led state government for increasing the prices of electricity and essential commodities.

On 23 July 2024, members of the INC including the Chief Minister, Deputy Chief Minister, MLAs and ministers staged a protest near the Mahatma Gandhi statue on the Vidhana Soudha premises in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the BJP-led Union government and government agencies such as the Enforcement Directorate for attempting to tarnish the reputation of the Chief Minister and the state government in connection with the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam case.

On 23 July 2024, Sarpanch (village head) and panch under the aegis of the Panch-Sarpanch Union from across the state gathered and held a dharna (sit-in protest) in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) over 20 points demands including an honorarium of Rs 15000 for Sarpanchs, Rs. 2000000 life insurance for Panch-Sarpanch, minimum pension of Rs 2000, etc. There was a split among the protesters over the invitation to INC state president to join the protest. One section left the venue after the INC leader joined the protest, and the other group tried to march towards the Chief Minister's house, but were stopped by police barricades.

On 23 July 2024, girl students of the Government Girls Vocational Higher Secondary School staged a protest on the road in BP Angadi village (Malappuram, Kerala) demanding the authorities to provide better civic and infrastructural facilities at the school including sturdy buildings, clean bathrooms and more classrooms.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests across Tamil Nadu state (coded to Chennai) against the DMK-led state government for increasing the price of electricity and for proposing to place restrictions on the distribution of tur dal and palm oil in fair price shops.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister staged protests in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for increasing the price of electricity and for proposing to place restrictions on the distribution of tur dal and palm oil in fair price shops.

On 23 July 2024, around 30 councillors belonging to various political parties including the DMK and the AIADMK staged a sit-in protest at the Corporation office in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) accusing the Corporation Commissioner of being biased and demanding his transfer.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including MLAs and a former Mayor staged a protest in Coimbatore town (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for increasing the prices of electricity, property tax and drinking water in the state.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister staged a protest in Dindigul city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increasing the prices of electricity and essential commodities in the state.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister, former MLAs and functionaries staged a protest in Erode city (Tamil Nadu) for increasing the prices of electricity, taxes and essential commodities. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 23 July 2024, residents of Annai Sathya Nagar on Bhavani Road and MGR Nagar in Kollampalayam staged a protest outside the Erode Corporation in Erode city (Tamil Nadu) against the authorities for imposing a higher property tax on their tenements that were constructed by the Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board (TNUHDB). The protesters also condemned the lack of basic civic amenities including drinking water, sanitation and garbage collection and held placards to mark their protest.

On 23 July 2024, members of the Nashik unit of Shiv Sena (UBT) held an hour-long protest at the Mumbai-Agra highway toll plaza in Ghoti Budruk city (Nashik district, Maharashtra) against the bad condition of the highway. After an hour, the Sena (UBT) members asked the motorists to leave without paying the toll fee.

On 23 July 2024, members of the BRS including MLAs and a former minister and BJP MLAs staged separate protests at the Gun Park in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against the INC-led state government for failing to implement the crop loan waiver without imposing any terms. The protesters also demanded financial assistance to Gram Panchayats (village governing institutions) raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 23 July 2024, locals, members of the INC, CPI(M) and the CPI staged a protest in Ibrahimpatnam town (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) after a boy drowned in a drain filled with ashes diverted from the Dr. Narla Tata Rao Thermal Power Station (NTTPS).The protesters demanded action against the power station authorities and compensation for the kin of the deceased.

On 23 July 2024, Kshetrigao Assembly Constituency's Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) and National Food Security Act (NFSA) beneficiaries staged a protest rally from his residence at Kshetri Awang Leikai to Imphal East's District Commissioner (DC) office, Porompat in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding authorities to release NFSA rice allocation for over 25,000 beneficiaries pending since November 2023 within 4 days.

On 23 July 2024, Lamphel Supermarket Coordinating Committee (Meitei group) staged a sit in protest at the supermarket in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the withdrawal of Assam Rifles from Manipur, claiming they were partisan towards the Kuki community and condemned the government's arrests of armed Meitei volunteers amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.
Around 23 July 2024 (as reported), locals staged a road block protest in Kakraban town (Gomati, Tripura) condemning the poor road conditions in the area and demanded prompt road repairs.
On 23 July 2024, students led by a local INC leader held a sit-in protest in Karadiya village (Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh) over the lack of teaching staff in the village.

On 23 July 2024, hundreds of AIADMK members including a former minister staged a protest in Komarapalayam town (Namakkal, Tamil Nadu) as part of a state-wide protest against the DMK-led state government for increasing the prices of electricity and essential commodities. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 23 July 2024, members of the Telangana Vibhinna Pratibhavantula Sangham (TVPS) (organisation for persons with disabilities) staged a protest in Kothagudem city (Bhadradri Kothagudem, Telangana) condemning the demeaning remarks made by an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) official about reservations for persons with disabilities (PwDs). The protesters demanded action against the official.

On 23 July 2024, employees of the Malabar Devaswom Board under the aegis of the Kerala Temple Employees' Coordination Committee (Hindu group) took out a protest march and staged a protest in front of the Kozhikode civil station in Kozhikode city (Kerala) against the LDF-led state government for not setting up a common fund to improve the financial condition of temples as per a court order and for not increasing their wages. The protesters took a buffalo on a truck to mark their protest.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including an MLA staged a protest in Krishnagiri city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increase in electricity charges and the prices of essential commodities.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including an MLA staged a protest in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increase in electricity charges. The protesters also condemned the killing of the Tamil Nadu BSP chief (coded separately) and highlighted the deteriorating law and order situation in the state.

On 23 July 2024, relatives and family members of a four year old girl who was kidnapped, raped and killed by a labourer staged a protest in Magadi town (Ramanagara, Karnataka) demanding the police to take action against the accused.

On 23 July 2024, members of Dakshina Kannada District Taximen and Maxicab Association staged a protest in Mangaluru city (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) against the INC-led state government's proposal to install vehicle location tracking devices and emergency panic buttons in vehicles. The protesters also opposed the 'white board' registered vehicles that were operating as 'taxis' in the city.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including MLAs and a former Mayor staged a protest in Mettupalayam town (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for increasing the prices of electricity, property tax and drinking water in the state.

On 23 July 2024, autorickshaw owners and drivers under the banner of Federation of Karnataka Drivers staged a protest in Mysuru city (Karnataka) against the INC-led state government's proposal to install vehicle location tracking devices and emergency panic buttons in vehicles. The protesters also opposed the 'white board' registered vehicles that were operating as 'taxis' in the city.

On 23 July 2024, hundreds of AIADMK members staged protests in Namakkal district (coded to Namakkal city, Tamil Nadu) as part of a state-wide protest against the DMK-led state government for increasing the prices of electricity and essential commodities.

On 23 July 2024, over 200 AASU activists including their leaders staged a human chain protest in Lakhimpur district (coded to North Lakhimpur town, Lakhimpur, Assam) demanding the prompt repair of national highway 15 passing from Narayanpur to Harmoti through Bandadewa.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including an MLA staged a protest at the Thiruvalluvar Thidal in Pollachi town (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for increasing the price of electricity, drinking water and property tax in the state.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister staged a protest in Pudukkottai town (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increase in the price of electricity in the state.

On 23 July 2024, members of the Dalit community took out a protest march to the Deputy Commissioner's office in Ramanagara city (Karnataka) demanding the authorities to provide protection to the community members after members of upper caste groups attacked Dalits in the district twice (coded separately).

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister staged a protest in Ramanathapuram city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for increasing the electricity charges in the state.

On 23 July 2024, hundreds of AIADMK members staged protests in Salem district (coded to Salem city, Tamil Nadu) as part of a state-wide protest against the DMK-led state government for increasing the prices of electricity and essential commodities.

On 23 July 2024, hundreds of AIADMK members including a former minister staged a protest at the Salem Fort Maidan in Salem city (Tamil Nadu) as part of a state-wide protest against the DMK-led state government for increasing the prices of electricity and essential commodities.
On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK staged a protest in Thanjavur city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increase in electricity charges in the state.

On 23 July 2024, farmers staged a protest in Thappetlamorsu village (Jogulamba Gadwal, Telangana) demanding the authorities to release the pending compensation for their land that was acquired by the state government for the Bharat Mala (road connectivity) project.

On 23 July 2024, representatives of five residents associations in Thiruvananthapuram staged a protest at the Vellayambalam Kerala Water Authority office in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) demanding the authorities to take measures to restore the water supply after the residents faced a disruption of their water supply due to the ongoing road work in the area.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former MP staged protests in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for the increase in the electricity charges in the state. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister staged a protest in front of the District Collector's office in Tirupattur city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for increasing the price of electricity and for proposing to place restrictions on the distribution of tur dal and palm oil in fair price shops.

On 23 July 2024, members of Dakshina Kannada District Taximen and Maxicab Association staged a protest in Udupi city (Udupi, Karnataka) against the INC-led state government's proposal to install vehicle location tracking devices and emergency panic buttons in vehicles. The protesters also opposed the 'white board' registered vehicles that were operating as 'taxis' in the city.

On 23 July 2024, members of the AIADMK including a former minister staged a protest near the new bus stand in Viluppuram city (Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government for increasing the price of electricity and for proposing to place restrictions on the distribution of tur dal and palm oil in fair price shops.

On 23 July 2024, members of the CPI staged a protest outside the Visakhapatnam Railway Station in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the BJP-led union government for not allocating funds for the railway sector and for the backward districts in Andhra Pradesh in the 2024 Union budget.

On 23 July 2024, locals of Wangoo Ahallup Makha Sandangkhong Awang Leikai and Mayai Leikai including local club members and Meira Paibi activists staged a protest in Wangoo Ahallup village area (Bishnupur, Manipur) demanding the immediate construction of Sagang Sugnu road. Protesters threatened of further agitation if their demand was not met.

On 23 July 2024, members of the CPI(M) staged a protest and attempted to 'lay siege' to the Mangaluru City Corporation (MCC) in Mangaluru city (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) demanding the removal of the MCC Commissioner over allegations that he had 'disproportionate assets'. The protesters accused the official of stealing public funds and shouted slogans to mark their protest. Police arrested the protesters.

On 23 July 2024, members of Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) clashed with police, during a two hours long demonstration at Vandana Convent School in Guna city (Madhya Pradesh) after the principal halted a sixth-grade student from chanting Sanskrit verses during the morning assembly. The principal had issued an apology. They ended the demonstration after the District Education Officer gave assurances. Police filed an FIR against the principal.

On 23 July 2024, members of the OBCs community, on the 2nd day of Arakshan (reservations) Bachao OBC Jan Akrosh Yatra, a protest march, reached Chaklamba village (Beed, Maharashtra) to protest OBC reservation by countering the hunger strike in Antarwali Sarathi village by the founder of Shivba Sanghatana.

On 24 July 2024, a large number of INC members, including AIMC and schedule tribe wing leaders and former ministers held a protest and engaged in a minor scuffle (likely non-violent as there were no injuries) with a policeman at Samba town (J&K) against the BJP-led central government over increase in militant attacks, unemployment, installation of smart power meters and amendments to the J&K reorganization act giving more powers to the governor before the assembly election. They also demanded restoration of statehood for J&K and early holding of assembly elections.

On 24 July 2024, hundreds of members of the Association of the Visually Handicapped staged a protest, raising slogans, along the Chhota Shimla-Sanjauli Road near the Secretariat in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) over various demands including the non-completion of the backlog recruitments. The protesters scuffled with the police and protesters were forcibly removed from the protest site.

On 24 July 2024, Kanwariyas (Hindu pilgrims) assaulted a man and vandalized his motorcycle along the Saharanpur-Dehradun Highway in the Saharanpur district (Uttar Pradesh) after the motorcycle hit a Kanwariya and broke his Kanwar (a pot holding water for religious purposes).

On 24 July 2024, members of the Dalit community staged protests at several locations in Ghaziabad city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the arrest of the chairperson of Gyansthali Vidyapeeth College whom the protesters accused of abusing a student using casteist slurs.

On 24 July 2024, farmers held a protest at Gonipora town (Kupwara district, J&K) against the mechanical department for failing to make a irrigation pump operational leading to a paddy field drying up.

On 24 July 2024, farmers and laborers on the '587th day' of their indefinite protest burned copies of the budget in the Jind district (Haryana) against the BJP-led central government for failing to address the concerns and demands of the farmers and laborers in the budget. The protesters have been demanding a Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops, loan waivers for farmers, and restoration of the old pension scheme, among others.

On 24 July 2024, a man (para-athlete) accompanied by his supporters (NGO members) staged a sit-in protest, carrying placards and raising slogans, in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Ludhiana city (Punjab) against the failure of the state government to provide him employment despite winning accolades for the nation at various international tournaments. The man also polished shoes as a symbolic gesture of protest.

On 24 July 2024, National Health Mission (NHM) employees went on a 2-hour strike and staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Civil Hospital in Fatehabad city (Haryana) over various demands including the provision of benefits as stated within the 7th pay commission.

On 24 July 2024, scores of workers from the National Health Mission (NHM) went on a 2-hour strike and staged a protest at the District Civil Hospital in Karnal city (Haryana) over various demands including regularization, retirement benefits, allowances, free medical facilities, and leaves.

On 24 July 2024, workers from the National Health Mission (NHM) went on a 2-hour strike and staged a protest, raising slogans, at the District Civil Hospital in Sirsa city (Haryana) over various demands including regularization, retirement benefits, allowances, free medical facilities, and leaves.

On 24 July 2024, Kanwariyas (Hindu pilgrims) vandalized an auto-rickshaw and assaulted the driver with rods and sticks in Libberheri village (Haridwar, Uttar Pradesh) over accusations that the auto-rickshaw hit a Kanwariya and broke his Kanwar (a pot holding water for religious purposes). The driver denied the accusations. A video of the incident was circulated online.

On 24 July 2024, local people and family members of the deceased staged a protest along the Shamsabad-Fatehabad Road near Dhimsiri village (Agra, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a man who died due to electrocution while repairing an electric line at a tubewell. The protesters demanded action against negligent officials and compensation for the deceased.

On 24 July 2024, members of the INDIA (alliance) including MPs from INC, SP, and TMC staged a protest at the Parliament premises in Delhi - Parliament Street (New Delhi, Delhi)) against the union budget which the protesters claimed was discriminatory and failed to address local needs of states.

On 24 July 2024, a large numbers of INC and IYC members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the BJP-led central government over increase in militant attacks and to demand the restoration of statehood.
On 24 July 2024, transporters along with locals held a protest at Taveri bridge in Ramnagar tehsil (Udhampur district, J&K) over the poor condition of the Chanunta-Udhampur road.
On 24 July 2024, local traders held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over Chinese garlic being sold in the market despite a ban.

On 24 July 2024, water supply pump operators and sanitation workers staged a protest, raising slogans, outside the Municipal Council in Sirhind-Fatehgarh city (Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab) over various demands including an increase in the honorarium amount, and timely payment of wages.

On 24 July 2024, members of the District Bar Association (DBA) continued their indefinite strike 'and staged a protest march 'day 3' to the Court Complex in Chandigarh city against the decision to implement the Chandigarh Union Territory Tenancy Act (2019).

On 24 July 2024, a large number of displaced persons from Pakistan who now have Indian citizenship held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand allotment of 10 marla plots and provision of 12 assembly seats, schedule tribe status among other demands.

On 24 July 2024, students staged a protest outside the residence of an AAP MLA in Faridkot city (Punjab) against the state education department's decision to implement the BSc Agricultura course (Government Brijindra College) in self-finance mode.

On 24 July 2024, Bajrang Dal and VHP members staged a bike rally and a protest 'day 2' outside the Superintendent of Police's (SP) residence in Banda city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding strict action against the Tindwari police station-in-charge whom the protesters accused of assaulting a VHP and a Bajrang Dal leader on earlier in the night (coded separately). The policeman and 2 constables were sent on line duty (as a form of punishment).

On 24 July 2024, the YSRCP president (MLA, former Chief Minister) and his supporters, joined by several leaders of the INDIA (alliance) including the SP Chief (MP), a TMC MP, an AIADMK MP, and 2 SS(UBT) MPs, staged a dharna (sit-in protest) at Jantar Mantar in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) over the rise in political violence in the Andhra Pradesh state and claimed that his party workers were being attacked.

On 24 July 2024, local people staged a protest along Lambi Road in Gidderbaha town (Sri Muktsar Sahib, Punjab) opposing the construction of a material recovery factory (MRF) and a waste collection center in the area.

text: On 27 August 2024, over 5000 people under the banner of Paschimbanga Chhatra Samaj (a student group) along with BJP and RSS leaders and members of other organizations including of Mahakal Nath Yogi Sena Seva Sangha, Brahmamayee Mahakali Ashram (right wing Hindu groups) and Sangrami Joutha Mancha (state government employees) held a demonstration march, pelted stones, glass bottles, broke barricades and clashed with police and RAF who responded with tear gas shells, water cannon and baton charge, from College Square in central Calcutta, Santragachhi and Howrah Maidan, Howrah bridge ending at state secretariat in Nabanna in Howrah (coded as Howrah city, WB), over the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case and demanded resignation of the chief minister of WB. At least 35 policemen and an unspecified number of women demonstrators were left injured and a police bike was set on fire in the incident. Police later arrested over 220 persons.
On 27 August 2024, members of the INC held a protest in all wards under Kolhapur city (Maharashtra) over the inferior quality of roads and the high number of potholes.
On 27 August 2024, members of INC led by the former chief minister held a protest in Karad city (Maharashtra) against the collapse of Shivaji Maharaj's statue at Fort Rajkot.

On 27 August 2024, members of the MNREGA Employees Union and Panchayat Secretaries Union held a dharna (sit-in protest) at Randhir Verma Chowk in Dhanbad city (Jharkhand) over various demands including regularization of MNREGA workers, amendment in honorarium and other facilities.

On 27 August 2024, members of the Mukhiya Union started an indefinite dharna (sit-in protest) in front of Raj Bhawan in Ranchi city (Jharkhand) over various demands, including the direct disbursal of the funds from the state finance commission.

On 27 August 2024, members of nine Rotary Clubs from the Kolhan region, including Jamshedpur West, Jamshedpur Green, Chaibasa Rotary Club, Jamshedpur Rotary Club Main, Jamshedpur Dalma Rotary Club, Jamshedpur Mid Town, Rotary Club Jamshedpur Femina, Rotary Club Jamshedpur Steel City, and Rotary Club Jamshedpur East, held a protest rally in Sakchi area of Jamshedpur city (East Singhbhum, Odisha) demanding justice for the victim in the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case.

On 27 August 2024, a group of people including members of a cow protection group assaulted and killed a man (Muslim) in Hansawas Khurd village (Bhiwani, Haryana) over suspicions of consuming beef (cow meat). The police arrested 7 people.
On 27 August 2024, people staged a protest in Tiruvennanallur village (Viluppuram, Tamil Nadu) against the district officials for attempting to demolish a church as per a high court order.

On 28 August 2024, a large number of womenfolk clashed with police forces and forcefully freed a KCP (N) cadre at Sekta village (Imphal East, Manipur) who was arrested during a search operation in the village, claiming that he was an armed volunteer amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Security forces fired some rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the crowd. No casualties.

On 28 August 2024, hundreds of INC Mahila members held placards, raised slogans against the BJP government, and held a sit-in protest as part of 'Nari Nyay Andolan' in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) demanding the implementation of Mahalaxmi Yojana. They were stopped by female police forces.

On 28 August 2024, a former employee and his associates abducted, assaulted, and burned the private parts of a tailor (likely Muslim based on name) in Kandivali West city (coded to Mumbai Suburban - Borivali, Maharashtra) on suspicion of design theft.

On 28 August 2024, a group of parents and locals assaulted, stripped, and paraded a tuition teacher in Palghar district (Maharashtra), over claimed misbehavior with girl students. They later handed him over to the police.

On 28 August 2024, members of Shiv Sena (UBT) and supporters of the BJP member of Lok Sabha from Ratnagiri-Sindhudurg seat clashed and threw stones at Rajkot Fort in Malvan town (Sindhudurg district, Maharashtra) during the visit by the Shiv Sena (UBT) and NCP (SP) leaders over the collapse of eight-month-old Chhatrapati Shivaji statue at Rajkot Fort. A policeman was injured.

On 28 August 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests for the second day across Tamil Nadu state (coded to Chennai) against the BJP state president for his derogatory remarks against the AIADMK's general secretary. The protesters burned effigies of the BJP leader to mark their protest.

On 28 August 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests near the central bus stand in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against the BJP state president for his derogatory remarks against the AIADMK's general secretary. The protesters burned posters of the BJP leader to mark their protest.

On 28 August 2024, members of the AIADMK staged protests near the near the check post in Viralimalai town (Pudukkottai, Tamil Nadu) against the BJP state president for his derogatory remarks against the AIADMK's general secretary.

On 28 August 2024, members of the AIADMK including an MLA staged a protest in front of the Electricity Department headquarters in Puducherry city (Puducherry) against the BJP-AINRC state government for increasing the price of electricity.
On 28 August 2024, members of the BJP including an MP staged a protest in Bijapur city (Vijayapura, Karnataka) against the INC-led state government and Chief Minister.

On 28 August 2024, members of the BJYM staged rasta roko (road block) protests in across Dakshina Kannada district (coded to Mangaluru, Karnataka) against the police for the delay in registering a case against an INC MLC who had made a demeaning comment about the Karnataka Governor.

On 28 August 2024, members of the BJYM staged rasta roko (road block protests near the Thokkottu junction in Ullal town (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) against the police for the delay in registering a case against an INC MLC who had made a demeaning comment about the Karnataka Governor.

On 28 August 2024, members of the BJYM staged rasta roko (road block protests in Bantval town (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) against the police for the delay in registering a case against an INC MLC who had made a demeaning comment about the Karnataka Governor.

On 28 August 2024, members of the BJYM staged rasta roko (road block protests in Puttur town (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) against the police for the delay in registering a case against an INC MLC who had made a demeaning comment about the Karnataka Governor.

On 28 August 2024, members of the BJYM staged rasta roko (road block protests in Sullia town (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) against the police for the delay in registering a case against an INC MLC who had made a demeaning comment about the Karnataka Governor.

On 28 August 2024, members of the BJYM and the BJP including an MLA and an MP staged rasta roko (road block) protests in Mangaluru city (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) against the police for the delay in registering a case against an INC MLC who had made a demeaning comment about the Karnataka Governor. Police detained the protesters.

On 28 August 2024, members of the CPI(M) staged a protest for the first day at the Penukonda Sub-Collector's office in Penukonda town (Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh) against the lack of provisions in the Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R&R) package given to individuals who had given up their agricultural land for the Nasan and BHEL industries in Sri Sathya Sai district.

On 28 August 2024, members of the CPI(M), the AIDWA, DYFI, SFI and other organisations staged a protest in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) against the rising instances of violence against the women and to condemn the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case where an on-duty trainee doctor was raped and murdered at the R.G. Kar Government Medical College and Hospital on 9 August 2024.

On 28 August 2024, several members of the CPI(M) including a councillor staged a protest near the Ripon Building in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) against the Greater Chennai Corporation's proposal to close down and merge some schools. The protesters also demanded the corporation to withdraw the increase in professional taxes and trade license fees.

On 28 August 2024, residents of Kaliyur village and nearby hamlets including Kalarur, Kodumampalli and Pachur, along with farmers staged a road block protest on the Natrampalli-Tirupattur Main Road (coded to Natrampalli town, Tirupattur, Tamil Nadu) against the proposal to re-open a private stone quarry in the village.

On 28 August 2024, farmers from Kodangal staged a protest in front of the Mandal Revenue Office in Dudyal village (Vikarabad, Telangana) against the INC-led state government plan to acquire land to set up pharmaceutical companies. A female farmer held a bottle of pesticide and threatened to die by suicide. Other protesters intervened and took the bottle from her.

On 28 August 2024, dairy farmers staged a protest during the opening of a Sangam Dairy outlet at Srinivasnagar locality in Miryalaguda city (Nalgonda, Telangana) demanding the VT Dairy officials to release their pending payments.

On 28 August 2024, a few corporators staged a protest before a meeting at the municipal corporation office in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) demanding action against the tray dog menace and the viral fevers in the city. The protesters also demanded the corporation authorities to ensure a regular supply of drinking water.

On 28 August 2024, a group of people including a Hindu seer and family members of those who died in a landslip in Shirur village staged a protest in Karwar city (Uttara Kannada, Karnataka) demanding the INC-led state government to give more compensation to the kin of the deceased and to restart the search operations.

On 28 August 2024, a large number of Kokrajhar INC's members organized a protest with slogans in front of the Sub-Divisional office of the Electricity Department in Kokrajhar town (Kokrajhar, Assam) against the installation of smart meters and increase in electricity tariffs.
On 28 August 2024, Kokrajhar INC's members organized a protest in Gossaigaon town (Kokrajhar, Assam) against the installation of smart meters and increase in electricity tariffs.

On 28 August 2024, Sivasagar unit of INC staged a protest with slogans against Assam Power Distribution Company Limited (APDCL) and Assam's Power Minister outside the APDCL office in Sivasagar town (Sivasagar, Assam) over the installation of smart meters claiming that they caused a rise in electricity bills.

On 28 August 2024, farmers affiliated to the KRRS staged a protest in front of the KIADB (Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board) Office in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding the authorities to give jobs to the children of farmers who lost their land to the industries set up by the KIADB.

On 28 August 2024, members of the Telangana Samagra Siksha Employees Union (TSSEU) staged a protest in front of the Collectorate in Adilabad city (Telangana) demanding the INC-led state government to regularise their services, provide a basic pay and other benefits.

On 28 August 2024, lawyers under the banner of the Advocates Joint Action Committee (JAC) staged a protest by forming a human chain outside the combined court complex in Coimbatore city (Tamil Nadu) as part of a statewide protest against the implementation of the three new criminal laws by the BJP-led Union government which sought to replace the Indian Penal Code, the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Indian Evidence Act. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 28 August 2024, members of various lawyer associations and unions under the banner of the Joint Action Forum for Justice staged an 'All India Human Chain' protest in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the implementation of the three new criminal laws by the BJP-led Union government which sought to replace the Indian Penal Code, the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Indian Evidence Act.

On 28 August 2024, All Wangjing, Lamding, Kairembikhok Clubs' Organisation and Meira Paibi activists organized a sit in protest at Wangjing-Heirok Lamkhai junction in Wangjing town (Thoubal, Manipur) condemning the arrest of 2 KYKL cadres by Thoubal police commando on 26 August and demanded their release, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 28 August 2024, Khongjom Circle Apunba Meira Paibi staged a sit in protest at Khongjom village (Thoubal, Manipur) condemning the arrest of 2 KYKL cadres by Thoubal police commando on 26 August and demanded their release, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 28 August 2024, members of MVA and NCP (SCP) led by MP held a protest in Baramati city (Pune, Maharashtra) against the collapse of the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's (Maratha and Hindutva icon) statue at Rajkot Fort.

On 28 August 2024, members of NSUI garlanded with shoes and burned the effigy of the state chief minister at the Rajasthan University (RU) main gate in Jaipur city (Rajasthan) during a protest over increasing crimes against children and women in the state.

Around 28 August 2024 (as reported), students staged a protest at the Zilla Parishad High School in Tadepalli suburb in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against the transfer of their social studies teacher. The protesters held placards to mark their protest.

On 28 August 2024, students and teachers of Government Polytechnic Imphal staged a sit in protest with banners in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning the rampant and high monetary demands imposed by several armed organizations amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters demanded for a peaceful academic atmosphere.

On 28 August 2024, a large number of teachers affiliated to the Tamil Nadu Retired College Teachers Association (TANRECTA) staged a protest in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) as part of a statewide protest demanding the DMK-led state government to increase their salaries, pensions and allowances.

On 28 August 2024, over 20,000 members of the tribal community held a protest marched from Tapovan to the Tribal Development Commissionerate in Nashik city (Maharashtra) over their demand for mega recruitment of tribals under the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) (PESA) Act 1996.

On 28 August 2024, members of the UDF, the BJP and women's organisations staged protests for the second day in front of an actor and CPI(M) MLA's residence in Kollam city (Kerala) demanding his resignation after a woman actor accused him of sexual assault in light of the publication of the Hema committee report which detailed instances of sexual abuse and gender discrimination in the Malayalam film industry.

On 28 August 2024, members of the Mahilodaya Mahila Okkoota (Mahilodaya Women's Union) took out a protest march in Mysuru city (Karnataka) against the increasing cases of violence against women and to condemn the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case where an on-duty trainee doctor was raped and murdered at the R.G. Kar Government Medical College and Hospital on 9 August 2024.

On 28 August 2024, villagers of Bisra block held a symbolic road blockade near Kukudagate level-crossing in the suburbs of Rourkela city (Sundargarh district, Odisha) during a protest demanding early completion of the ongoing road-over-bridge (ROB) project and improvement of NH-320 D from Rourkela to Jareikela.

On 28 August 2024, half a dozen villagers 'created a ruckus', shouted slogans, and threatened employees in the electricity office located in the Bajaria area of Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) against the Madhya Pradesh Madhya Kshetra Vidyut Vitaran Company Limited (MPMKVVCL)'s drive to regularize illegal connections.

On 28 August 2024, local activists from various political parties and social organizations held a protest in Jawhar taluka (Palghar, Maharashtra), demanding capital punishment for the accused involved in sexually assaulting a child.

On 28 August 2024, members of the Erode District Hearing Impaired Welfare Association staged a sit-in protest on the premises of the Collectorate in Erode city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to fulfil their demands which included the relaxing norms at the Erode District Central Cooperative Bank, providing loans and driving licences, providing houses under the Kalaignar Kanavu Illam Scheme (government scheme) and ensuring their rights as per the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2018.

On 28 August 2024, villagers staged a protest for the 764th day in Ekanapuram village (Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu) against the DMK-led state government's notice to acquire land for the Parandur greenfield airport. The protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 28 August 2024, members of the Nagarika Hitarakshana Vedikegala Okkuta (Union of Civil Defense Forums) staged a protest on the premises of the city corporation in Shimoga city (Shivamogga, Karnataka) demanding the authorities to remove an unauthorised shed that was set up on the road by the Shivamogga Bhadravathi Urban Development Authority office in the Vinobnagar locality.

On 28 August 2024, over 200 people staged a protest at a school in Purusanahalli village (Bengaluru Rural, Karnataka) against the school management after a student died after a snake bit him near his school when he went to pick coconuts from a grove near the school based on the instructions from his teacher. The protesters accused the school of negligence and demanded action against the authorities.

On 28 August 2024, various political parties, organizations and locals staged a protest in Dhakuakhana town (Lakhimpur, Assam) against a non Assamese businessman for physically assaulting a differently abled minor with the staffs of his store. Protesters also closed his store and threatened of severe consequences an apology was not issued within 3 hours.

On 28 August 2024, Peoples Committee on Restoration of Loktak and Its Associate Wetland Manipur (PCRLAWM) organized a protest rally with slogans, attended by villagers living around Loktak lake from Ithai community hall after a public meeting till Ithai dam (Bishnupur, Manipur) demanding Manipur government to take charge of Ithai barrage and keep the 5 gates open till November to prevent flooding across the valley districts.

On 28 August 2024, locals staged a sit in protest with placards and slogans at Lalambung Takhellambam Leikai in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) against the planting of a grenade at the residence of a member of the Board of Directors, Salai Holdings (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 28 August 2024, students and staff of Teresian College took out a protest march in Mysuru city (Karnataka) against the increasing cases of violence against women. The protesters demanded the BJP-led Union government to start a country-wide campaign to educate the public about the importance of gender equality.

On 28 August 2024, residents evicted from Silsako staged a demonstration with placards and slogans outside the Assam Legislative Assembly in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) demanding compensation and rehabilitation. Demonstrators physically clashed with police forces after a woman police officer slapped a female demonstrator while some demonstrators were forcibly removed from the area.

On 28 August 2024, a group of local people assaulted a policeman (constable), tore his clothes, and removed his turban, near Dinewal village (Tarn Taran, Punjab) over accusations of registering a false theft case. The policeman received injuries in different parts of his body.

On 28 August 2024, AAP members staged protests at a few locations in the Haryana state (coded as Chandigarh city) against a BJP MP whom the protesters accused of making negative remarks against farmers, and demanded the termination of her MP membership

On 28 August 2024, BJP supporters of one faction held a protest at Katra town (Reasi district, J&K) over being denied ticket to their leader ahead of the state assembly elections.

On 28 August 2024, BJP members staged a protest and burned an effigy in Rohtak city (Haryana) demanding action against INC and AIMC members, including an INC MLA, for disrupting the work of, and clashing with (likely non-violent), BJP and BJP-MM members on 24 August - including hurling casteist slurs at a female Dalit member of BJP-MM (coded separately).

On 28 August 2024, between 30-50 BJP members including a minister held protests as part of 12-hour shutdown call at Shantipur town (Nadia district, WB) over the police action against the demonstrators in Nabanna area in Howrah city (coded separately).

On 28 August 2024, between 30-50 BJP members led by a minister held a protest as part of 12-hour shutdown call at Nandigram town (Purba Medinipur district, WB) over the police action against the demonstrators in Nabanna area in Howrah city (coded separately).

On 28 August 2024, locals including a district development council member from BJP held a protest at Gande village in Miran Sahib block area (Jammu district, J&K) over the installation of Auqaf board on the burial ground for infants.

On 28 August 2024, BJYM members staged a protest march towards the residence of an INC leader (former Chief Minister and Leader of the Opposition) in Chandigarh city (Haryana) condemning the INC for halting the recruitment process and contributing to the rise in unemployment. The protesters jostled with the police.

On 28 August 2024, hundreds of BKU (Ugrahan) members staged a protest near Saraud village (Sangrur, Punjab) against the acquisition of land near Saraud village by the National Highway Authority of India for the construction of the Delhi-Katra expressway. The police stopped the protesters from marching towards the village resulting in a minor scuffle between them (likely non-violent due to lack of injuries and other details indicating the use of physical violence).

On 28 August 2024, members of BKU (Lokhit) staged a protest at the Gandhi statue along the Garh-Delhi Road in Hapur city (Uttar Pradesh) against a BJP MP whom the protesters accused of making negative remarks against farmers, and demanded her removal from the BJP and the registration of police case against her. The police prevented the protesters from burning an effigy.

On 28 August 2024, members of Jamhoori Kisan Sabha (JKS) (farmer group) staged protests outside the offices of cooperative societies and the Assistant Registrar in Tarn Taran city (Punjab) against the suspected prevalence of corruption in cooperative institutions.

On 28 August 2024, members of Jamhoori Kisan Sabha (JKS) (farmer group) staged protests outside the offices of cooperative societies and the Assistant Registrar in Patti city (Tarn Taran, Punjab) against the suspected prevalence of corruption in cooperative institutions.

On 28 August 2024, members of Jamhoori Kisan Sabha (JKS) (farmer group) staged protests outside the offices of cooperative societies and the Assistant Registrar in Khadur Sahib town (Tarn Taran, Punjab) against the suspected prevalence of corruption in cooperative institutions.

On 28 August 2024, members of the Sarpanch (village chief) Association staged a massive protest in Jhajjar city (Haryana) against the registration of a case filed against a sarpanch and his son by the electricity department.

On 28 August 2024, Community Health Officers (CHOs) staged a protest march, wearing black bands, to the National Health Mission (NHM) office in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) over various demands including regularization and a revision of the Attendance Management System (AMS). The protesters engaged in a scuffle with the police (pushing and shoving) when they intervened in the protest march - badges and nameplates of CHOs and policemen fell on the ground.

On 28 August 2024, around 70 doctors gathered from various districts and staged a 2-hour protest at the office of the Health Directorate in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) against the non-implementation of the Special Dynamic Assured Career Progression (SDACP) scheme.
On 28 August 2024, junior doctors held a protest march at Kolkata city (WB) over the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case and to demand justice.
On 28 August 2024, Anganwadi workers staged a protest, carrying banners and raising slogans, at the Collectorate in Haridwar city (Uttarakhand) demanding an increase in honorarium and monthly pay.

On 28 August 2024, supporters of a independent candidate and former JKNC leader held a protest at Manjakote town (Rajouri district, J&K) over being denied ticket ahead of the state assembly elections.
On 28 August 2024, voluntary retired transport workers held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand release of pending dues.

On 28 August 2024, employees under the banner of the Municipal Employees Sangharsh (Struggle) Committee staged a protest rally in front of the Municipal Corporation's (MC) Zone A office at Mata Rani Chowk (intersection) in Ludhiana city (Punjab) over various demands including regularization and the provision of permanent posting for class 4 employees.

On 28 August 2024, hundreds of MGNREGA Rozgar Prapat Mazdoor Union (labor group) and CPI members staged a protest at the Block Development and Panchayat Office (BDPO) in Jalalabad city (Fazilka, Punjab) demanding the allotment of MGNREGA works in a transparent manner. AAP members and supporters gathered in large numbers and staged a counter-protest accusing the MGNREGA Rozgar Prapat Mazdoor Union and CPI members of pressurizing the government to its supporters.

On 28 August 2024, SP members, led by its metropolitan president, staged a dharna (sit-in protest), raising slogans, at the Upperkot police station in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) after the police stopped them from submitting a memorandum of demands to the Chief Minister. The protesters were demanding the provision of a better drinking water system and the repair of potholed roads.

On 28 August 2024, hundreds of physical education teachers (unemployed) staged a protest at the Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly) in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) demanding recruitment for unfilled government jobs/vacancies.
On 28 August 2024, TMC members led by a minister held a protest at Belakoba town (Jalpaiguri district, WB) over the 12 hour shutdown call by BJP.
On 28 August 2024, TMC members led by a minister held a protest at Rajganj city (Jalpaiguri district, WB) over the 12 hour shutdown call by BJP.
On 28 August 2024, a large number of people held a protest march at Jammu city (J&K) against the police over the sexual assault of a girl in Kishtwar and demanded speedy action by the police.

On 28 August 2024, members of the Shimla Nagrik Sabha (residents committee) staged a protest at the Deputy Commissioner's office in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) demanding a stop to the installation of prepaid smart meters, and privatization of the state electricity board, and called for a repeal of the Electricity (Amendment) Bill 2022.

On 28 August 2024, residents of Sector B (Pocket 1) staged a protest at the Vasant Kunj locality in Delhi - Vasant Vihar city (New Delhi, Delhi) against an upcoming housing project in the area - claiming that it goes against the Delhi Development Authority's regulations.

On 28 August 2024, BJP claimed that around 50-60 assailants owing allegiance to TMC fired and lobbed 7-8 bombs at two BJP members during a protest as part of 12-hour shutdown call at Bhatpara town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) over the police action against the demonstrators in Nabanna area in Howrah city (coded separately). One BJP member received a gunshot injury. Police however claimed that two men were assaulted and that there was no gunshot injury.

On 28 August 2024, members of the AAP Farmer's Wing, led by an AAP MLA (farmer's wing in-charge) staged a protest march, raising slogans, towards the BJP office in Chandigarh city (Punjab) against a BJP MP whom the protesters accused of making negative remarks against farmers, and demanded the termination of her MP membership. The police briefly detained the protesters.

On 28 August 2024, BJP members held protests and blocked railway tracks as part of 12-hour shutdown call at Kharagpur town (Paschim Medinipur district, WB) over the police action against the demonstrators in Nabanna area in Howrah city (coded separately). Police detained the protestors.

On 28 August 2024, BJP members held protests and blocked roads as part of 12-hour shutdown call at Kaliaganj city (Uttar Dinajpur district, WB) over the police action against the demonstrators in Nabanna area in Howrah city (coded separately). Police dispersed the protestors.

On 28 August 2024, TMC members engaged in a scuffle (likely violent based on similar trend at other locations) with BJP members holding a protest as part of 12-hour shutdown call at Kolkata city (WB) over the police action against the demonstrators in Nabanna area in Howrah city (coded separately).

On 14 September 2024, passengers staged a protest at the Indira Gandhi International Airport in the Delhi - Delhi Cantonment area (New Delhi, Delhi) against Spice Jet Airlines over the cancellation of the Delhi-Darbhanga flight.

On 14 September 2024, some people assaulted sanitation workers (likely including members of the Valmiki community based on the use of casteist slurs and the name of the person who registered a case against the assailants) with sticks and were suspected of using casteist slurs near Bataulal Mandir (temple) in Kalpi city (Jalaun, Uttar Pradesh) when the sanitation workers objected to the assailants' misbehaviour. The sanitation workers were seriously injured.

Around 14 September 2024 (as reported), dozens of people including family members of the assault victims (likely including members of the Valmiki community based on the use of casteist slurs and the name of the person who registered a case against the assailants) staged a protest at the police station in Kalpi city (Jalaun, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused involved in the assault on sanitation workers. The police arrested one of the accused.

On 14 September 2024, 76 people (volunteers from Ladakh), led by a climate activist, on 'Day 14' of their protest march (on foot/ongoing) reached the Lahul and Spiti district (coded as Keylong town, Himachal Pradesh) as a part of their 'Delhi Chalo Yatra' to demand statehood, extension of the constitution's sixth schedule, early recruitment process along with a public service commission for Ladakh, and separate Lok Sabha seats for Leh and Kargil districts. An INC MLA and local people joined and the protesters. The protest march has been called by LAB and KDA. The protesters are scheduled to reach New Delhi on 2 October.

On 14 September 2024, local people staged a protest, raising slogans and black flags, in Chhatar village (Jind, Haryana) against the JJP president (MLA) during his campaign visit for the assembly elections and over joining BJP after wining the election.

On 14 September 2024, a large number of people (likely from the Hindu community since the issue was over the suspected slaughter of a protected animal (cow)) near Nagla Birkhu village (Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh) after the remains of an animal were found in the area - which the protesters claimed belonged to a protected (cow) animal.

On 14 September 2024, members of various Kashmiri Pandit organizations including Kashmiri Samiti Delhi (KSD), Panun Kashmir (PK), Roots in Kashmir (RiK), Youth for Panun Kashmir (Y4PK), and Kashmiri Pandit Conference (KPC) staged a massive protest, on the occasion of 'Kashmiri Pandit Balidan Diwas Commemoration (Martyrs Day)', at Jantar Mantar in the Delhi - Connaught Place area (New Delhi, Delhi) demanding the enactment of the 'Genocide Bill' and the formal recognition of the atrocities committed against Kashmiri Pandits (Hindus) in Kashmir in 1989.

On 14 September 2024, some local people, led by the former village head, assaulted a woman and her husband - after tying them to a tree - in Parsa Jungle village (Deoria, Uttar Pradesh) over suspicions of stealing. The assailants also branded the woman's body with a hot iron. The woman was also assaulted the previous day over the same issue (coded separately). A video of the incident was circulated online. The police arrested 5 accused.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Special Task Force
text: On 14 September 2024, some people assaulted a police team (Special Task Force), armed with sharp-edged weapons, and held them hostage in Barara town (Ambala, Haryana) when the police team arrived in the area to interrogate a suspect in the supply of illegal arms.

On 14 September 2024, members of the BJP staged a protest in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against an INC MP and the Leader of the Opposition's comments about reservation for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes while he was in the US.

On 14 September 2024, members of the KRV staged protests across Karnataka state (coded to Bengaluru) demanding the BJP-led Union government to notify all 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule as languages of administration. The protesters also condemned the imposition of Hindi in government offices.
On 14 September 2024, members of the INC staged protests in Calangute town (North Goa, Goa) to mark the second anniversary of the defection of eight INC MLAs to the BJP.

On 14 September 2024, members of the INC including an MLA staged a protest in Coimbatore city (Tamil Nadu) against the Union Finance Minister for forcing an entrepreneur to apologise for raising concerns regarding the imposition of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) on food served in hotels. The protesters wore garlands made of cream buns to mark their protest.

On 14 September 2024, residents of Ramani Mayuri Layout staged a road roko (block) protest on the Saravanampatti-Thudiyalur road in the Saravanampatti locality in Coimbatore city (Tamil Nadu) against the Tamil Nadu Water Supply And Drainage Board and city corporation authorities for the delay in supplying water to their area.

On 14 September 2024, members of people's organisations staged a protest at the bus stand area in Kothagudem town (Bhadradri Kothagudem, Telangana) after the police detained members of the Civil Liberties Committee (CLC) who were on their way to conduct an investigation into a police encounter with members of the CPI (Maoist) cadres that had taken place near Mothe village (coded separately). The protesters raised slogans against the INC-led state government to mark their protest and condemned the detention.

On 14 September 2024, local residents and family members of a woman and newborn who died soon after giving birth due to complications staged a protest with the body of the deceased woman outside a private hospital in Kozhikode city (Kerala) accusing the hospital of medical negligence. The protesters demanded action against the doctors.

On 14 September 2024, members of the Tamil Nadu Sugarcane Producers Association staged a protest near the Arignar Anna Cooperative Sugar Mill in Kurungulam village (Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu) against the allegations of corruption in the mill administration.

On 14 September 2024, members of the VCK including an MP staged a sit-in protest in the K.Pudur locality in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) against the police for removing a party flagpole that the VCK functionaries had erected in the locality.

On 14 September 2024, members of the INC along with an MLA staged protests in Margao city (South Goa, Goa) to mark the second anniversary of the defection of eight INC MLAs to the BJP. The protesters burned effigies of the eight MLAs to mark their protest.

On 14 September 2024, members of Dalit organisations along with a former INC MLA and a former Mayor staged a protest by forming a human chain at the Ballal circle in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding action against a BJP MLA for using a casteist slur while demanding a bribe from a Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) garbage contractor. The protesters demanded the police to take action against the BJP MLA.
On 14 September 2024, members of the INC staged protests in the Old Goa city (North Goa, Goa) to mark the second anniversary of the defection of eight INC MLAs to the BJP.

On 14 September 2024, school midday meal workers affiliated to the cooking workers association, along with rights activists staged a 'satyagraha' (holding on to the truth) protest in front of the Fort gate in Palakkad city (Kerala) against the LDF-led state government for not giving them a bonus for Onam (Kerala's harvest festival). The protesters also demanded the government to release wage arrears and increase their wages.

On 14 September 2024, fishers who had been arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy on charges of poaching along with their families staged a protest near the near the Madurai-Rameswaram national highway in Thangachimadam village (Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu) accusing the Sri Lankan authorities of violating their rights after the Sri Lanka authorities tonsured the heads of six fishers after they were late to pay the fines imposed by the Sri Lankan court. The protesters demanded the BJP-led Union government and the DMK-led state government to take action against Sri Lanka.

On 14 September 2024, members of the Visakha Ukku Parirakshana Porata Committee (VUPPC) (Visakha Steel Conservation Struggle Committee) along with a TDP MLA and an MP staged a protest for the 1,311th day in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the NDA-led Union and state government's proposal to shutdown the RINL-Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (RINL-VSP).

On 14 September 2024, junior doctors held a sit-in protest at the operation theater of Maharaja Yeshwantrao Hospital in Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) a day after a fellow doctor went missing after a Lady Professor accused him of misbehaviour. They demanded a detailed probe into the matter.
On 14 September 2024, IYC members coloured potholes on roads with yellow, held a rally and shouted slogans, in Ajmer city (Rajasthan) during a protest against poor road conditions.

On 14 September 2024, a large number of people (likely Meitei based on geography) demonstrated and placed a stillborn baby at the gate of Singjamei police station of Kakwa locality in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) after a pregnant woman, exposed to tear gas from her residence during violent demonstrations on September 10 (coded separately), was hospitalized amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Police forces and RAF fired tear gas and mock bombs at demonstrators to control the mob.

On 14 September 2024, Wangoo Ahallup Laipham Apunba Lup (WALAL) organized a torch rally protest attended by Meira Paibi activists from different parts of Wangoo from Wangoo Lupa Marup Keithel to Wangoo Mamang Sabal in Wangoo town (Kakching, Manipur) demanding a resolution to the conflict amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

Around 14 September 2024 (as reported), relatives of a deceased patient physically assaulted a doctor at Karimganj Civil Hospital in Karimganj town (Karimganj, Assam) blaming him for the death of the patient 2 months ago and demanded a compensation of 5 lakhs.

On 14 September 2024, students of Pramodenagar Higher Secondary School staged a road block protest and locked the gates of their school in Promodenagar village (Sepahijala, Tripura) against the transfer of their teacher.

Around 14 September 2024 (as reported), hundreds of students, and NSUI members, held a demonstration and clashed with police at the residence of the Vice-Chancellor of Jiwaji University in Jabalpur city (Madhya Pradesh) over the university's paper-checking procedure after 150 Students were given 'Zero' in B.Com results.

On 14 September 2024, residents assaulted a man in Kohani Deori village (Dindori, Madhya Pradesh) after he was caught assaulting a minor girl.

On 14 September 2024, a group of locals staged a protest with anti-INC slogans and prevented a delegation of 15 INC members from entering Kochutoli village near Sonapur town (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) following an eviction drive that resulted in the death of 2 Bengali Muslim villagers (coded separately).

On 14 September 2024, unidentified persons threw stones during Bewan Yatra, a Hindu religious procession, in the Jahazpur town (Bhilwara, Rajasthan). This incident led to demonstration (coded separately).

On 14 September 2024, All BTC Minority Students' Union (ABMSU) organized a protest in all sub-divisions of Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR) including Bhergaon town (Udalguri, Assam) against the killing of 2 Bengali-Muslims during an eviction drive at Kachutali (coded separately) and the BJP government.

On 15 September 2024, several locals and BJP members held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) against a police station in-charge who was arrested over the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case, over claimed mishandling of the case by the local police and to demand justice for the victim.

On 15 September 2024, hundreds of locals and doctors under the banner of the IMA held a protest march at Jalpaiguri city (WB) over the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case and to demand justice for the victim.

On 15 September 2024, thousands of professionals, locals and junior doctors held a protest march towards the 'Swastha Bhavan' (health department) amidst an ongoing sit-in protest from Kolkata to Bidhannagar (coded as Bidhannagar city, North 24 Parganas district, WB) over the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case, to demand justice for the victim and resignation of Kolkata police commissioner, the state health secretary, director of health education, and director of health services.
On 15 September 2024, hundreds of former students of a girls high school held a protest march at Kolkata city (WB) over the Kolkata doctor rape-murder case and to demand justice for the victim.

On 15 September 2024, INC members held a demonstration by blocking a road burning tyres at a highway in Manikchak tehsil (Maldah district, WB) against the killing of their leader in Dharampur village on the same day (coded separately) and to demand the arrest of the perpetrators.
On 15 September 2024, family members of a deceased held a protest at Pulwama town (J&K) over claimed medical negligence leading to the death of a patient.
